By living the Amtrak values, focusing on our capabilities, and actively embracing and fostering diverse ideas, backgrounds, and perspectives, together we will honor our past and make Amtrak a company of the future.

Job Summary

The Sr. Director Architecture - Train Operations is responsible for providing visionary senior architecture leadership to ensure technology investments are in alignment with corporate goals and its ability to move towards the future in an evolving business environment. As a Digital Technology senior leader, this role will utilize communication, guidance, and governance processes to maximize return on technology investment, and reduce time to capability, while minimizing operational costs. The Sr. Director Architecture will use visionary strategic thinking to choose technology capabilities, strategize and build around them to solve corporate problems.

As part of the DT management team the senior director will be responsible for communicating train operations technology target state, roadmap and change progress to senior leadership and other stakeholders. They will also use their communication and influence skills to promote awareness and understanding of architecture principles across the organization, evangelizing for strategic enterprise change, executing strategy, technical senior leadership.

As a senior people leader they will provide direction and development of leaders and teams to move architecture and business objectives forward.

Essential Functions

  • Set up and provide senior leadership steering for the architectural vision for core enterprise capabilities and aligning patterns to allow for consistency and reuse
  • Govern and direct enterprise principles, patterns and guidance that help in technology infrastructure, how applications are built, deployed, and maintained to align with strategic needs and maximizing technology investments
  • Provide Oversight and Governance to the current, interim and potential future state of key architecture domains value aligned with the organization's overall goals and objectives.
  • Ensure the reference architectures, standards, and guidelines of the organization's technology is safe, secure, stable and compliant with industry standards.
  • Direct enterprise-wide, transformational leadership to drive adoption and re-use of the preferred resources, processes and technology across the company.
  • Champion organizational design, enterprise strategy, innovation leadership for the architecture practice
  • Lead and mentor a team of architects, providing guidance and fostering a culture of excellence.
  • Create and provide senior leadership steering of strategic roadmaps and comprehensive plans that outline how the Digital Technology architecture will evolve to support the business strategy over time and ensure DT initiatives are prioritized based on their expected business value and strategic importance.
  • Guide Investment Decisions Aligning technology plans and investments to business vision and strategy that is necessary to ensure we are building the right things.
  • Provide senior leadership steering in the design, governance, and oversight for implementing robust, scalable, and efficient architectural solutions for domain business problems.
  • Guide and govern the translation of complex technical ideas into digestible concepts for both technical teams and non-technical stakeholders. Act as a leadership liaison for architecture best practices between digital technology and business teams to ensure alignment and understanding.

Minimum Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in computer science, data and intelligence or related field with 15+ year’s relevant architecture experience or equivalent work experience.
  • Experience creating significant business value realization with $1B+ or more enterprises as an architect providing vision and choosing platforms moving organizations forward and scaled for expanding future initiatives.
  • 11+ years of relevant technical and business managerial experience with 2 to 3 years leading an Architecture Practice area.
  • Requires leadership experience in managing architecture teams and influencing executive level management and key stakeholders.
  • Requires demonstrated ability to manage multiple architecture engagement and effectively plan and use staff to ensure the architecture view.
  • Previous experience shaping enterprise architecture vision and leading an org-wide transformation and culture shift to that vision
  • Must possess strong communication and interpersonal skills, work well with others in an integrated team environment, and must be self-motivated.
  • Must possess a mastery of business acumen
  • Relationship building and collaboration skills across diverse and matrixed stakeholders and customers. 
  • Ability to surface, prioritize, and balance priorities across multiple stakeholders.
  • Excellent problem-solving and analytical skills, including experience leveraging data to inform decision-making.
  • Passenger Rail Operations Architecture: Fellow-level expertise defining target-state architectures and capability roadmaps for large-scale, mission-critical day-of-train operations across passenger rail networks.
  • Crew, Yard, and Consist Management: Deep domain knowledge designing integrated capabilities for crew planning and assignment, yard operations, equipment and consist management, and operational readiness.
  • Unified Train Tracking and Predictive Intelligence: Experience architecting real-time train tracking and status platforms that combine operational data to deliver predictive ETA/ETD, disruption awareness, and actionable decision support.
  • Schedule Management and Service Recovery: Expertise in operational schedule management, real-time re-planning, conflict resolution, and service recovery across complex passenger rail environments.
  • Optimization, Simulation, and Decision Science: Proven ability to apply optimization, simulation, digital-twin, and advanced analytics capabilities to crew, yard, consist, schedule, and network operating decisions.
  • Train Movement and Dispatch: Strong architecture experience with train movement, dispatching, traffic management, route and resource conflict management, and safety-critical operational integrations.
  • Rail Ecosystem Integration: Experience establishing secure, resilient, standards-based data exchange and partner communications with host railroads, state sponsors, commuter agencies, and other operating partners.
  • Resilient Real-Time Platforms: Demonstrated expertise architecting highly available, scalable, observable, and cybersecure event-driven platforms spanning IT/OT systems, edge environments, control centers, and cloud services.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Master’s degree in business or related field
  • Travel and Transportation experience or relevant technology domain experience
  • Experience with governance, risk, regulatory and compliance.
  • The Architect’s skills and knowledge should span multiple architecture domains (e.g., Business Architecture, Application/Solution Architecture, Technical/Infrastructure Architecture & Information/Data Architecture)

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities

  • 15+ years’ experience in relevant industry experience
  • 11+ years in managing talent.
  • Experience managing teams.

  • Knowledge of IT, OT, domain and business architecture

jobs.title: Release Strategist, Professional Services
jobs.excerpt: About the Job: Most companies don’t have a “release problem” so much as a way-of-working problem.
jobs.description:
About the Job:

Most companies don’t have a “release problem” so much as a way-of-working problem. Shipping live functionality to their customers takes too long, depends on a few heroes, or happens with fingers crossed, and AI-assisted development is raising the stakes. LaunchDarkly Professional Services is helping our most strategic customers change that, and we’re hiring a Release Strategist to lead those engagements.

As a Release Strategist on LaunchDarkly's Professional Services team, you are the “product manager” for each customer engagement, responsible for defining how that customer achieves release excellence by evolving their software and agentic release processes. You join the sales cycle early to define the problem and quantify what it’s costing them, then own the engagement through delivery and adoption until the change sticks. You own the “why” and the “what”; our Solutions Architects, who serve as our Forward Deployed Engineers (FDEs), own the “how.”

Day to day, you’ll partner with a Solutions Architect on each engagement, combining their technical judgment with your view of the commercial context, customer priorities, and relationship dynamics. Neither of you can do the job alone. You own the problem, the value, the scope, and the success criteria; your Solutions Architect owns the technical approach and its quality. You’ll also work closely with Account Executives and Customer Success Managers, and you’ll lead without direct authority, so influence, clarity, and trust matter more than title.

This is a new role, and its shape will flex and adapt as the business grows. Early on, expect to lean into scoping, delivery, and change leadership on both the pre-sales and post-sales side of the business. As we establish a feedback loop through customer delivery, you’ll extend that product mindset from individual engagements to our offerings themselves, and help write the playbook for how we package engagements, measure success, and bring on the next Release Strategist.

Responsibilities:

  • Product & Value
    • Scope the problem and the value if solved: join sales cycles from early discovery, map the customer’s organization and decision landscape, and quantify the business value of their release and delivery problem.
    • Define the customer engagement like a product: identify the business challenges and, with your Solutions Architect, the technical ones behind them; set the MVP or first phase, success criteria, and timeline; write the engagement plan (the outcomes, deliverables, and acceptance criteria the team delivers against); and shape the SOW with PS leadership so what we sell is what we can deliver.
    • Own scope and prioritization: decide what we do first and what we defer, manage scope as the engagement evolves, and continuously assess whether it still serves both the customer’s outcomes and LaunchDarkly’s interests, reshaping the plan when they diverge.
    • Own the outcome from go-live, the point where the customer starts working the new way, through adoption: capture feedback, iterate, and prove the business value defined at the start.
  • Change & Adoption
    • Facilitate discovery and design sessions mapping release processes and visualizing “who should get a feature and when” without the technology or process on how to accomplish it. Adapt or invent new collaborative practices when a customer’s situation doesn’t fit one we already use, to turn ambiguous goals into clear, owned success plans.
    • Lead and grow our change management practices: align customer teams on new ways of working, address resistance, and drive adoption so changes stick after the engagement ends. Scope the ongoing support plan and create the documentation and enablement the customer needs to sustain it.
  • Executive & Growth
    • Act as a trusted advisor to VP and C-level stakeholders: set expectations, present progress, risks, recommend data-driven decisions, and drive decisions quickly.
    • Monitor account health and surface expansion or renewal signals; scope the next engagement as a natural outcome of delivered value.
  • Offerings & Playbook (grows as our FDE engagement volume does)
    • Turn what you learn across engagements into a feedback loop for our offerings: capture patterns, help shape how we package engagements and measure success, and help write the playbook, including how we bring on future hires.
  • Delivery & Execution
    • Run the delivery rhythm: status calls and reporting, accountability to tasks and deadlines across the engagement team, and escalation of technical or political blockers.
    • Keep a running view of budget/burn against SOW and flag over/under-projection early; partner with PM-type support (where it exists on an account) for detailed tracking and change-order mechanics.
  • Customer Landscape
    • Our customers struggle with long lead times, risky deployments, feature flag sprawl, unclear ownership of releases, and a gap between what engineering ships and what the business expects. You’ll need to speak confidently about CI/CD, progressive delivery, testing and quality gates, how agent-generated changes affect release risk, and delivery metrics such as deployment frequency, lead time, and change-failure rate. You don’t need to write the code. You do need to know when a customer is describing a real constraint and when they’re describing a habit.

Qualifications:

  • Core
    • 8+ years of relevant experience, ideally in senior, client-facing roles across product management, delivery, or consulting within B2B SaaS or technology services; or as a forward-deployed/deployment strategist, or early builder/founder at a high-growth tech startup.
    • Product and systems thinking: you can define what to deliver and why (MVP or first-phase scoping, prioritization, and success criteria) and manage scope against it.
    • Value-based scoping experience (ROI/TCO) with executive buyers, ideally within sales cycles.
    • A track record owning both delivery accountability and the executive relationship on the same engagement, with the judgment to decide whether an engagement’s scope still serves the business, not just execute against an agreed plan. Executive-level communication and presence.
    • You’ve helped an organization move off an entrenched process and adopt a new way of working, not just documented a better one, including facilitating workshops with mixed engineering and leadership groups and adapting formats on the fly.
    • Regular, practical use of AI tools in your work, with good judgment about their limits.
    • Enough confidence in SDLC and software delivery to be credible with technical stakeholders, and experience partnering closely with technical roles (solutions engineers, architects, or similar).
  • Preferred Qualifications
    • Familiarity with progressive delivery and feature management, ideally including LaunchDarkly or a similar tool. Fluency with delivery metrics such as deployment frequency, lead time, and change-failure rate. We’ll teach you the LaunchDarkly specifics.
    • Demonstrated fluency with AI tooling to analyze data, generate insights, and build visualizations and narratives, with sound judgment about accuracy and appropriate use.
    • Experience writing PRDs and managing agile software projects.
    • Experience surfacing expansion/renewal signals to Sales or AM; comfort with a role that may take on commercial ownership over time.
    • (Bonus) Experience operating in a scaling PS org where role boundaries are still being defined.

Travel

  • Travel roughly once per quarter for customer workshops and team onsites; more frequent travel may be needed around specific engagements.

Pay:

Target pay ranges based on Geographic Zones* for Level P4:

  • Zone 1: San Francisco/Bay Area or NYC Metropolitan Area, Boston, Seattle - $171,200- $235,400**
  • Zone 2: Irvine, LA, Monterey, Santa Barbara, Santa Rosa, Austin, Portland, Philadelphia, Chicago - $154,100 - $211,860**
  • Zone 3: All other US locations - $145,500 - $200,090**

LaunchDarkly operates from a place of high trust and transparency; we are happy to state the pay range for our open roles to best align with your needs. Exact compensation may vary based on skills, experience, and location.

*Within the United States, our geographic pay zones are defined by counties surrounding major metropolitan areas.
**Restricted Stock Units (RSUs), health, vision, and dental insurance, and mental health benefits in addition to salary.

About LaunchDarkly:

Modern software delivery was supposed to be the foundation for a thriving digital business but reality has proven otherwise. Slow, inefficient development cycles, costly outages, and fragmented customer experiences are preventing developers from building their best software. The LaunchDarkly platform helps developers innovate on new features faster while protecting them with a safety valve to instantly rewind when things go wrong. Developers can target product experiences to any customer segment and maximize the business impact of every feature. And by gradually rolling out new application components, they escape nightmare "big-bang" technology migrations.

The LaunchDarkly platform was built to guide engineers to the next frontier of DevOps by:

  • Improving the velocity and stability of software releases, without the fear of end customer outages
  • Delivering targeted experiences by easily personalizing features to customer cohorts
  • Maximizing the business impact of every feature through the ability to experiment and optimize
  • Coordinating the release and optimization of software to provide consistent experiences across mobile platforms and device types
  • Improving the effectiveness and productivity of engineering teams, by providing insights into engineering cadence and stability

These fellows will receive in kind support to explore their research questions using the full datasets B Lab has available, subject to necessary data protection steps and measures (see more on this below).

How to apply

Number of fellowship openings

About B LabB Lab™ is the nonprofit behind Certified B Corporations™, a community of businesses that meet verified social, environmental, and governance standards. Together, our movement is working towards a more inclusive, equitable, and fair economic system.

Our history B Lab began in 2006 with the idea that a different kind of economy was not only possible — it was necessary. Our founders Andrew Kassoy, Bart Houlahan, and Jay Coen Gilbert believed there was a better way to do business: better for workers, better for communities, and better for the planet. When our movement’s first 81 Founding B Corps signed the Declaration of Interdependence in 2007, they were not just proposing a better way of doing business. They were proposing a different definition altogether.

What we’ve achieved B Lab became known for certifying B Corporations™, companies that meet verified standards of social and environmental performance, accountability, and transparency. But we do much more than that. We help mobilize a global community of businesses committed to collective action on society’s most critical challenges. In 2010, B Lab was part of successfully drafting and passing benefit corporation in Maryland, the first U.S. state to do so. This created a legal framework that allows companies to keep their values of care and community, not just shareholder value, at the forefront. Today, benefit corporation legislation is active in 52 jurisdictions around the world.

Our futureIn 2024, leaders from across the network agreed to evolve into a more integrated organization that embodies interdependence. This next iteration of our global network will balance global coherence with local agency to achieve our vision of economic systems change. We are now building this future together.

Job Summary

We're looking for a Program Manager to drive day-to-day execution of large-scale data center programs across the QC Ecosystem. This is the role that keeps everything moving — coordinating across ecosystem entities, partners, vendors, and stakeholders to ensure commitments are executed, milestones are achieved, and issues are resolved before they impact delivery.

This role sits at the intersection of program planning, execution, and coordination. In addition to overseeing active program delivery, the Program Manager helps coordinate new opportunities as they move from proposal and planning through mobilization and kickoff, ensuring key stakeholders are engaged, execution plans are aligned, and critical milestones remain on track.

Program Execution & Delivery

  • Drive day-to-day execution against master program schedules and phase-gate milestones.

jobs.excerpt: 🚀 We’re on a mission to make money work for everyone.
jobs.description:
🚀 We’re on a mission to make money work for everyone.

We’re waving goodbye to the complicated and confusing ways of traditional banking.

After starting as a prepaid card, our product offering has grown a lot in the last 10 years in the UK. As well as personal and business bank accounts, we offer joint accounts, accounts for 16-17 year olds, a free kids account and credit cards in the UK, with more exciting things to come beyond. Our UK customers can also save, invest and combine their pensions with us.

With our hot coral cards and get-paid-early feature, combined with financial education on social media and our award winning customer service, we have a long history of creating magical moments for our customers!

We’re not only about selling products - we want to solve problems and change lives through Monzo.

📍London/Cardiff/UK Remote | 💰£85,000 - £115,000 + Incentive Awards tied to your performance + Benefits ✨

⭐️ Our Third Party & Outsourcing Risk Management Team

We are a high-performing Global team focused on delivering pragmatic Third Party Risk Management (‘TPRM’) that protects Monzo and our customers globally. As Monzo expands across new markets and scales its product range, the operational footprint is growing fast, and the operating environment is becoming more complex.

We’re looking for a Senior Third Party Risk Manager to help shape and deliver our approach. As well as ensuring Monzo’s TPRM has well defined controls, processes and governance models in place to meet the continually growing and evolving demands of global Third Party Risk Management regulations - you’ll also set priorities and turn them into measurable improvements.

Reporting to the Director of Third Party Risk, this is a hands-on role, with strategic scope. You’ll work across the global team, and with a variety of stakeholders throughout Monzo, to strengthen our framework, manage complex risks and improve how we deliver TPRM both tactically and strategically.

🔑 You’ll play a key role by...

  • Delivering Core TPRM Operations Globally: Operating end-to-end operational activities, including supplier tiering, materiality assessments, due diligence reviews, exit planning support, and regulatory reporting.
  • Driving Operational Excellence: Taking ownership of process quality, making sure TPRM activities are completed accurately, consistently and on time. You’ll look for ways to improve how we manage third party risk in practice.
  • Helping shape our priorities: Identifying emerging risks, gaps and opportunities across third party risk management, and making recommendations to inform the team’s strategy and roadmap. You’ll develop practical solutions and help deliver improvements through to completion.
  • Enabling Strategic Delivery: Supporting and feeding into higher-level strategic initiatives and complex risk landscapes. Leading agreed initiatives from problem definition through implementation autonomously, working across teams and global markets to deliver measurable improvements and ensuring clear visibility throughout.
  • Collaborating Across Teams: Working directly with internal stakeholders across the 3LOD, and external suppliers to clear blockers, follow up on actions, and resolve issues effectively.
  • Sharing your expertise: Support colleagues and stakeholders with practical guidance, helping them understand how to deliver their third party risk responsibilities.

🤩 We’d love to hear from you if…

  • You know Outsourcing, Third Party Risk & Regulation: You have substantial practical TPRM experience (ideally in banking or financial services) operating in both the UK and EU financial markets.
  • You’ve contributed to a risk strategy, framework or operating model: You can demonstrate how you translated an identified gap into a practical improvement.
  • You’re comfortable leading complex assessments: You make balanced, well-reasoned recommendations when information is incomplete or stakeholders have different priorities.
  • You have experience working with various technologies: TPR tooling and AI to build innovative solutions and streamline operational workflows.
  • You hold a high quality bar: You pay close attention to detail and care about accuracy. You use data and reporting to spot patterns, make evidence-based decisions and improve processes.
  • You take ownership: You work independently, take initiative and prioritise your workload in a fast-moving environment. You use sound risk judgement and know when to seek guidance or involve others.
  • You focus on outcomes, not just activity: You measure success by what has materially improved whether that's faster turnaround times, clearer risk ownership, or cleaner supplier data.
  • You are a clear, pragmatic communicator: You build strong relationships with internal teams, third parties and regulators. You’re comfortable holding colleagues accountable and offering constructive challenges when needed. You bring together input from specialists across Information Security, Data Protection, Legal and Operational Resilience to form a clear view of risk.
  • You are comfortable escalating: You use sound judgement to know when to involve your team or manager in emerging issues or concerns, and communicate your priorities and workload clearly and regularly, defaulting to transparency and taking accountability.

🙌 What’s in it for you

💰 £85,000 - £115,000 ➕Incentive Awards tied to your performance.

➕ Plus lots more! Read our full list of benefits.

The Data Modeler will support the design, development, and maintenance of logical and physical data models that enable analytics, reporting, and operational data use cases. This role works with business and technical stakeholders to translate requirements into structured data solutions while applying established enterprise data modeling standards and practices. The Data Modeler contributes to data quality, consistency, and usability across systems while developing expertise in enterprise data modeling, data warehousing, data integration, and database technologies.

What you will do:

  • Design and maintain logical and physical data models for operational, analytics, and reporting use cases, including dimensional, normalized, and relational models under guidance from senior team members.
  • Translate business and technical requirements into structured data definitions, entities, relationships, and model components.
  • Apply enterprise naming conventions, data standards, and modeling practices consistently across deliverables, and maintain model documentation, metadata, versioning, and change tracking.
  • Create and maintain modeling artifacts, including entity relationship diagrams (ERDs), data mappings, model definitions, and supporting documentation.
  • Perform data profiling, validation, and quality reviews to support model accuracy, consistency, and usability, and assist in troubleshooting data structure, lineage, mapping, and integration issues.
  • Support data warehouse development and data integration initiatives across multiple systems while collaborating with data engineers, analysts, architects, and business stakeholders to clarify data requirements.

What you will bring:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Information Systems, Computer Science, Business, or a related field, with 2 to 4 years of experience in data modeling, database design, analytics engineering, or a related data discipline.
  • Working knowledge of logical and physical data modeling concepts, dimensional modeling, and relational database design principles.
  • Experience using SQL for querying, validation, and data analysis, along with experience using data modeling tools such as ER/Studio, ERwin, or similar platforms and familiarity with cloud database or warehouse technologies such as PostgreSQL, Redshift, Athena, Snowflake, or similar platforms.

• Performs review and analysis of centralized, aggregated data to identify potential signals and trends in predefined risk indicators.

  • Conducts periodic review of site-level Key Risk Indicators (KRIs).
  • Monitors site performance and identifies potential issues requiring further review or corrective action.
  • Reviews the effectiveness of implemented actions and escalates concerns when additional action may be required.
  • Evaluates the quality and integrity of study site practices related to protocol compliance and applicable regulations based on centralized monitoring outputs.
  • Maintains effective project-level communication with relevant stakeholders regarding centralized monitoring findings and follow-up activities.
  • Maintains relevant project documentation and contributes to the development and maintenance of centralized monitoring documentation, as applicable.
  • Attends study kick-off meetings, recurring project meetings and other relevant meetings according to project needs.
  • Maintains knowledge of applicable company SOPs, processes and centralized monitoring requirements
  • Education - BA/BS degree in a Life Science field, or equivalent education and experience in line with country-specific requirements
  • Minimum of 1 year of experience in clinical research or a related field
  • Understanding of Risk Based Quality Management and centralized monitoring principles.
  • Working knowledge of applicable clinical research regulations, ICH-GCP principles
  • Ability to review and interpret clinical study data, trends and risk indicators.
  • Good analytical and problem-solving skills.
  • Good written and verbal communication skills.
  • Ability to work effectively within cross-functional study teams.
  • Good organizational skills and ability to manage activities across assigned studies

When you join Ergomed Group, you make a difference by helping to bring safe and effective pharmaceutical treatment to patients around the world. You’ll join a passionate and collaborative team of experts in clinical research, pharmacovigilance, and quality consulting.

We are diverse in many ways, yet our values unite us. Our values are how we work, not words on a wall. If they sound like you, you will feel at home here.

  • Quality: we hold ourselves to the standard patients deserve.
  • Integrity and trust: we do the right thing, especially when it is hard.
  • Drive and passion: we care about the outcome, because someone is waiting on it.
  • Agility and responsiveness: we move quickly, because patients cannot wait.
  • Belonging: everyone is welcome, and every voice counts.
  • Collaborative partnerships: we go further by going together.

We look forward to welcoming your application.

Medicine moves forward here. So will you.

Ergomed is a specialist clinical research organization focused on rare disease and select oncology indications. We focus on the most complex trials, the studies where experience, judgement, and rigorous operational accountability make the biggest difference. We partner with small to midsize biotech companies to move promising therapies through early phase development, so they reach the patients sooner.

We choose complex work on purpose. Rare disease and oncology trials carry real operational risk, and our people are experts at reducing it, protecting timelines, data quality and the experience of sites and patients at the same time. It is demanding, meaningful work, and no one here forgets that patients cannot wait.

That is why culture matters to us as much as capability. We have built a collaborative, international team where people share ideas, grow their careers and are trusted to take ownership early. With colleagues across North America, South America, Europe, Asia and Australia, we value teamwork, flexibility and a real commitment to work-life balance, because good science comes from people who feel supported.

If you want work with purpose, the agility to make an impact and a team that cares about the people behind the work as much as the work itself, we would love to hear from you.

jobs.title: Engineering Manager - Grafana Infrastructure (Remote, Canada)
jobs.excerpt: Grafana Labs is the company behind Grafana Cloud, the fully managed observability platform trusted by more than 10,000 organizations to ensure reliability, resolve incidents faster, and optimize telemetry at scale.
jobs.description:
Grafana Labs is the company behind Grafana Cloud, the fully managed observability platform trusted by more than 10,000 organizations to ensure reliability, resolve incidents faster, and optimize telemetry at scale. Built on open source and open standards and designed for interoperability across any stack, Grafana Cloud brings AI to observability and observability to AI, giving teams (and their agents) unified visibility so they can see, understand, and act on all their disparate data, wherever it lives, and move at the speed of their ambitions. Customers, including Anthropic, Bloomberg, NVIDIA, Microsoft, and Salesforce, rely on Grafana Labs. We are a 100% remote company with team members across 40+ countries, backed by leading investors including Lightspeed Venture Partners, Sequoia Capital, GIC, Coatue, J.P. Morgan, CapitalG, and Lead Edge Capital. Learn more at and follow us on LinkedIn and X.

We’re scaling fast and staying true to what makes us different: an open-source legacy, a global collaborative culture, and a passion for meaningful work. Our team thrives in an innovation-driven environment where transparency, autonomy, and trust fuel everything we do.

You may not meet every requirement, and that’s okay. If this role excites you, we’d love you to raise your hand for what could be a truly career-defining opportunity.

This is a remote position and we're considering candidates in the US or Canada (residents of Québec are not eligible for this position).

The Opportunity

About our platform

Grafana Cloud moves millions of metrics, log lines, and traces per second from our customers' environments into a highly available, low-latency stack that processes and stores this data, and serves it to dashboards and alerting tools. We aim to grow this to hundreds of millions per second, and it's critical that as we grow, we improve our performance, increase our reliability, and do it efficiently and securely.

The Foundations department owns the Internal Engineering Platform (IEP): the Kubernetes clusters, cloud service provider resources (CSP), hardware, identity, delivery, and observability systems that Grafana Labs's application engineers use to build, deploy, and run their workloads.

About the Infrastructure group

We're hiring an engineering manager for the Foundations Infrastructure group, which owns the cloud infrastructure Grafana Cloud runs on. The group provisions and operates Kubernetes clusters and CSP resources across GCP, AWS, and Azure; enforces identity, access, and security controls across those environments; and runs the observability and cost-visibility systems that keep the infrastructure measurable and accountable.

You'll lead one of the squads of platform engineers that comprise the group.

We're platform engineers, and our application teams are our users. Our job is to give them leverage: self-service building blocks that take care of the hard parts of infrastructure, so they can focus on what they're building. We treat the platform as a product and value the experience of the people who use it. When a change is well communicated and understood, teams welcome it, and it lands as an improvement that makes the right way the easy way. You'll lead a squad that makes that happen.

How we work

Foundations is a global team that works asynchronously. The people who own a component or problem make the decisions about it, once stakeholders have had a chance to weigh in. Application teams build and run their own services; we give them a self-service platform to do it on.

Every engineer is on-call for the components their squad provides. We plan on-call, tactical work, and time off into every quarter, so roadmap work is roughly half of an engineer's time rather than all of it.

What You'll Be Doing

  • Hire, manage, and develop a squad of platform engineers, with regular feedback and career conversations that support each person's growth.
  • Own your squad's roadmap and quarterly objectives: help decide what the squad works on, what it defers, and why, across a broad remit where demand always exceeds capacity.
  • Take platform changes from design to fleet-wide adoption: staged rollouts, migration paths, and clear communication, so changes land well for the teams who depend on them.
  • Partner with the other Infrastructure squads on work that spans them, and with the teams across Foundations and the rest of Engineering whose work depends on yours.
  • Help shape how the group works as a whole, including planning, on-call, and the ownership model between squads.
  • Own the squad's intake. Requests, reviews, and support from application teams arrive continuously; keep them triaged and visible so that planned work still moves.
  • Keep on-call healthy: ensure a sustainable load and support incident response.
  • Work across team boundaries, contributing beyond your squad's scope where Foundations needs it.

We invest heavily in developer productivity. You can use modern AI coding assistants as part of your daily workflow (your choice of tools, within security guidelines), backed by a company-funded usage budget so you can iterate quickly without unnecessary friction.

We encourage pragmatic AI-assisted development: faster prototyping, test generation, refactors, documentation, and incident follow-ups, always paired with strong code review and quality standards.

What Makes You a Great Fit

  • Experience managing engineers, ideally a team that builds and operates production CSP infrastructure, security, networking and/or storage
  • Hands-on depth in at least one area of platform engineering, such as cloud infrastructure and Kubernetes, infrastructure security and access, or observability. You can challenge a design in your area on its merits, and the engineers on your team will expect you to.
  • Fluency with infrastructure as code and with running Kubernetes in production.
  • A track record of landing internal engineering/developer platform changes at scale. You've driven a migration or a rollout across many teams or many clusters, and you know what makes one stall.
  • The ability to explain platform engineering to very different audiences (platform engineers, application teams, product management and business leadership) and to make the case for what the squad should and shouldn't take on.
  • Be comfortable collaborating across time zones and cultures in a fully remote environment, using clear, written communication to build trust and psychological safety.
  • You're a motivated self-starter with a strong bias toward action and ownership, able to navigate ambiguity in a complex problem space.
  • Comfort with AI-assisted tooling. We embrace AI and agentic development, so we expect you to be curious and comfortable using AI-powered tools, and ideally to have practical experience folding them into a team's workflow.

Bonus Points For

  • Experience across more than one of the group's areas: cloud infrastructure, infrastructure security, and observability
  • Hands-on depth in cloud infrastructure security: cloud IAM, Kubernetes security, secrets, and workload identity on at least one major cloud provider. You can challenge a threat model or an access design on its merits, and the engineers on your team will expect you to.
  • Building self-service infrastructure for application teams
  • Running observability for a production platform at scale
  • Operating across more than one of GCP, AWS, and Azure
  • You've worked in or on open source, or other community-based projects. At Grafana Labs, "OSS is in our DNA"

In Canada, the base compensation range for this role is $192,891 CAD - $231,469 CAD. Actual compensation may vary based on level, experience, and skillset as assessed throughout the interview process. All of our roles include Restricted Stock Units (RSUs), giving every team member ownership in Grafana Labs' success. We believe in shared outcomes—RSUs help us stay aligned and invested as we scale globally.

*Compensation ranges are country specific. If you are applying for this role from a different location than listed above, your recruiter will discuss your specific market’s defined pay range & benefits at the beginning of the process.

Why You’ll Thrive at Grafana Labs:

  • 100% Remote, Global Culture - As a remote-only company, we bring together talent from around the world, united by a culture of collaboration and shared purpose.
  • Scaling Organization – Tackle meaningful work in a high-growth, ever-evolving environment.
  • Transparent Communication – Expect open decision-making and regular company-wide updates.
  • Innovation-Driven – Autonomy and support to ship great work and try new things.
  • Open Source Roots – Built on community-driven values that shape how we work.
  • Empowered Teams – High trust, low ego culture that values outcomes over optics.
  • Career Growth Pathways – Defined opportunities to grow and develop your career.
  • Approachable Leadership – Transparent execs who are involved, visible, and human.
  • Passionate People – Join a team of smart, supportive folks who care deeply about what they do.
  • In-Person onboarding - We want you to thrive from day 1 with your fellow new ‘Grafanistas’ to learn all about what we do and how we do it.

jobs.description:
Job Title: Senior QA Engineer, Runtime

By governing the use of AI across the development lifecycle, Unqork empowers enterprises with a new way to leverage AI to build, run, and evolve complex, mission-critical software without creating unvetted, unsecured code. Unqork helps enterprises, like Goldman Sachs, Marsh, and BlackRock accelerate digital transformation while reducing risk and total cost of ownership across their application portfolio.

At Unqork, we value inclusive and innovative thinkers who boldly challenge the status quo. We encourage you to apply!

The Team:

The Runtime team owns the programming model and engine that runs every application built on Unqork. We keep today's runtime stable, fast, and secure for enterprise customers, and we are actively building the next generation. We ship fast, and we hold the highest bar for quality and security while we do it.

What U’ll Do:

  • Own test automation for the Runtime team. Design, write, and maintain Playwright test suites that cover critical runtime flows and run on every pull request and release. Keep them fast, deterministic, and trusted. A flaky test is a bug to fix, not a test to rerun.
  • Review automation as code. Review the tests engineers write with their features, hold them to the same standard as production code, and coach the team on writing tests that catch real regressions.
  • Gate releases with automation. Wire suites into CI/CD (GitHub Actions) as quality gates, track pass rate, flakiness, and run time, and decide when a release is ready to ship.
  • Test proactively. Join feature refinement early, define testability requirements and acceptance criteria, and have tests ready as features land, not after.
  • Raise the security bar. Build checks for authentication, authorization, input handling, and data exposure into the suite, and partner with Security to turn findings into regression tests.
  • Build and run performance tests. Write k6 load and stress tests for runtime APIs and rendering paths, set baselines, and catch regressions in CI before customers do.
  • Use AI to scale coverage. Use Claude Code, Gemini, and similar tools to generate test scaffolding, triage failures, and grow regression coverage faster. Review their output with the rigor you'd apply to a teammate's code.
  • Modernize legacy coverage. Migrate historical CodeceptJS and Selenium tests to Playwright, and retire tests that no longer earn their run time.
  • Close the loop on escaped bugs. Reproduce and isolate customer-reported issues, file clear bugs with evidence and severity, and turn every escape into an automated test so it can't come back.
  • Explore where automation can't. Do focused exploratory testing in the browser with DevTools, and build complex, nested applications that act like real customer use cases and push the runtime to its limits.

The Impact U will make:

  • Deliver a regression suite the team trusts enough to ship on.
  • Find and close gaps in our test suites using client use cases, past bug patterns, and customer feedback.
  • Raise the quality and security bar while increasing how fast we ship.
  • Become the Runtime team's trusted voice on whether something is ready to ship.

What U bring:

  • 5+ years of experience in Quality Engineering or Software Engineering, with at least 3 focused on test automation.
  • Strong JavaScript/TypeScript experience required. Your test code reads like production code.
  • Deep, hands-on experience building and maintaining E2E suites with Playwright.
  • A track record of building a stable regression suite from scratch, or turning a flaky one around, with the metrics to show it.
  • Experience reviewing other engineers' test code and setting automation standards for a team.
  • A solid grasp of web development: HTML, CSS, the DOM, HTTP and REST APIs, browser DevTools, and how modern front-end apps render and manage state.
  • Working knowledge of web application security testing, such as the OWASP Top 10 and authentication and authorization checks.
  • Experience writing performance or load tests, ideally with k6.
  • Proven fluency with AI coding tools such as Claude Code, Gemini, Copilot, or Cursor, and the judgment to know when their output needs a second look.
  • The ability to work autonomously as the only QA on a fast-moving team: you set priorities, make the call, and communicate risk clearly.
  • The confidence to push back on a release, and the communication skills to explain why.
  • Nice to have: API contract testing, visual regression testing, and testing low-code or codeless platforms.
  • An AI-forward mindset: You are an avid user of AI tools and are passionate about exploring how AI can automate workflows, enhance creativity, and increase your personal impact.

Compensation, Benefits, & Perks

💻 Work from home with a remote-first community

🏝 Unlimited PTO (and the encouragement to use it)

📝 Student loan payback program

🏥 100% employer-covered medical, dental, and vision options available to you and your dependents

💸 Flexible Spending Account (FSA)

🏠 Monthly stipend toward your WFH setup, vacation, development and more

💰 Employer-sponsored 401(k) with contribution match

🏋🏻‍♀️ Subsidized ClassPass Membership

🍼 Generous Paid Parental Leave

💲 Hiring Ranges:

  • Tier 1: $109,600.00 - $137,000.00
  • Tier 2: $100,000.00 - $125,000.00

Unqork employs a market-driven approach to establish compensation ranges. In addition to a base salary, employees may also be eligible to receive a target incentive and company equity in the form of stock options.

An employee’s compensation within the range provided above depends on a variety of factors including, but not limited to, their location, role, skillset, level of experience, and similar peer salaries. As a remote-first company, Unqork incorporates a geographic differential into our compensation structure, depending on the candidate’s location. We utilize a tiered system—Tier 1 and Tier 2—to accurately reflect local market rates and ensure our compensation packages are both fair and competitive.

jobs.description:
Who We Are

Lightning AI is the company behind PyTorch Lightning. Founded in 2019, we build an end-to-end platform for developing, training, and deploying AI systems—designed to take ideas from research to production with less friction.

Through our merger with Voltage Park, a neocloud and AI Factory, Lightning AI combines developer-first software with cost-efficient, large-scale compute. Teams get the tools they need for experimentation, training, and production inference, with security, observability, and control built in.

We serve solo researchers, startups, and large enterprises. Lightning AI operates globally with offices in New York City, San Francisco, Seattle, and London, and is backed by Coatue, Index Ventures, Bain Capital Ventures, and Firstminute.

The Way We Work

The people who thrive here are builders who move fast, communicate openly, take ownership, and continuously improve themselves, their teams, and our company. Here's what that looks like in practice:

  • Move with Urgency: We move quickly, make thoughtful decisions, and keep momentum. We value action over perfection and learn by shipping.
  • Take Ownership: We own outcomes, not just our individual work. We make decisions that move the company forward and follow through.
  • Communicate Openly: We communicate directly, seek to understand, and create clarity for others. Honest conversations help us move faster together.
  • Build Great Teams: We lead by example, empower others, and create healthy teams where people can do their best work.
  • Raise the Bar: We're always improving ourselves. We learn from feedback, consistently challenge ourselves to grow, and focus on the work that matters most.
  • Think Long-Term: We design for what's next. We create scalable systems, simplify complexity, and use AI and automation to amplify our impact.

About the Role

Lightning AI is seeking an Engineering Manager, Infrastructure Software to lead a team of engineers building the software systems that operate and manage our large-scale GPU and bare-metal infrastructure.

The Infrastructure Software Engineering team develops production services, APIs, and automation that support the full infrastructure lifecycle, from provisioning and bring-up through monitoring, maintenance, and decommissioning. These systems enable engineers and other services to manage thousands of servers, storage systems, and high-performance networks programmatically, improving reliability and reducing manual operations.

In this role, a key initial priority will be scaling the team through hiring, interviewing, and onboarding new engineers. You'll inherit a highly capable, self-sufficient team, allowing you to focus significant time on recruiting and integrating new talent while providing technical direction, supporting engineer development, and overseeing the delivery of infrastructure software. You'll work closely with engineers across all of Infrastructure Engineering, including Compute, Storage, Infrastructure Operations, Networking, Data Center Operations, and Managed Services.

This is a software-first engineering management role that combines technical leadership, people management, and cross-functional collaboration. We're looking for someone who can guide architectural decisions, develop engineers, and help the team deliver reliable software as our infrastructure grows.

This role may be fully remote within the U.S., or hybrid out of one of our office hubs (NYC, SF, Seattle, or London), with occasional team and company offsites. We are not able to provide visa sponsorship for this position at this time.

What You Will Do

Engineering Leadership & Team Development

  • Manage, mentor, and develop a distributed team of infrastructure software engineers, including hiring, onboarding, performance management, and career development.
  • Establish clear priorities, ownership, and engineering practices that support effective collaboration and execution.
  • Provide technical guidance while enabling engineers to take ownership of projects and architectural decisions.
  • Foster a collaborative environment that encourages knowledge sharing, feedback, and continuous improvement.

Infrastructure Software & Technical Strategy

  • Lead the development of production services, APIs, and automation for managing GPU and bare-metal infrastructure throughout its lifecycle.
  • Define the team's technical roadmap and guide architectural decisions for infrastructure software and orchestration systems.
  • Drive improvements to infrastructure provisioning, validation, monitoring, and lifecycle management through scalable software solutions.
  • Establish standards for software quality, testing, deployment, and operational reliability.
  • Balance immediate infrastructure needs with longer-term investments in software architecture and maintainability.

Cross-Functional Collaboration

  • Partner with Compute, Storage, Networking, Infrastructure Operations, and Data Center Operations to translate infrastructure requirements into software solutions.
  • Collaborate with Managed Services to support integrations between underlying infrastructure systems and customer-facing Kubernetes and Slurm services.
  • Establish clear technical interfaces and ownership across teams to improve infrastructure operations and reduce manual work.
  • Communicate engineering priorities, project progress, and technical tradeoffs to stakeholders and leadership.

Who You Are

Required Qualifications

  • 3+ years experience managing software engineers, including hiring, mentoring, performance management, and career development.
  • Strong software engineering background building production backend services, APIs, or distributed systems.
  • Proficiency in Python, Go, or similar backend programming languages, with the ability to guide technical design and architectural decisions.
  • Experience leading infrastructure software, platform engineering, or automation projects.
  • Working knowledge of Linux, infrastructure automation, and production systems.
  • Experience setting technical priorities, delivering engineering projects, and collaborating across teams.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience with bare-metal provisioning, infrastructure orchestration, or hardware lifecycle management.
  • Experience with GPU infrastructure, GPU cloud platforms, or high-performance computing (HPC).
  • Familiarity with hardware management technologies such as PXE/iPXE, BMC, Redfish, or IPMI.
  • Experience designing infrastructure control planes or integrations across compute, networking, and storage systems.
  • Familiarity with Kubernetes, Slurm, or similar orchestration platforms.
  • Experience working in a startup or growing engineering organization.

Compensation

We are committed to offering competitive compensation that reflects the value each team member brings to our mission. Final offers are based on factors such as experience, skills, geographic location, and role expectations. In addition to base salary, our total rewards package for eligible roles includes a discretionary bonus, a meaningful equity component, and comprehensive benefits.

The anticipated annual base salary range for this role is:
$205,000—$310,000 USD

Benefits and Perks

We offer a comprehensive and competitive benefits package designed to support our employees’ health, well-being, and long-term success:

  • Comprehensive Health Coverage: Medical, dental, and vision coverage for employees and eligible dependents.
  • Meaningful Equity: RSUs that give employees a stake in the company's long-term success.
  • Retirement Savings: 401(k) matching (U.S.) and pension contributions (U.K.).
  • Flexible Time Off: Unlimited PTO, company holidays, and floating holidays to support work-life balance.
  • Paid Parental & Family Leave: Paid leave to support you and your family through life's important moments.
  • Professional Development: Annual learning and development allowance to support your professional growth.

  • Sabbatical Program: Four weeks of paid sabbatical leave after four years of service.
  • Flexible Work: Flexible schedules and a hybrid work model for our office-based teams.
  • In-Office Meals: Complimentary meals at our office hubs.

Benefits may vary by location, team, and role.

jobs.excerpt: Position overview SNV is building a catalytic commercial accelerator, built to close the gap between capital and impact in markets where both are urgently needed.
jobs.description:
Position overview
SNV is building a catalytic commercial accelerator, built to close the gap between capital and impact in markets where both are urgently needed. The Senior Manager for Impact and Intelligence is the intellectual engine within the unit. This role has two distinct but connected responsibilities: delivering client-facing impact measurement as a billable service, and synthesising knowledge across the portfolio to build a body of evidence that sharpens our offer and strengthens our market position.

This is not a back-office role. Impact measurement is a revenue line in its own right — impact investors, DFIs, and corporations with sustainability commitments are increasingly willing to pay for rigorous, credible measurement of their programmes. The right person combines analytical rigour with commercial awareness, and understands that evidence is only valuable if it changes decisions.

SNV holds a significant body of institutional knowledge — proposals, evaluations, programme data, sector evidence — accumulated across 50+ years and 25+ countries. Most of it is inaccessible or underused. This role is responsible for changing that: activating SNV’s knowledge base as a commercial asset, not just an archive.

Who you are
You are a curious and analytical professional who enjoys uncovering insights that help organisations make better decisions. You look beyond the data to understand what is happening, why it matters, and how evidence can be translated into practical action and measurable results.

You combine analytical rigour with commercial awareness. You understand that research, impact measurement, and intelligence create value when they influence strategy, strengthen client relationships, support business growth, or improve development outcomes. You are comfortable working with both quantitative and qualitative data and know when deep analysis is required and when a pragmatic, timely recommendation is the better solution.

You are collaborative, proactive, and enjoy working across disciplines, bringing together perspectives from colleagues, clients, and partners. When you identify important trends, insights, or opportunities, you share them and help others act on them.

Most importantly, you are excited by the opportunity to turn evidence into impact. You identify insights that can be leveraged across the organisation, helping shape new approaches, strengthen market positioning, and inform business development decisions. You are equally motivated by building knowledge systems and intelligence mechanisms that support better future decision-making, reducing uncertainty through the effective use of data, intelligence, and learning.

Key Responsibilities

Client-facing impact measurement

  • Design and deliver impact measurement frameworks for clients — impact investors, blended finance facilities, agribusinesses, and government counterparts.
  • Develop results chains, theories of change, and indicator sets for IDF and ICVC engagements where measurement is part of the scope.
  • Conduct primary and secondary data collection, analysis, and reporting to investor-grade standards.
  • Package measurement outputs as standalone deliverables — not appendices to strategy documents.
  • Identify and convert standalone measurement mandates: fund impact reporting, programme evaluations, baseline and endline studies.
  • Stay current with impact measurement standards — IRIS+, IMP, GIIRS, and equivalents — and advise clients on which frameworks fit their reporting requirements.

Cross-portfolio intelligence

  • Synthesise findings and evidence across all Accelerator engagements into consolidated intelligence: what is working, for whom, at what cost, and under what conditions.
  • Build and maintain a knowledge base that captures reusable assets — frameworks, datasets, case studies, and sector-specific evidence — from every completed engagement. Every engagement should produce a reusable asset. You own the system that makes that happen and the quality standard it is held to.
  • Identify patterns in the portfolio that strengthen the offer: which client types convert fastest, which interventions generate the strongest returns, which geographies show the most traction.
  • Produce quarterly intelligence briefs covering portfolio-level insights and implications for strategy.
  • Own the donor and tender intelligence function: maintain a systematic view of active and upcoming funding opportunities relevant to the Accelerator’s two streams. This is an early operational priority — a structured weekly digest feeding the pipeline, not an ad hoc scan.

Sales enablement and competitive intelligence

  • Build and maintain the Accelerator's sales collateral: sector evidence packs, impact data sheets, and proof-of-concept case studies for both IDF and ICVC streams.
  • Conduct competitive landscape analysis — who else operates in our space, how they position, what they charge, where we are differentiated.
  • Track market trends in impact finance and value chain development that are relevant to pipeline development. Feed findings to the team.
  • Support proposal development with data, evidence, and impact methodology sections where required.

What you bring

To be considered for this role, you bring:

  • At least 8 years of experience in impact measurement, monitoring and evaluation, or related analytical roles — with a significant portion in a commercial or advisory context.
  • Demonstrated experience delivering impact measurement as a client-facing service, not just as internal reporting.
  • Familiarity with the impact investing and development finance landscape — understanding what DFIs and impact funds require from their portfolio companies and TA providers.
  • Experience synthesising evidence across multiple programmes or geographies into actionable insights.
  • Track record of producing high-quality analytical outputs under time pressure — reports, evidence reviews, data packs — to external standards.

jobs.title: Senior Field Service Engineer-CMP Platforms (Remote, UE)
jobs.excerpt: Job Summary: The Senior Field Service Engineer – CMP (Mirra / Reflexion) is a remote, EU-based role, with Munich or Grenoble as the preferred location.
jobs.description:
Job Summary:

The Senior Field Service Engineer – CMP (Mirra / Reflexion) is a remote, EU-based role, with Munich or Grenoble as the preferred location. The engineer serves as a senior technical resource for worldwide aftermarket service activities, independently leading complex equipment installations, maintenance, troubleshooting, repairs, and upgrades. This role requires 8+ years of relevant field service experience, including hands-on experience with Mirra and/or Reflexion CMP platforms, wafer-cleaning (scrubber) equipment, and head and subassembly rebuilds on the applicable CMP platforms. The engineer owns complex customer technical escalations through resolution, collaborates with engineering and technical support, delivers advanced customer training, and mentors field service colleagues while following established safety and quality procedures.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities:

·Independently lead complex installations, calibration, and commissioning of Amtech manufacturing equipment at customer sites, including Mirra and/or Reflexion CMP platforms and wafer-cleaning (scrubber) equipment within the assigned service scope.

·Perform and coordinate routine and preventive maintenance on CMP platforms and wafer-cleaning (scrubber) equipment to optimize performance, improve reliability, and minimize downtime.

·Serve as a senior technical resource for diagnosing complex equipment malfunctions, identifying root causes, and implementing and verifying corrective actions.

·Perform head rebuilds and subassembly rebuilds on Mirra and/or Reflexion CMP platforms, including disassembly, inspection, repair or replacement, reassembly, calibration, and functional verification in accordance with approved procedures. Lead advanced equipment upgrades and modifications to enhance performance and meet customer requirements.

·Provide advanced technical support and hands-on training to customers on the safe operation, troubleshooting, and maintenance of CMP platforms and wafer-cleaning (scrubber) equipment.

·Maintain detailed and accurate service records, including maintenance logs, repair and rebuild reports, diagnostic findings, corrective actions, verification results, and customer communications.

·Own complex technical escalations from initial assessment through resolution and documented handoff, coordinating with engineering and technical support as needed. Use Field Service Reports, Start-Up Checklist, and Installation Quality Reports as appropriate to document and verify completed work.

·Maintain a high level of customer satisfaction by communicating service status, technical findings, recovery plans, and next steps promptly and professionally, while managing customer expectations throughout complex service events.

·Mentor field service engineers through hands-on coaching, troubleshooting guidance, and knowledge sharing. Lead onsite and offsite training on products and services, and collaborate cross-functionally to improve service practices while supporting company culture and values.

·Follow ISO procedures, quality guidelines, approved service and rebuild procedures, and applicable safety protocols, including wearing appropriate PPE where designated. Reinforce these practices when mentoring colleagues and coordinating field work.

Qualifications:

Required Education & Experience:

·Must have a valid Driver’s license and passport.

·Bachelor's in Electrical, Electronics, and Mechanical engineering or equivalent experience.

·8+ years of field service experience installing, maintaining, troubleshooting, and repairing complex electromechanical equipment at customer sites, including hands-on semiconductor equipment experience.

·Hands-on experience servicing Mirra and/or Reflexion CMP platforms is required for both US and EU postings.

·Hands-on wafer-cleaning (scrubber) equipment experience is required for both US and EU postings.

·Head-rebuild and subassembly-rebuild experience on Mirra and/or Reflexion CMP platforms is required for both US and EU postings.

·Understanding of Programmable Logic Controller (PLC) programs.

·This is a remote position with up to 50% travel to customer sites worldwide with regular last-minute travel. Some evenings and weekends are necessary to accommodate production and scheduled service demands.

Skills & Competencies:

·Ability to independently prioritize and lead complex field service assignments, collaborate across teams, and meet time-sensitive deadlines.

·Ability to perform intermediate math to perform electrical and mechanical troubleshooting.

·Demonstrated ability to resolve complex equipment issues, manage technical escalations, and mentor field service colleagues in troubleshooting and service practices.

·Ability to read, write, speak, and understand English to perform detailed machine installations, repairs, and ensure accurate documentation and reporting. Must be able to communicate with internal and external customers through multiple means of communication such as phone, email, etc.

·Ability to lift up to 40 pounds, stand for periods of extended time, sit for extended periods of time, and work in front of a computer screen for extended periods.

Other duties may be assigned to support the overall business. Amtech Systems has the right to revise and update this job description at any time.

jobs.excerpt: At Qualtrics, we create software the world’s best brands use to deliver exceptional frontline experiences, build high-performing teams, and design products people love.
jobs.description:
At Qualtrics, we create software the world’s best brands use to deliver exceptional frontline experiences, build high-performing teams, and design products people love. But we are more than a platform—we are the creators and stewards of the Experience Management category serving over 18K clients globally. Building a category takes grit, determination, and a disdain for convention—but most of all it requires close-knit, high-functioning teams with an unwavering dedication to serving our customers.

When you join one of our teams, you’ll be part of a nimble group that’s empowered to set aggressive goals and move fast to achieve them. Strategic risks are encouraged and complex problems are solved together, by passing the mic and iterating until the best solution comes to light. You won’t have to look to find growth opportunities—ready or not, they’ll find you. From retail to government to healthcare, we’re on a mission to bring humanity, connection, and empathy back to business. Join over 5,000 people across the globe who think that’s work worth doing.

Solutions Consultant - Senior Principal, NA ENT

Why We Have This Role

Our pre-sales team helps some of the largest organizations in the world find and close experience gaps with the Qualtrics XM Data & AI Platform, which combines experience management (XM) data with artificial intelligence (AI) to predict what comes next and act on it.

As a Senior Principal Solution Consultant in North America Enterprise (NA ENT), you will partner with our Sales Teams on our largest and most strategic opportunities to win both the technical decision and the business case. You bring the product depth to show what the platform can do and the strategic perspective to help executives decide what to do with it. While most of your efforts will be focused in the pre-sales environment, some of the additional cross-functional initiatives may include input in product direction, content generation, contributing to analyst reports/relationships and attending marketing events.

You will report to a Solution Consulting Manager in North America Enterprise.

How You’ll Find Success

  • Earning trust with Account Executives and Sales leaders as their go-to partner on deal strategy and execution.
  • Becoming a trusted advisor and strategic partner to customer executives, helping them build their XM vision and a roadmap toward the art of the possible.
  • Building and showcasing world-class product demonstrations to highlight the value of Qualtrics products in unique, compelling and creative ways.
  • Winning the technical decision and the business case on complex, multi-stakeholder deals.
  • Contributing to team outcomes, including win rate, pipeline, net new annual recurring revenue (ARR), customer satisfaction and strategy for key accounts.
  • Raising the bar for the team by sharing what works and helping your peers grow.

How You’ll Grow

  • Learning the full XM platform, including customer experience, employee experience and market research, and the AI capabilities that connect them.

  • Build influence with Product and Marketing by bringing field insight into product direction and go-to-market strategy.
  • Grow as a leader through mentoring, deal coaching and cross-functional initiatives, with a career action plan built alongside your manager.
  • As we build an AI-first company and change the market for Experience Management, you will be at the cutting edge of this transformation in enterprise software.

Things You’ll Do

  • Partner with account executives on discovery, deal strategy and account planning for key opportunities.
  • Lead discovery that uncovers business challenges and ties them to measurable outcomes.
  • Design, build and deliver tailored demonstrations, prototypes and proofs of concept.
  • Build business cases and value stories that connect XM and AI to revenue, cost and risk.
  • Lead executive briefings and workshops that help customers shape their XM vision and roadmap.
  • Answer technical questions on architecture, integrations, APIs, security and data.
  • Position Qualtrics against competitors on both product strengths and business value.
  • Mentor peers through deal reviews, demonstration feedback and shared asset development.
  • Partner with Product Management, Marketing and Engineering on new and existing products by sharing customer and field feedback, and contribute to content, events and enablement.

Required Qualifications

  • 7 or more years in pre-sales, consulting or another go-to-market customer-facing technical or strategic role at a business-to-business (B2B) software as a service (SaaS) company, or as a practitioner leading large-scale customer, employee or research programs.
  • Demonstrated ability to influence complex sales cycles both strategically and technically with C-level and vice president buyers.
  • Strong technical aptitude and the drive to configure, build and deliver software demonstrations tailored to a customer’s needs.
  • Experience building a business case or value story that ties a solution to measurable outcomes.
  • Working understanding of AI and data-driven solutions.
  • Experience coaching or mentoring others, formally or informally.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication, including presenting to executives.
  • Undergraduate degree.
  • Legally authorized to work in the United States.
  • Travel required (up to 25%).

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience in pre-sales (solution consulting, solutions engineering or solution strategy).
  • Hands-on experience configuring, building or demonstrating tailored software solutions
  • Experience with Customer or Employee Experience software or programs.
  • Hands-on experience with AI tools in a customer-facing setting, using them to improve how you sell and go to market.
  • Knowledge of survey design, change management, or quantitative and qualitative data analysis.
  • Experience with manufacturing, consumer goods or business services customers.

What You Should Know About This Team

  • We play a critical role in the commercial engine, driving innovation and market penetration through direct work with customer decision makers and scaling our expertise across the field.
  • Our team values initiative and independence. Everyone is encouraged to think ahead, anticipate potential issues and solve them proactively.
  • We are known for our collaborative spirit, a strong desire to learn and, most importantly, a commitment to our customers’ success. We help Sales and Qualtrics hit their targets by building customer confidence and demonstrating the value of our technology. We are comfortable in a fast-changing environment, and creativity is often our best tool.

Our Team’s Favorite Perks and Benefits

  • Pension plan match
  • We offer private dental and health insurance
  • Wellness reimbursement - up to the value of $300 per quarter can be reimbursed for a variety of wellness activities

The Qualtrics Hybrid Work Model: While this role is exempt from working in office, our hybrid work model remains elegantly simple for the rest of the company: we all gather in the office three days a week; Mondays and Thursdays, plus one day selected by your organizational leader. These purposeful in-person days in thoughtfully designed offices help us do our best work and harness the power of collaboration and innovation. For the rest of the week, work where you want, owning the integration of work and life. #remote

About BJAK

The original mission of BJAK is we believe people deserve smarter ways to plan, save and grow their money. This is the origin of our name.

Started in 2019, we built the first mobile-first, insurance platform, enabling insurance to be accessible online by millions in the region. Today, its the leading insurance platform in Southeast Asia.

Today, we are expanding ways to help people in the region — this includes spending, saving, investing, exchanging, travelling, and more. Our mission is help people get more from their money every day.

We have teams working around the world, with over 20 nationalities from our offices and remotely, who truly enjoys their work. We are looking for the most talented and driven people we can find. We are looking for people who work for their passion, not counting hours. Who loves building great next-generation products, not status quo. Who cares about redefining how everyone around us can get the best financial applications, not for an exclusive few.

If you're this person, we'd love to talk to you.

The Role

We are looking for a UI Designer to craft intuitive, elegant and high-performing interfaces for BJAK's AI and financial products.

What We're Looking For
