jobs.description:
Lead Talent Partner

About the Role

We’re seeking a Lead Talent Partner to join our growing People team. This is a full-time position focused on leading talent acquisition and helping shape the overall candidate and hiring experience at QD.

As Lead Talent Partner, you'll be more than a recruiter. You'll serve as a strategic talent advisor, a partner to hiring managers, and a champion of QD's culture. You'll own the full recruitment lifecycle, from workforce planning and role definition through sourcing, interviewing, offer management, and early new-hire integration.

This is a builder's role, not a maintainer's role. QD does not yet have a fully established talent acquisition function, and we're actively transitioning to a new Applicant Tracking System — so the right candidate has done this before: stood up recruiting process, policy, and systems from the ground up at a small or growing organization, not simply operated within a function someone else already built.

The ideal candidate is proactive, resourceful, and passionate about creating an exceptional experience for both candidates and hiring teams. They bring a consultative approach to recruiting, aren't afraid to challenge assumptions or push back when needed, and understand that successful talent acquisition goes beyond filling open positions. They are focused on quality of hire, building strong talent pipelines, improving recruitment processes, and using modern tools and technology to make hiring more effective.

This person will thrive in a fast-paced environment, take ownership of their work, and view talent acquisition as a key driver of business growth.

Responsibilities

Strategic Sourcing & Full-Cycle Recruiting

  • Own the full recruitment lifecycle across permanent, contractor, and temporary employment types, from initial intake and sourcing through interviews, offers, and onboarding coordination
  • Develop and maintain proactive talent pipelines for ongoing and evergreen positions to ensure QD can quickly respond to hiring needs
  • Create and execute customized sourcing strategies to attract qualified candidates through direct outreach, networking, referrals, and other creative channels
  • Recruit effectively across a wide range of functions — technical/engineering, data & analytics, strategy/UX, client services, project management, creative, and operations — rather than specializing in a single talent vertical
  • Champion QD's employer brand and communicate the company's culture, values, and opportunities consistently throughout the candidate experience
  • Serve as a primary point of contact for candidates, ensuring a professional, welcoming, transparent, and positive experience regardless of the hiring outcome
  • Lead offer management and negotiations, partnering with hiring managers, People leadership, and Finance on compensation, approvals, and start-date logistics
  • Maintain strong candidate relationships throughout the recruitment process, providing timely communication and clear expectations

Stakeholder Advisory & Recruitment Process Management

  • Partner with hiring managers to define role requirements, develop job descriptions, establish appropriate leveling, and align on hiring priorities
  • Lead structured intake conversations to understand business needs, challenge assumptions, clarify expectations, and ensure alignment on the ideal candidate profile
  • Act as a trusted advisor to hiring managers, providing guidance and constructive pushback on unclear requirements, unrealistic timelines, and delayed feedback
  • Help hiring managers establish effective interview panels, interview stages, and evaluation criteria aligned with the needs of each role
  • Coach hiring managers and interviewers on recruitment best practices, effective interviewing, structured feedback, and reducing unconscious bias
  • Build and manage interview processes, including interview loops, scorecards, scheduling coordination, calibration sessions, and decision timelines
  • Keep recruitment processes moving efficiently by maintaining accountability across stakeholders and proactively addressing bottlenecks
  • Continuously evaluate and improve the hiring lifecycle, including requisition approvals, interview scheduling, ATS workflows, candidate communication, and offer processes

Recruitment Innovation, Systems & Reporting

  • Manage recruitment vendors and evaluate new hiring tools, technologies, and assessment solutions to improve recruitment outcomes
  • Recommend and implement appropriate, role-specific candidate assessments to support consistent and effective candidate evaluation
  • Explore and integrate AI-powered tools and modern recruitment technologies to improve sourcing, candidate communication, and overall recruiting efficiency
  • Manage current recruitment tools within QD's Deel-based HR environment and lead the transition to a new Applicant Tracking System (ATS)
  • Own ATS implementation end-to-end, including system setup, workflow design, process configuration, and automation to maximize the platform's capabilities — this is a hands-on build, not an oversight function
  • Manage current recruitment tools within QD's Deel-based HR environment and support the transition to a new Applicant Tracking System (ATS)
  • Play a key role in ATS implementation, including system setup, workflow design, process configuration, and automation to maximize the platform's capabilities
  • Establish and maintain strong ATS data hygiene, ensuring candidate records, interview feedback, and recruitment activity are accurately documented
  • Track, analyze, and report on key recruitment metrics, including time-to-fill, pipeline health, candidate experience, and hiring manager satisfaction
  • Use recruitment data and feedback to identify opportunities for process improvements and provide meaningful hiring insights to People leadership

Onboarding & Early-Tenure Experience

  • Partner with People leadership and hiring managers to develop and improve QD's new-hire onboarding and early-tenure experience
  • Help define onboarding programs, processes, and standards that create a consistent and welcoming experience for new team members
  • Coordinate with internal stakeholders to ensure new hires have the information, resources, and support needed to get started successfully
  • Establish structured early-tenure check-ins to gather feedback, identify potential challenges, and ensure new employees feel supported and engaged
  • Monitor the early employee experience and identify opportunities to improve integration, engagement, and retention

Qualifications

  • 6+ years of full-cycle recruitment experience, including experience hiring across permanent, contingent, and temporary roles
  • Proven, hands-on experience building a talent acquisition function from the ground up — creating foundational process, policy, and systems — not solely operating within an already-established recruiting function. This can be from a smaller or growing organization and is the single most important qualification for this role.
  • Experience recruiting within an agency or consulting environment with billable-hours or utilization-based economics, and a genuine understanding of how that model shapes hiring urgency, cost tradeoffs, and role justification — not just general “agency experience”
  • Familiarity with technical concepts and terminology, with the ability to understand and credibly discuss engineering, technology, and other specialized role requirements
  • Proven ability to develop and execute customized recruitment plans and creative sourcing strategies that attract high-quality talent
  • Demonstrated experience proactively sourcing candidates, building talent pipelines, and developing strong professional networks rather than relying solely on inbound applications
  • Strong focus on quality of hire, with an understanding of how successful recruitment contributes to employee performance, engagement, and retention
  • Experience partnering directly with hiring managers and senior leadership to define roles, calibrate expectations, and drive hiring decisions
  • Experience coaching hiring managers and interview teams on structured interviewing, candidate evaluation, and recruitment best practices
  • Hands-on experience leading an ATS transition or implementation from evaluation through go-live — required, not simply preferred, given QD is actively transitioning systems now
  • Experience using recruitment technology and AI-powered tools to improve sourcing, candidate engagement, and hiring workflows
  • Experience supporting new-hire onboarding and early-tenure engagement, with the ability to maintain ownership beyond offer acceptance
  • Working knowledge of employment regulations and hiring market trends across the regions supported
  • Strong organizational skills and attention to detail, particularly when managing ATS data, recruitment reporting, and multiple hiring processes
  • Exceptional communication, relationship-building, and negotiation skills, with the ability to work effectively with candidates, hiring managers, and senior leadership
  • Ability to manage competing priorities, work independently, and take ownership in a fast-paced and evolving environment
  • Strong judgment, problem-solving skills, and the confidence to challenge existing processes and recommend improvements

Applicants who’d like to be considered for a full-time position must be US based.

The target range of base compensation for this role is $120,000 - $145,000. Actual compensation is influenced by a wide array of factors including but not limited to skill set, level of experience, and location.

Qualified Digital (QD) is a full-service digital agency focused on imagining, building, measuring, and improving digital experiences across marketing ecosystems. As a woman-owned and LGBTQIA+-owned business, we understand that diversity isn’t a box to tick or a quota to hit; it’s in the very fabric of the work we do. jobs.description:
About our Aerospace & Defense business

Our Aerospace & Defense business helps the world’s leading airlines, MROs, OEMs and defense operators keep complex fleets and platforms mission-ready — managing the full maintenance, asset and service lifecycle at scale. We are reimagining how that software is built and delivered around AI, and we are investing in engineering leaders who can put AI to work both inside our products and in how we build them.

About the role

As Senior Manager of Engineering for our Defense solutions, you lead the engineering teams that build software for the U.S. defense operators who keep their fleets and platforms mission-ready. You are an engineer first and a people manager second, and we mean both halves. This is a player-coach role: you carry the technical depth of a Principal Engineer or Architect, you guide architectural decisions and set the technical bar, and you take direct responsibility for hiring, developing and retaining the engineers on your teams.

Your teams are autonomous and own the full delivery lifecycle — design, development, testing, deployment and operations — with a you-build-it, you-run-it mindset. You make sure they have the clarity, context and conditions to deliver great work, in a domain where reliability, security and compliance are not optional. You stay close to the work: you join design reviews, weigh architectural trade-offs, unblock hard technical problems, and use the same engineering practices and AI tools your teams use every day.

AI fluency is central. You will drive AI adoption across your teams, from AI-assisted development workflows that accelerate delivery to AI-powered product capabilities that create customer value. This is not about hype. It is about making AI a practical, embedded part of how your teams work and what they ship, including in environments with strict data-handling and deployment constraints.

This is not a role for managers who have left the code behind.

What you’ll do

  • Lead and grow engineers. Hire, onboard, coach and develop software engineers across the full career ladder, from associate through senior lead. You measure your success by the growth and output of your teams.
  • Be the technical leader. Participate in architecture reviews, guide technology choices, and set the technical bar for the Defense solutions portfolio. You can read, review and reason about production code, and your engineers trust your judgment because you have earned it.
  • Own delivery outcomes. Ensure your teams deliver high-quality software at a sustainable pace, balancing technical quality with business and mission value.
  • Drive engineering excellence. Ensure teams follow modern practices: CI/CD, automated testing, observability, infrastructure as code and secure-by-default design, including the supply chain, hardening and accreditation expectations of defense customers.
  • Champion AI fluency. Drive adoption of AI-assisted development across your teams. Make sure your engineers can build and validate AI-powered product features, from retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) and agentic architectures to evaluation harnesses, and foster a culture where AI is a practical tool with responsible guardrails.
  • Remove obstacles. Resolve cross-team dependencies, shield teams from organizational noise, and keep engineers focused on what matters.
  • Partner across the business. Work closely with Product Management, Design, Architecture and senior leadership to align technical execution with product strategy, and engage directly with defense customers in technical discussions, workshops and co-creation.
  • Shape engineering culture. Foster continuous learning, healthy debate and ownership. Help engineers find and grow deep specialisms such as front-end, back-end, data engineering, applied AI, platform and SRE, and security.

What you’ll bring

Essential

  • Technical depth: significant experience in software engineering, with a track record of operating at Principal Engineer or Architect level — system design, cross-team architectural thinking and technology strategy.
  • People leadership: proven experience managing and developing engineering teams, including hiring, performance management and career development, with a coaching mindset.
  • Modern engineering foundations: strong hands-on background in cloud-native architectures, microservices, API-first design, CI/CD, containerization and infrastructure as code, and proficiency in one or more modern languages (e.g., Go, Python, Java, C#, TypeScript).
  • AI fluency: hands-on experience with AI-assisted development tools, an understanding of AI/ML integration patterns (RAG, agents, prompt engineering, evaluation), and a track record of driving AI adoption within engineering teams.
  • Full-lifecycle ownership: experience leading teams that own development, testing, deployment and production operations.
  • Communication: the ability to explain technical concepts to non-technical stakeholders and to translate business and mission needs into engineering direction.
  • Eligibility: based in the United States and able to meet the eligibility requirements for U.S. defense work for this requisition.

Nice to have

  • Experience delivering software to defense, government or other regulated customers, including security accreditation, restricted or disconnected networks, and controlled-data handling.
  • Experience in enterprise software or SaaS product development at scale.
  • Experience building or leading teams that ship AI-powered product capabilities — MLOps pipelines, AI safety and governance practices, or AI evaluation frameworks.
  • Experience working in or with Aerospace & Defense organizations, or on solutions for asset, maintenance, MRO or fleet-readiness management.
  • Background across multiple engineering disciplines (e.g., front-end and back-end, or platform and application development).
  • Experience with event-driven architectures, message brokers and streaming platforms.
  • Track record of modernizing legacy systems or migrating to cloud-native architectures.
  • Familiarity with security practices (OWASP, threat modeling, security tooling in CI/CD).
  • Experience with organizational design — team structures, team topologies and scaling engineering organizations.

What we’re looking for in you

  • You are technically deep, and your ambition is to multiply the impact of others, not just your own.
  • You lead with context, not control. You set direction and trust your teams to execute.
  • You are comfortable with healthy tension and constructive debate, and you optimize for better decisions rather than comfortable meetings.
  • You are AI-native. You use AI tools in your own work and are energized by helping others do the same.
  • You stay curious and expect the same from your teams.
  • You have grit. You navigate ambiguity, remove blockers and keep teams moving forward.

We embrace flexibility and hybrid work opportunities to support diverse needs and lifestyles, while also valuing inclusive workplace experiences. By fostering a sense of community, we drive innovation, strengthen connections, and nurture belonging. Our commitment ensures you can work in a way that suits you best, while also engaging with colleagues to share ideas and build meaningful relationships.

At SentinelOne, we are driven by a clear purpose: to give the advantage to those who secure our future. About Us

SentinelOne is a company at the intersection of AI and security, pioneering a new operating model for cybersecurity. Our AI-native platform unifies protection across endpoint, cloud, identity, data, and AI systems to deliver autonomous detection and response with clarity and speed. By combining real-time analytics, intelligent automation, and a unified data foundation, we reduce noise, simplify complexity, and empower security teams to focus on what truly matters.

Our teams are builders, problem-solvers, and innovators committed to shaping the future of security. If you are excited to solve hard problems alongside talented, mission-driven people, we invite you to help us build a safer future for humanity.

AI is reshaping every function across our business, and we enable every team member, regardless of role or level, to build fluency in AI tools and concepts. Those who thrive here actively seek out new solutions, experiment thoughtfully, and apply what they learn to drive better, faster, smarter outcomes.

As a Deployment Customer Success Manager, Strategic Accounts, you will be tasked with leading the customer-side success of SentinelOne's largest and most complex partner-delivered implementations, as our expanded global relationship with strategic partners brings together SentinelOne's AI-powered security platform and our partners' expertise in managed detection and response, managed SIEM, and incident response. You will coordinate executive stakeholders, technical prerequisites, cross-functional dependencies, regulatory or data residency constraints where applicable, and formal acceptance, helping ensure clear customer ownership, technical quality, and measurable results as partner-delivered services grow. This is a senior orchestration role that connects commercial promises, technical scope, and the real-life conditions required for a deployment to succeed.

  • Own strategic deployment success plans, executive governance, success criteria, and milestone alignment across high-complexity accounts.
  • Establish customer and internal stakeholder maps, decision rights, escalation pathways, and readiness checkpoints.
  • Validate POV exit criteria, solution design, SOW scope, and implementation assumptions before work begins.
  • Collaborate with partner delivery leadership to address schedule risk, scope drift, customer dependencies, and technical escalations.

  • Analyze repeat strategic-deployment friction and improve playbooks for complex enterprise delivery.

What Skills and Knowledge Will You Bring?

  • 5 or more years in enterprise customer success, complex implementation governance, professional-services program coordination, or technical account management.
  • A successful track record with strategic enterprise deployments involving multiple technical and executive stakeholders.
  • A working understanding of EDR/XDR, SIEM, security architecture, integrations, or enterprise cybersecurity operations.
  • The ability to navigate procurement, regulatory, security assurance, and change-control requirements without overstating technical authority.
  • Strong executive presence, written reporting, negotiation, and escalation leadership.
  • Experience partnering with systems integrators or external technical service organizations.
  • Disciplined control of project scope, customer readiness, decisions, acceptance, and risk registers.
  • Familiarity with AI SIEM, enterprise endpoint migrations, or AI runtime security implementations.
  • The ability to deliver measurable results, including successful completion of strategic deployments against accepted outcomes; fewer compliance-related surprises and customer-side readiness failures; predictable executive governance and faster escalation resolution; strong strategic deployment CSAT and time to value; and consistent scope integrity and first-time acceptance.

Why SentinelOne?

AI is redefining how the world operates and rewriting the rules of security in real time, and SentinelOne was built for this moment. From day one, we architected an AI-native platform designed to operate at machine speed, not as an add-on to legacy systems but as the foundation itself. jobs.title: Digital Marketing Specialist
jobs.excerpt: Digital Marketing Specialist eCommerce Remote, Philippines | 3 to 5 years of experience | Australian market OutsourcedIn is looking for a Digital Marketing Specialist who enjoys building campaigns, understanding why people buy and getting the details right.
jobs.description:
Digital Marketing Specialist

eCommerce

Remote, Philippines | 3 to 5 years of experience | Australian market

OutsourcedIn is looking for a Digital Marketing Specialist who enjoys building campaigns, understanding why people buy and getting the details right.

You are comfortable inside an ad account, an online store and a CRM. You can take a brief and turn it into a campaign, spot where customers are dropping out and make practical changes that improve the result. You care about the words on the page as much as whether the tracking works.

This role brings that work together across three Australian brands. There are online stores to improve, campaigns to run, commercial enquiries to generate and customers who could become regular buyers. With a transition from BigCommerce to Shopify and GoHighLevel being introduced, you will also help put important marketing systems into everyday use.

About Our Client

Our client operates three businesses across labelling products, office furniture and workplace supplies. Each has its own website, social media presence and advertising activity, serving a mix of consumers and business customers.

The products are connected, but the buying decisions are different. Understanding those differences will be an important part of your work.

Labels and consumables: A customer may be searching for an exact printer model, product code or label size. The opportunity is to help them find the correct product, place an order and return when they need more.

Office furniture: A customer buying one chair needs useful product information and a straightforward purchase. A business furnishing an office may need quantities, delivery details and a quote before committing.

Workplace supplies: A first order can develop into an ongoing business account. Marketing needs to support regular purchasing, relevant offers and consistent follow up.

You will help each brand reach the right customers while keeping its messaging, campaigns and results distinct. Customer information and retention activity will be coordinated where relevant and permitted.

The Role

You will implement the agreed marketing plan and personally deliver the work behind it. Your responsibilities will cover paid advertising, Shopify updates, product SEO, content, email campaigns, GoHighLevel workflows and performance reporting.

We want someone who can follow direction accurately and use their judgement. When a campaign underperforms, you should be able to investigate likely causes, make changes within your authority and explain what happened. When an issue needs a commercial decision or specialist technical help, raise it clearly with enough information to move it forward.

Priorities will be agreed across the three brands. You will be expected to keep work organised, use approved budgets and offers, and follow through from implementation to testing and review.

Key Responsibilities

Google Ads and Paid Customer Acquisition

Your paid campaigns will support both product purchases and qualified business enquiries. You will need to understand what the customer is trying to buy and whether the campaign makes commercial sense.

Build, launch and optimise Google Search, Shopping and Performance Max campaigns around agreed products, customer groups and locations. Maintain clear campaign structures and separate reporting for each brand.

Review search terms, negative keywords, bids, budgets, product performance and geographic results. Identify irrelevant traffic and adjust campaigns within the agreed spending limits.

Match the search, advertisement and destination page. Someone looking for replacement labels should reach a relevant product or collection, with compatibility and purchase information easy to find.

Investigate weak performance by checking the audience, search intent, offer, landing page, stock availability and delivery conditions. Make changes within your authority and record the problem, your reasoning and the result.

Use available margin and sales information when recommending where to increase or reduce spend. Consider order value, delivery costs, returns and repeat purchase potential alongside advertising returns.

Run relevant Meta campaigns and remarketing activity. Test audiences, messages and creative variations against a clear objective, and record what each test teaches you.

Product Feeds and Merchant Center

A product campaign depends on accurate product information. You will be expected to check the feed and the website together when something is wrong.

Maintain product titles, descriptions, images, identifiers, prices and availability within the relevant feed setup. Check that advertised information matches the product page.

Monitor disapprovals, warnings, missing attributes and other feed issues. Identify the source of recurring errors and complete corrections within your access.

Review performance by product group and brand. Flag products that are consuming budget without worthwhile sales, as well as products that merit further testing.

Check feeds after catalogue updates, promotions and migration changes. Raise stock, pricing or fulfilment issues before continuing to promote affected products.

Shopify Management and Migration Support

You will support the marketing side of the BigCommerce to Shopify transition and continue improving the stores once they are live.

Prepare and maintain products, variants, collections, images, descriptions and promotional content. Organise information around how customers choose, including label compatibility, furniture dimensions and workplace supply categories.

Review priority existing pages and their new destinations. Help prepare redirect requirements, then check that important links from search results, advertisements and emails reach the correct pages.

Check priority product content, prices, availability, forms and tracking before and after launch. Keep a clear list of issues, their business impact and their status.

Test shopping and enquiry journeys on mobile and desktop, including product selection, variant choices, promotional codes, forms and checkout where authorised.

Improve product and campaign pages so customers can understand the offer and take the next step. For larger furniture requirements, make the route to a commercial quote clear.

Complete routine Shopify configuration and content updates. Identify custom development or integration work that requires additional expertise and provide a useful brief on the problem.

SEO and Local Search

Your SEO work should help the business appear for relevant searches and help visitors make a buying decision once they arrive.

Research product and commercial search intent, including model numbers, product codes, label sizes, furniture categories and business purchasing requirements. Use this to prioritise agreed page improvements.

Improve product titles, descriptions, collection content, metadata and internal links. Make compatibility, specifications and practical buying information clear and accurate.

Create useful buying guides, comparisons and FAQs based on real customer questions. Check product claims against approved information before publishing.

Use Google Search Console and analytics to monitor visibility, indexing and organic performance. Investigate broken links, missing pages and changes following the migration.

Maintain relevant Google Business Profiles and consistent business information. Support local search opportunities appropriate to the business's actual service and delivery areas.

GoHighLevel Setup and CRM Workflows

The CRM needs to make enquiries easier to handle and customer follow up more reliable. You will help configure the agreed processes and test how they behave in practice.

Set up and maintain contact fields, brand segments, forms, pipelines, lead assignment and workflows. Keep the originating brand, lead source, enquiry type and current status identifiable.

Configure pipeline stages around the business's agreed sales process, including enquiries, quotes and completed sales. Confirm what information the person handling each enquiry needs.

Configure and test supported connections between Shopify, website forms and GoHighLevel. Check contact capture, relevant field mapping and source information.

Test an enquiry from submission through acknowledgement, assignment and follow up. Check repeated submissions, missing information and duplicate records so customers do not enter unnecessary overlapping sequences.

Review what happens when someone replies, purchases, receives a quote or opts out. Adjust workflow conditions and stop rules where the available data and integration support them.

Maintain a simple record of live automations, their triggers, intended audience and purpose. Document changes so later updates can be made accurately.

Email Marketing and Customer Retention

Different customers need different reasons to return. You will build campaigns around their purchasing behaviour and their relationship with the relevant brand.

Create and send promotional emails with a clear audience, offer and next step. Check product information, links, display on mobile and the intended customer segment before sending.

Build abandoned checkout, replenishment and customer reactivation campaigns using the agreed platforms and available data. Check that reminders stop when they are no longer relevant.

For labels and consumables, use purchase history to identify relevant repeat ordering opportunities. Check that the products promoted match the customer's likely requirements.

For furniture, support incomplete purchases and commercial enquiries with useful information about products, options or delivery. Distinguish an open enquiry from a customer who already has a quote.

For workplace supplies, support regular ordering and business account development with relevant offers and follow up based on known buying patterns.

Coordinate cross selling where the customer context, brand approach and communication permissions support it. Monitor delivery, clicks, conversions and unsubscribe activity, and use the findings to improve the next campaign.

Content and Social Media

Each brand needs content that fits its products and customers. You will be expected to create useful material and maintain a realistic publishing schedule alongside campaign work.

Maintain content calendars aligned with agreed product priorities, promotions and seasonal opportunities. Keep the brands' messages and assets clearly organised.

Write advertising copy, product content, social posts, emails and landing pages in clear English suited to Australian customers.

Turn product information into useful content, such as a compatibility explanation, a furniture comparison or a practical guide to buying in bulk.

Create straightforward campaign assets using available product images and approved brand material. Identify additional assets needed and prepare clear briefs where more specialist creative work is required.

Monitor relevant comments and messages, and route commercial enquiries to the agreed contact. Use recurring customer questions to improve future content.

B2B Enquiries and Sales Follow Up

A commercial enquiry can involve several steps before it becomes revenue. Your role is to improve the quality of those enquiries and make their progress visible.

Build campaign pages and forms for bulk orders, commercial furniture requirements and recurring office supply accounts. Collect useful details such as products, quantities and delivery location without making the form unnecessarily difficult.

Support targeted B2B campaigns and agreed LinkedIn or email outreach activity. Adapt the message to the purchasing needs of business owners, office managers and other relevant buyers.

Check that enquiries reach the right person and carry the information needed for a response. Help maintain follow up visibility through the CRM.

Work with the business to understand which enquiries become quotes and which quotes become orders. Use feedback on suitability, timing and purchasing requirements to refine campaigns.

Tracking and Commercial Reporting

You should be able to explain what the results mean and how reliable the underlying information is.

Maintain GA4, Google Tag Manager and advertising conversion tracking for the agreed purchase and enquiry actions. Validate events after website or campaign changes.

Investigate discrepancies between advertising conversions, website orders and CRM enquiries. Check for duplicate submissions, missing events and differences in reporting periods before drawing conclusions.

Report by brand and campaign, separating online purchases from commercial enquiries. Include relevant measures such as acquisition cost, advertising returns, conversion rate, average order value and repeat purchases.

Use available sales and margin data to assess profitability after advertising costs. Explain when a change in stock, pricing, promotions or delivery availability may have affected the result.

Track B2B enquiry quality, quote progress and completed sales with the business. Keep reported marketing results connected to what happened after the lead was generated.

Provide clear weekly updates and monthly performance reviews. Record the change made, the reason, the period reviewed and the outcome, with a practical recommendation for what to do next.

Your First 90 Days

The initial focus is to understand the businesses, establish reliable foundations and put the highest priority improvements into use. The exact sequence will follow the Shopify timetable, available access and agreed business priorities.

First 30 Days

Learn the product ranges, customers and sales processes. Review the existing campaigns, websites, feeds and measurement. Establish a baseline for each brand and a prioritised list of practical fixes. Map the agreed CRM process and the information needed to handle enquiries properly.

Days 31 to 60

Launch or improve the agreed priority campaigns and pages. Put initial CRM capture and follow up workflows into use after testing. Complete the relevant marketing checks for the Shopify transition as its schedule allows, and establish clear reporting for each business.

Days 61 to 90

Use the first results to refine targeting, spending, pages and follow up. Review enquiry quality with the business, improve the initial retention campaigns and address recurring feed or workflow problems. Present the next practical improvements with evidence from the work completed.

What Good Performance Looks Like

The work is accurate, organised and connected to commercial outcomes. Campaigns launch with the correct products, offers, links and tracking. Enquiries reach the right people. Automations behave as intended, and reports make it clear where progress is being made.

Over time, the focus will be profitable online sales, repeat purchasing and qualified business opportunities. Targets will reflect each brand's baseline, margins, approved budget and operating conditions. You should be able to explain the contribution of your work and the limitations of the available data.

How You Will Work

Follow the agreed brief and keep commitments visible. Bring practical ideas, explain why they are worth testing and work within approved budgets, offers and brand requirements.

Check your work before it reaches customers. Review the content, click the links, test the form and confirm the relevant tracking or workflow. Keep a record of changes and raise blockers early, with a clear explanation of what you have already investigated.

Use AI and automation where they help with research, first drafts, analysis or repetitive tasks. You remain responsible for product accuracy, customer relevance and the quality of anything published.

The Successful Applicant

You will have 3 to 5 years of practical digital marketing experience, including eCommerce work you have personally delivered. You should be able to walk us through a campaign or improvement, explain your contribution and discuss the results with confidence.

Essential Experience

Practical Google Ads experience, including Search and Shopping, with working knowledge of Merchant Center, product feeds and campaign optimisation.

Shopify experience covering product and collection updates, promotions, landing pages and improvements to the buying experience.

Practical GoHighLevel experience with forms, contact organisation, pipelines, workflows and email campaigns.

Working knowledge of product and collection SEO, GA4, Google Tag Manager and Google Search Console.

Experience writing and implementing marketing content, including advertising copy, website content and email campaigns.

The ability to interpret performance data, investigate problems and recommend proportionate changes.

Strong written and spoken English, attention to detail and the organisation needed to manage work across several brands.

Experience We Would Also Value

Previous involvement in a BigCommerce to Shopify migration, Meta advertising, B2B quote generation or marketing to Australian customers would be useful. Experience with large catalogues, consumables, office supplies, furniture or regular business purchasing would help you understand the products and customers more quickly.

Why This Opportunity Is Worth Considering

You will have the chance to get to know three related brands properly and see your work develop over time. A change you make to a product page, an advertisement or a customer email can be followed through to orders, enquiries and repeat business.

The variety is practical: everyday product purchases, larger commercial requirements and customers who return regularly. The Shopify transition and GHL implementation also give you the opportunity to help build systems the business will use every day.

For someone who enjoys doing the work, understanding the customer and improving the result, there is plenty here to get stuck into. You will work remotely from the Philippines, supporting an Australian client through OutsourcedIn.

How to Apply

Apply through OutsourcedIn with your CV. Use the cover letter field to describe one eCommerce campaign or improvement you personally delivered. Explain the business objective, what you were responsible for, what you changed and the result.

Include a short outline of your Shopify and GoHighLevel experience, particularly any pages, workflows or campaigns you built yourself. Relevant portfolio links and anonymised examples are welcome. If you share results, include enough context to understand the period, budget and your contribution.

Job Description

Work at Home Bilingual Dari-English Video-Phone Interpreter


Job Title: Dari Interpreter (for speakers of Afghan Dari)

Location: Work at Home position in United States

Position: Video-Phone Interpreter

Pay: $17 - $21 per hour

  • Compensation will not be less than any applicable state or local minimum wage.

We Offer:

  • Paid professional interpreter training and continuous development.
  • Incentives for meeting attendance targets.
  • Benefits include: Paid Sick Leave in accordance with applicable law, Medical, Dental, Vision, Employee Assistance Program (EAP), Accident, Critical Illness & Life, AD&D, Insurance Package, Inpatient Hospital, Short Term Disability, and 401K Retirement.
  • Employee Referral Program.
  • Advancement opportunities within the organization.
  • Interpreter support.
  • An inclusive and diverse work environment.

Position Overview:


The Dari Video-Telephone- Interpreter is responsible for handling calls on demand, and renders the meaning of conversations between Dari and English speakers. The interpreter breaks the communication barrier in a wide range of industries that LanguageLine Solutions serves: Healthcare, Government, Insurance, Financial, Utilities, Travel & Hospitality, General Business, Law Enforcement, Court, and 911.


The interpreter processes information quickly, concisely and recognizes sensitive cultural differences. The interpreter is professional and courteous at all times and uses appropriate terminology and understands common industry procedures and practices. The video and audio interpreting sessions may involve simple or complex, technical or non-technical subjects.


This position does not involve written translation however translators and other skilled linguists are encouraged to apply. The interpreters translate verbally.


**This is a remote position. The Interpreter works from his/her home-office. It is essential to ensure a quiet & secure environment**


Essential Job Functions:

  • Respond to video and audio interpreting sessions promptly and conduct interpretation in a friendly and professional manner.
  • Participate in online, video and audio training sessions.
  • Deliver interpretation services via video and expediently type data on a dedicated device, such as a laptop, desktop computer, mobile phone, or tablet, in order to perform the essential functions of the job.
  • Render correct concepts and meanings according to the conventions of established interpretation protocol, avoiding omissions or additions.
  • Speak clearly in both languages using proper pronunciation, enunciation and polite expressions.
  • Maintain a professional demeanor throughout the video and audio interpreting sessions at all times.
  • Remain calm during video and audio interpreting sessions in the event that one of the primary speakers is incoherent or upset, especially in emergency situations such as 911 calls.
  • Maintain punctuality and availability during scheduled work hours.
  • Follow client instructions, in compliance with protocol to ensure client expectations are met with the Limited English-speaking Person (LEP), avoiding interaction with the LEP without client’s permission.
  • Understand protocol and terminology for various industries including, but not limited to, Medical, Insurance, Finance and Law.
  • Demonstrate commitment to cultural sensitivity and working in a diverse environment.
  • **Some calls may be highly emotional and/or stressful in nature. The interpreter may need to remain on a call for extended periods without breaks due to the nature of the call or may, at times experience high call volumes. The interpreter must have the ability to provide the required, company standards of service within this dynamic environment. **

Qualifications

  • Fluency inDari and English and skilled in the associated cultural dynamics.
  • Ability to provide cultural competency and assess regional and accent differences to find ways of communicating with the LEP.
  • Excellent listening, retention and note-taking skills to maintain a high level of accuracy during interpretation.
  • Ability to concentrate, stay detached from the conversation, remain neutral and objective at all times, and remain on calls that involve sensitive subjects such as end of life conversations, pregnancy termination, vaccinations, and matters concerning sexual orientation and/or gender expression.
  • Education or work experience in language-related fields such as teaching, language assessment, translation or interpretation preferred.
  • Must be able to adapt to any LLS technology enhancements that improve service delivery and meet client demands.
  • Must be at least 18 years of age.
  • Legally authorized to work in the United States.
  • Applicants for employment in the US must have work authorization that does not now or in the future require sponsorship of a visa for employment authorization in the United States and with LanguageLine Solutions (i.e., H1-B visa, F-1 visa (OPT), TN visa or any other non-immigrant status).
  • High school diploma or equivalent.
  • Candidates who are currently employed by a client of LanguageLine Solutions or an affiliated LanguageLine Solutions business may not be eligible for consideration.
  • Ability to read and write the requested languages – highly preferred.

**Based on your location, a post-offer, a pre-employment background check and/or drug screen may be required**


Technical Requirements:

  • Dedicated personal device for business purposes.
    • Desktop / Laptop Computers with any of the following Operating Systems: Windows, MacOS, or ChromeOS.
    • Tablets (iPadOS or Android) are acceptable.
    • Smartphones (iOS or Android) are also acceptable.
  • Restricted brands:
    • Kaspersky products.
    • Huawei hardware.
  • High speed Internet connection for work related electronic communication. This internet connection should provide download speeds of no less than 5 Mbps, upload speeds of 3 Mbps, Ping value of no more than 300 ms, Jitter value of no more than 30 ms.
  • Must have access to a quiet space free from background noise or distraction.

Physical Requirements:

  • Must be able to operate a keyboard and mouse and remain in a stationary position in front of a computer and webcam the majority of the workday.
  • Must use a headset for prolonged periods of time.
  • Must be able to operate company provided software and systems to perform all aspects of the job.
  • Must have sufficient manual dexterity to type or write.
  • Able to lift up to 26 lbs.

We lead with empathy, act with an owner’s mindset, demand clarity, work without fences, and execute with urgency because patients are counting on us. From how we hire and develop our people to how we advance rigorous science, we are building a team committed to transforming medicine in autoimmune diseases, starting with the kidney.

Position Summary:

The Director, Commercial Analytics drives promotional effectiveness analytics for TRUTAKNA — measuring whether Vera’s promotional investment is working and shaping where it goes next. Reporting to the Senior Director, Commercial Forecasting and Advanced Analytics, the role also carries opportunities to flex into support for commercial forecasting as business needs and the individual’s interests align.

This is a hands-on, high-visibility individual contributor role in a lean commercial team. The person in this seat builds the models, forms a view on what they mean, and brings that thinking to commercial leadership. Partners include Business Operations, Marketing, Market Access, Sales, Patient Services, Launch Excellence, Finance, and Supply.

Responsibilities:

Promotional Effectiveness

  • Drive promotional effectiveness analytics for TRUTAKNA and inform the optimal level and mix of promotional investment across channels, audiences, and customer segments
  • Build and interpret promotional response models, program ROI analyses, and channel and campaign measurement; develop marketing mix and promotional sequence optimization capability as promotional history accumulates
  • Estimate the sales impact of personal and non-personal channels using statistical and predictive modeling, and design test-and-learn approaches where historical data is thin
  • Ground segmentation, targeting, and customer prioritization in promotional responsiveness rather than volume alone, refreshing as diagnostic patterns and account discovery evolve
  • Support field sizing and deployment, territory alignment, goal setting, and incentive compensation design with promotional responsiveness and workload analysis

Forecasting Support

Analytics Foundation

  • Draw on internal business data — CRM and field activity, patient services and HUB enrollment, market access and specialty pharmacy feeds, and sales data — to build a coherent analytical view of the business
  • Partner with Business Operations and IT on analytical requirements for the commercial data environment
  • Build reusable, well-documented analytics assets in place of one-off analyses

AI-Enabled Analytics

  • Apply AI and generative AI tools to accelerate analysis, automate recurring reporting, and synthesize unstructured inputs such as field insights, congress content, etc.
  • Evaluate AI-enabled analytics capabilities and vendor solutions with a practical view of where they add value and where they do not
  • Help set standards for responsible use, including validation of AI-generated output, data privacy, and compliance guardrails

Partnership and Communication

  • Contribute analysis and interpretation into launch reporting and the sales quarterly business review
  • Serve as an analytics partner to Business Operations, Marketing, Market Access, Sales, Patient Services, and Launch Excellence, translating ambiguous business questions into clear analytical plans
  • Deliver executive-level readouts that lead with the decision at hand, carry appropriate caveats, and land with non-technical audiences
  • Balance and sequence competing priorities across stakeholders, negotiating scope and timing transparently
  • Partner with Legal and Compliance to ensure analytics practices meet healthcare regulatory, privacy, and data-use standards

Required

  • Advanced degree (MS, MPH, PhD, or MBA) in a quantitative, scientific, or business discipline preferred; a bachelor’s degree in a quantitative or scientific field with commensurate depth of experience will also be considered
  • 8+ years of commercial analytics, business insights, or commercial data experience on biotech or pharmaceutical commercial teams
  • Demonstrated ownership of promotional effectiveness work, including promotional response modeling, program ROI, and channel or campaign measurement; exposure to marketing mix modeling or promotional sequence optimization a plus
  • Experience supporting patient-based demand forecasting, including funnel or patient flow models
  • Hands-on experience with real-world data assets, including anonymized patient-level data, claims, lab data, specialty pharmacy or HUB data, and syndicated prescription or shipment data
  • Experience working with internal business data sources, including CRM and field activity data, patient services data, and market access or channel data
  • Advanced Excel; proficiency with BI and visualization tools such as Tableau or Power BI; Python, SQL, R a plus
  • Practical, current proficiency with AI tools applied to biotechnology commercial work, with specific examples of where they changed the speed or quality of an output
  • Excellent written and verbal communication, with a track record of presenting to and influencing executive audiences
  • Proven ability to manage multiple concurrent priorities across a broad stakeholder set with limited direction

Preferred

  • Depth in forecasting methodology, including scenario modeling, long-range forecasting, and analog-based assumption development
  • Experience commissioning primary market research and integrating it with secondary and internal data
  • Product launch experience in a specialty, rare disease, or nephrology, immunology, or autoimmune setting
  • Experience in a small or mid-sized biotech where the analytics function is being built rather than inherited

jobs.description:
About Abridge

Founded in 2018, Abridge is the first AI-native clinician intelligence platform organized around the patient, built for clinicians, and designed to help health systems coordinate the clinical, financial, and evidence-based decisions for every moment of care. Powered by purpose-built AI for healthcare, Abridge connects patients, providers, payers, and life sciences companies. This year, the platform will support more than 100 million patient-clinician conversations across more than 300 of the largest and most complex health systems in the U.S. With deep workflow integration, the Abridge clinician intelligence platform has been validated to support encounters in 28+ languages across specialties and care settings.

Abridge is setting the industry standard for the responsible deployment of Al across health systems with continual and transparent Al evaluation. Clinical decision support references and cites gold-standard sources of evidence, and features like Linked Evidence map AI-generated documentation to source data, helping clinicians quickly trust and verify the output.

Abridge was awarded Best in KLAS for Ambient AI in 2025 and 2026, in addition to other accolades, including TIME Best Inventions of 2024 and 2025, CNBC Disruptor 2025, and Fast Company’s Most Innovative Companies 2025.

We are a growing team of practicing clinicians, AI scientists, PhDs, creatives, technologists, and engineers working together to transform healthcare. We have offices located in San Francisco, New York, and Pittsburgh.

THE ROLE

We're looking for a Business Systems Engineer to connect and automate the systems Abridge runs on, starting with Finance. You'll own the data and AI platform our Finance team runs on, and help every person on the team build with it.

Abridge's AI is used by clinicians at hundreds of health systems, and Finance has to keep pace with a company growing that fast. We do it with a lean team that builds. Every finance system lands in one warehouse, one semantic layer defines the numbers, and agentic workflows take on more of the close, reconciliations and reporting every month. You'll be the engineer at the center of it, reporting to our VP of Finance Operations.

The role has four parts:

→ Integrations. Keep every finance system flowing into Snowflake, accurately and on time: ERP, spend management, banking, CRM, HRIS and payroll, and cloud and AI cost.

→ Semantic layer. Grow the governed metrics layer, so ARR, burn, headcount and spend mean one thing everywhere. Its users are people and AI agents alike, and both read the same definitions.

→ A harness-agnostic agent platform. This is a design principle for us: skills, connectors and context that run the same in Claude Code, Codex, Cursor or whatever ships next, so no single tool locks us in.

→ Team enablement. Help accountants and analysts build, ship and maintain their own agentic workflows for close, reconciliations, AP, procurement, revenue recognition, technical accounting and reporting.

This isn't an ERP administration role, and it isn't about evaluating tools and writing decks. You won't configure the ERP, but you will design and build what flows into and out of it. It's hands-on engineering: you'll own what you build and keep owning it. You'll also know when a problem needs an agent and when a plain, deterministic pipeline is the better answer.

Most of your time will go to Finance's systems. You'll also partner with our IT & Automation, People and Revenue Systems teams on the systems we share, such as HRIS, CRM and identity.

You'll work closely with:

→ our GL Accounting Manager, Technical Accounting Manager, FinOps Lead and Payroll Manager, who build and run workflows on the platform

→ FP&A, who own most metric definitions

→ our IT & Automation, Revenue Systems, People, Data Engineering and Security partners

This role is based in San Francisco or Chicago, working from our office on a regular schedule.


WHAT YOU'LL DO

Own Finance Integrations

→ Own the Finance team's GitHub repositories: pipelines, the semantic layer, workflows and our skills marketplace. Review changes, keep CI healthy and set the standard for how the team ships.

→ Architect and own the integrations between Rillet, our ERP, and the systems around it: payroll (Rippling), spend (Ramp), banking (SVB), Salesforce (CRM), and others as we add them. Decide what flows where, by API, webhook or pipeline, and when to use a native connector or build our own.

→ Build and maintain the Python loaders and scheduled jobs that land our finance systems in Snowflake every day.

→ Keep them healthy: freshness, row-count and source tie-out checks every day, alerts that reach the right person, and runbooks someone else can follow.

→ Close the coverage gaps by bringing in the systems that don't reach the warehouse yet, such as sales tax, close management, equity and contracts.

→ Maintain the scripted ERP postings we already run, with tie-out checks and change control.

→ Partner with our IT & Automation and Revenue Systems teams on shared systems and standards.


Build Out the Semantic Layer

→ Extend the governed metrics layer (Snowflake Cortex Analyst today) to cover spend, AI tooling, budget and the hiring plan, and add the relationships that let it answer cross-table questions.

→ Take metric definitions from draft to canonical with their owners in FP&A and Accounting: one definition each, documented, tested and versioned.

→ Run validation and drift checks on every change, and keep the monitoring agent that proposes fixes honest.


Keep Us Harness Agnostic

→ Design the shared context (skills, MCP connectors and operating instructions) so a workflow behaves the same in every agent harness we use.

→ Run the team's skills marketplace: packaging, versioning, auto-update and retiring stale skills.

→ Evaluate new models and agent tools as they ship, and adopt the good ones without rewriting our workflows.

→ Own the guardrails: service credentials, read-only roles, data tiers, and a person approving anything an agent sends, posts or changes.


Help the Finance Team Build

→ Partner with accountants and analysts to scope, build and ship agentic workflows for the close, reconciliations, accruals, AP, procurement, revenue recognition, technical accounting and reporting.

→ Every workflow has a named owner in Accounting or Finance who signs off on its logic and output. You own the engineering; they own the answer.

→ Move workflows from draft to live with tie-outs, a clear human review step and an exception path.

→ Examples of what you'll build: reconciliation agents that prepare a workbook for an accountant's review, scripted journal entries that post only when amounts tie, a contract-to-revenue agent that drafts subscription setups, and month-end accrual analyses. Workflows can live in GitHub or inside the tools the team already uses: our ERP, spend management and HRIS.

WHAT YOU'LL BRING

About BJAK

The original mission of BJAK is we believe people deserve smarter ways to plan, save and grow their money. This is the origin of our name.

Started in 2019, we built the first mobile-first, insurance platform, enabling insurance to be accessible online by millions in the region. Today, its the leading insurance platform in Southeast Asia.

Today, we are expanding ways to help people in the region — this includes spending, saving, investing, exchanging, travelling, and more. Our mission is help people get more from their money every day.

We have teams working around the world, with over 20 nationalities from our offices and remotely, who truly enjoys their work. We are looking for the most talented and driven people we can find. We are looking for people who work for their passion, not counting hours. Who loves building great next-generation products, not status quo. Who cares about redefining how everyone around us can get the best financial applications, not for an exclusive few.

If you're this person, we'd love to talk to you.

The Role

BJAK is building a AI Finance Superapp for Southeast Asia across payments, remittance, insurance, wealth, and trading.

These products move real money. Reliability, regulatory requirements, and third-party financial rails are fundamental to the product - not considerations around the edges.

The Technical Product Lead owns a product vertical end-to-end, from strategy and outcomes through technical design, delivery, and launch.

We are AI-native by default, but AI is a means, not the goal. The bar is knowing where AI genuinely improves an outcome, where deterministic systems must remain in control, and how to build products that are reliable, auditable, and trusted.

What You'll Own

  • Owning a product vertical end-to-end, including strategy, metrics, roadmap, priorities and delivery.

  • Shaping technical design with engineering across APIs, data flows, ledgering, reconciliation, failure handling, security and scalability.

  • Driving trade-offs across correctness, speed, cost, reliability, regulatory requirements and user experience.

  • Building regulatory requirements into the product across KYC, transaction monitoring, limits, privacy and licensing.

  • Applying AI where it improves outcomes, with clear evaluation, safeguards, human oversight and failure handling.

  • Shipping products around external dependencies, including regulatory approvals, financial rails and third-party partners.

  • Aligning Engineering, Design, Compliance, Operations, Treasury and Finance around clear product decisions and launch requirements.

What We're Looking For

  • 5+ years of product management experience, including ownership of complex technical products from strategy through production.

  • Strong technical foundation across system architecture, APIs, databases, workflows, failure modes and distributed systems.

  • Experience working closely with engineers and ability to review, challenge and contribute to technical designs.

  • Experience in payments, banking, remittance, insurance, trading or another regulated, high-consequence product domain.

  • Strong product judgment and ability to make difficult trade-offs under technical, regulatory and operational constraints.

  • Experience building with LLMs or AI products, including evaluation, reliability and understanding when AI should not be used.

Nice to have

  • Engineering or highly technical product background.

  • Experience building zero-to-one fintech or consumer products.

  • Experience defining evaluation frameworks for ML or LLM-powered products.

Outcome

  • Clear vertical strategy and legible roadmap

  • Ships fast and clears the gates that actually block launch

  • Money is correct and users are never misled about the state of their funds

  • AI features are valuable, predictable and trusted

  • Trade-offs made deliberately under uncertainty and hold up when challenged

  • Engineering, design, compliance, and operations are aligned with minimal friction

Location

This is a remote role. We hire globally and work across multiple countries and time zones.

Candidates should be comfortable working effectively in a distributed, fast-moving international team and collaborating with colleagues across different locations.

Language

English is our main working language across global teams. Strong English communication is required.

Interview Process

Our process is designed to move fast:

  1. Online assessment or practical task

  2. Technical interview

  3. CEO / final round

For strong candidates, we aim to complete the process and make an offer within 1 week from the start of the interview process. Candidates who complete assessments quickly will be prioritized.

jobs.description:
About Refold

Enterprise integrations are still built by hand, one customer at a time, by a human supply chain of consultants. We think that's the last big software category that hasn't been automated — and we're automating it.

Refold is the AI integration delivery layer. Our agents build, test, deploy, and maintain integration workflows inside our customers' own products, white-labeled, up to 90% faster. Trained on millions of real-world contexts across SAP, Oracle, Workday, NetSuite, and Salesforce, we turn integration work that used to take quarters into days — and then keep it running, because the agents detect failures and repair mappings themselves.

Traction: 30+ paying enterprise customers, 1,500+ active users, 10M+ API calls processed daily, seven-figure ARR. Customers include Incorta, Kantata, Coupa, Naehas, OvationCXM, and Zycus. The results are the pitch: Kantata ships integrations 75% faster with 8x delivery capacity; Incorta cut time-to-go-live by 70% and recovered 8,000+ engineering hours; Naehas went from 3–5-month builds to 90% faster delivery.

Refold was founded by Jugal Anchalia and Abhishek Kumar, who have been featured in Forbes 30 Under 30. We've raised $6.5M led by Eniac Ventures (early investors in Airbnb & Uber) and Tidal Ventures, with Better Capital, Ahead VC, Karman Ventures, Z21 Ventures, and Titan Ventures participating.

We're assembling a founding team of people who learn fast, raise the bar, and shape the company from day one. This is the second AE seat in the US and the first hired to build the motion, not inherit it.

Key Responsibilities

  • Open doors: Land net-new logos across our core segments — supply chain, procurement, finance, and PSA software companies where an ERP connector is the thing standing between them and their next enterprise deal

  • Map the maze: Multi-thread accounts, secure executive sponsors across Product and Professional Services, and build champions who can carry the business case internally

  • Sell the blocker, not the feature: Run consultative, value-led cycles anchored on the cost of the status quo — stalled go-lives, deals lost to integration gaps, engineering pulled into plumbing, margin leaking into SI spend

  • Run crisp POCs: Design focused evaluations with explicit success criteria, timelines, and ROI; exit with a no-doubt close plan. We're deliberately moving away from 4-week POCs — help us prove value faster

  • Orchestrate to win: Partner with Marketing, Solutions, and Product to advance deals and set customers up to go live from day one

  • Own numbers: Deliver ARR targets with disciplined pipeline hygiene, forecast accuracy, and stage-by-stage conversion

  • Execute plays: Generate pipeline via outbound, inbound, partner co-sell, events, and executive dinners — and write the plays that work into the playbook

  • Close the loop: Feed timely, specific market signal back to Product, Marketing, and Leadership. At this stage, what you hear on calls changes the roadmap

Role Information

  • Average deal size: $50–100K land / $200–300K expand

  • Average deal cycle: 3–6 months

  • Quota: $1M first year, ramping to $1.2–1.5M in year two

  • Selling into: CTOs, CPOs, VPs of Product, and VPs of Professional Services / Delivery at software companies selling into enterprises that run SAP, Oracle, NetSuite, or Dynamics

  • Ideal customer: Sales-led with an integrations page, an internal PS team or SI dependency, and enterprise deals that hinge on connectors

  • Current growth team: 4 BDRs, 1 AE, 2 Marketing, 4 post-sales, 2 partnerships plus a 20-person engineering team

Required Skills & Abilities

  • Proven closer: 5–8 years in frontline sales with 2+ in Enterprise SaaS, consistently at the top of the leaderboard

  • Enterprise hunter: Track record of landing and expanding complex, multi-stakeholder deals at $100K+ ACV

  • Technical cred: Comfortable demoing and positioning a deeply technical product. You can hold a real conversation about APIs, schema mapping, auth, in-tenant/air-gapped deployment, and why an integration broke — without reaching for a Solutions Engineer every time

  • Executive-ready: Skilled at winning C-level trust and navigating legal, security, and procurement with ease

  • Builder DNA: You don't just run plays, you write them. Forecast with rigour, operate with ownership, and be comfortable when the process doesn't exist yet

  • Presence matters: Based in the Bay Area and ready to collaborate in-office 2–3 days a week (travel weeks excluded)

Nice to Have

  • Sold integration, iPaaS, middleware, or data infrastructure — or sold against SIs and system integrators

  • Experience selling to platform teams, not just end enterprises

  • Sold a white-labeled or embedded product where your buyer's customer is the end user

  • Early-stage experience where you were the one building the territory, not working an assigned patch

Why do you want to work here?

  • Impact: Fast-growing seed-stage company ($6.5M from Eniac Ventures & Tidal Ventures) with early Fortune 500-scale deployments and real, quantified customer outcomes

  • Speed: Founding-team seat to build the GTM motion from the ground up, with a direct line to the founders and a clear path to sales leadership

  • Ownership: Cutting-edge AI solving a high-value enterprise problem nobody has cracked — backed by technical founders building a next-generation infrastructure platform

Compensation

We're a small, fast-growing team, and we're intentional about building an inclusive culture from day one. We welcome teammates of all backgrounds and don't discriminate based on gender, ethnicity, sexual orientation, religion, civil or family status, age, disability, or race. If you're excited by our mission, you belong here.

Mission Lane is combining the power of data, technology, and exceptional service to pave a clear way forward for millions of people on the path to financial success. By attracting top talent and leveraging cutting-edge technology, we’re enabling people to unlock real financial progress. Sound like a mission you can get behind?

We're looking for a Principal Governance, Risk and Compliance Analyst to own the bridge between security compliance and engineering work, reporting to the Senior Security and Governance Compliance Manager.

The impact you'll make:

A Mission Lane cardholder opens the app on a Tuesday night to check her balance and schedule a payment before rent is due. She never sees the safeguards behind that screen, and that's by design. As Principal Security GRC Analyst, you make sure those safeguards are operating correctly and efficiently.

You'll take requirements from PCI DSS, SOC 2, SOX, and NIST and turn them into controls that run continuously across GCP, Kubernetes, and deployment pipelines. Evidence comes from the systems themselves, and engineers get guardrails that fit how they already ship.

Our GRC practice is still taking shape as we scale, and as a Principal you help define what good looks like: the standards, the workflows in our GRC platform, and the security habits engineering teams carry day to day.

Our core tech stack includes: AWS/GCP, Kubernetes, and automated deployment pipelines.

What you'll own:

  • Enterprise security policies and technical standards through their annual review cycle, plus the security awareness training strategy and content
  • Security frameworks (NIST, PCI DSS, SOC 2, SOX) and audit readiness: technical evidence collection, remediation tracking, and recurring milestones like quarterly access reviews, vulnerability scans, and IT DR exercises
  • Annual risk assessments and the risk register, plus the security metrics and operational risk dashboards behind joint executive reporting and KRIs, including how backup and recovery capabilities feed business continuity planning
  • Continuous control monitoring requirements across AWS/GCP, Kubernetes, and deployment pipelines (set with Cloud Platform Engineering and Security Engineering), GRC platform workflows that remove manual effort, and day-to-day work with engineers on simpler compliance tasks and earlier threat identification
  • Technical due diligence for third-party risk across the vendor lifecycle (proofs of concept, onboarding, annual reviews) for 100+ actively monitored vendors, plus customer and bank partner security evaluations, working with business owners, Procurement, VMO, Legal, and vendor contacts to gather documentation and track remediation
  • Primary security contact for external auditors and partner bank contacts (evidence requests, walkthroughs, inquiries), and guidance for non-technical partners on data privacy, security controls, and compliance requirements

You'll thrive in this role if:

  • You like making a control simple enough that engineers adopt it on their own
  • You enjoy explaining what a regulation requires to people who have never read it, in terms they can act on
  • You stay curious about new threats and new technology, including how AI and ML pipelines change what controls need to cover

Minimum qualifications:

  • 8+ years of progressive experience in information security and GRC, with significant experience in a FinTech, banking, or cloud-native environment
  • Demonstrated expertise translating complex frameworks (NIST SP 800-53, PCI DSS v4.0, SOC 2, GLBA, Sarbanes-Oxley) into practical risk analyses and technical control requirements
  • Strong working understanding of modern cloud architectures (GCP), containerization (Kubernetes), and continuous delivery models
  • Familiarity with continuous compliance concepts, API-driven evidence automation, and how platform engineers use Infrastructure-as-Code to enforce guardrails
  • Proven track record of executing complex external audits (PCI ROC, SOC 2 Type 2, SOX) in close collaboration with team leadership
  • Cross-functional communication skills, with a history of building collaborative relationships across software development, platform engineering, IT, legal/privacy, Procurement, and non-technical business teams, and of communicating security and compliance requirements clearly to auditors, partner banks, and vendors
  • Ability to travel 3-4 times per year for high quality in person collaboration

Preferred qualifications:

  • Active industry certifications such as CRISC, CISA, CISSP, CCSP, CCSK, AAISM, or cloud security specialties
  • Direct experience supporting bank partner due diligence, regulatory examinations, or GLBA compliance audits
  • Hands-on experience with compliance and collaboration platforms (Vanta, Workiva, Google Workspace, Jira, Confluence), Tableau, and third-party risk tools such as UpGuard
  • Experience evaluating security, continuous monitoring, and privacy controls for modern data platforms and AI/ML pipelines

Compensation:

Annual full-time starting base salary range: $137,958 – $180,000

Mission Lane also offers a comprehensive benefits plan, which includes paid time off, 401(k) match, a monthly wellness stipend, health/dental/vision insurance options, disability coverage, paid parental leave, flexible spending account (for childcare and healthcare), life insurance, and a remote-first work environment.

About Mission Lane:

Founded in December 2018, Mission Lane is a purpose-driven fintech company based in the U.S., with headquarters in Richmond, Virginia.

It all started with a realization: nearly fifty percent of the adult population in the U.S. doesn’t have access to a clear line of credit.
