Meet Instinct 👋

Instinct Science is at the forefront of veterinary innovation, comprised of world-class tools that have served our industry for decades: easy-to-use veterinary practice software (Instinct EMR), an essential resource for expanding your knowledge and skills (Clinician's Brief), clinical and pharmaceutical decision support (Standards of Care & Plumb's), and an AI scribing platform (ScribbleVet). Combined, Instinct Science offers an ecosystem that veterinarians rely on for every aspect and stage of their careers.

At Instinct Science, we believe in leading with compassion. Our team, our customers, and their patients and clients are the foundation of everything we do. Our culture is guided by our U.C.A.R.E. values: We move fast because our mission matters, we put customers at the center of every decision, and we treat each other with kindness and high standards.

A Sneak Peek of Your Role 🔭

This is a fully remote role.

We are seeking a dynamic, tech-savvy Senior Enterprise Account Executive to join our business development team. This is a hybrid role designed for a high performer who excels at nurturing long-term relationships while maintaining the "hunter" instinct for new business.

You will represent a sophisticated suite of tools, including Instinct EMR, the Plumb's and Standards platforms, and our ScribbleVet AI solutions. Your unique value lies in your ability to find white space within existing clients while winning new enterprise relationships and elevating the team around you through mentorship.

What You'll Do 🛠️

Your time and energy will be divided evenly across two key pillars.

1. Strategic Account Management (50%)

  • Maximize Value: Act as the primary point of contact for our highest-value clients, ensuring they are fully utilizing existing solutions. These accounts may include corporate groups, from smaller emerging groups to the largest and most complex organizations. As the senior member of the team, you will own the most strategic of these relationships.
  • Expansion Sales: Identify "white space" within existing accounts to upsell new features and cross-sell solutions.
  • Retention: Monitor account health and lead the contract renewal process to maintain a near-zero churn rate. Lead multi-year renewals and contract negotiations, and own escalations at the corporate level.
  • Consensus Building: Be a key consensus builder for internal resource allocation to enterprise accounts. Working with sales, marketing, operations, support, and development, you will help deliver the resources needed to win, maintain, and grow enterprise accounts, and provide internal strategic feedback on enterprise accounts across the organization.
  • Strategic Account Planning: Build and own a documented account plan for each of your largest accounts, with clear growth, risk, and renewal goals.
  • Executive Sponsorship: Serve as executive sponsor for key accounts and lead executive business reviews with C-level and senior leaders as needed.
  • Voice of the Customer: Bring enterprise customer feedback into the product roadmap.
  • Mentorship and Onboarding: Mentor junior account executives, and help onboard new team members.

2. New Business Development (50%)

  • Lead Acquisition: Prospect and win new enterprise accounts within the corporate sector.
  • Territory and Account Planning: Build and own a target account list of corporate groups, with a clear plan for each.
  • Strategic Outreach: Develop a pipeline of high-intent prospects through networking, social selling, and industry events.
  • Multi-Stakeholder Selling: Build relationships across the buying committee, including executives, clinical and operations leaders, IT, and procurement.
  • Proposal Management: Lead the end-to-end sales cycle from initial discovery to final contract negotiation. Proposals may be for a single solution or bundled solutions.
  • Deal Authority: Negotiate pricing and contract terms within defined guardrails, and lead complex bundled deals across Instinct EMR, ScribbleVet, Plumb's, and Standards.
  • Executive Demonstrations: Lead high-impact platform demonstrations on large enterprise deals, showing executive stakeholders how Instinct fits their workflows.
  • Cross-Functional Deal Support: Lead the cross-functional deal team, working with legal, finance, product, and implementation to scope pricing, security reviews, and onboarding for enterprise deals.
  • Pipeline Management and Forecasting: Keep HubSpot current and provide accurate pipeline forecasts.
  • Market Intelligence: Track competitors, industry consolidation, and market trends, and share insights with product and leadership.
  • Handoff to Onboarding: Ensure won accounts transition smoothly into implementation and into your account management book.
  • Account Plans and Enablement: Build and maintain account plans and proposal templates the team can reuse.
  • Strategy and Segment Input: Help shape corporate segment and go-to-market strategy, including win/loss reviews of closed deals.
  • Leadership Reviews: Participate in forecast and leadership reviews.

Who You Are 🐱‍💻

Must Haves:

  • Experience: 7+ years in Enterprise Account Management or Business Development, with a track record of closing large, multi-year enterprise deals. SaaS experience highly preferred.
  • Domain Knowledge: Familiarity with the animal health field and technology solutions.
  • AI Literacy: A working grasp of how AI is transforming enterprise workflows, with the ability to explain the "how" and "why" of AI in clinical management.
  • Communication: Exceptional presentation skills, with the ability to explain complex technical concepts to non-technical stakeholders, including at the executive level.

  • Leadership: Experience mentoring or leading teammates, and the executive presence to engage C-level stakeholders.

About the company

Nuitée is the API infrastructure powering travel, inside banks, AI assistants, airlines, loyalty programs and hotel brands. Nuitée Connect gives businesses one API for 2.9M properties, 600+ airlines and 200K+ experiences, built for apps and AI agents alike. Nuitée Cloud lets hotels reach new demand and control pricing, payments and operations in one platform.

Founded in 2017, Nuitée has 300 colleagues across 25 countries and a mission to make travel distribution simpler, faster and fairer for everyone in travel. We raised a $48M Series A led by Accel and work with companies such as Revolut, Grab, and Sabre.

About the role

Remote in Europe, or hybrid in Barcelona, Dublin, London, or Palma.

A live product making its mark in travel tech, a team ready to grow, and the engineering direction yours to set.

You’ll lead engineering for Nuitée Cloud: the platform hotels use to reach new demand and control pricing, payments, and operations in one place. It’s well past MVP, and 400+ hotel chains trust Nuitée to distribute their inventory. There’s still a lot to build from scratch.

Cloud has two engineering teams, and you’ll lead both: Connectivity, which builds the backend in Go, and Product, a full-stack team with real product ownership.

You’ll start with how the team works: how Cloud codes, designs, and tests. From there, you’ll set the technical direction with the senior ICs and grow the team. The challenge underneath is speed. Cloud has a lot of R&D, and a single product change can move metrics fast. How do you keep that pace while making the system more reliable and secure?

What makes it interesting for you

  • You set the standard. You’ll define how a whole product area writes code, designs systems, and tests, and shape those practices around how Nuitée works.
  • The architecture is still open. Cloud has to stay fast and also become more reliable and secure, and you’ll help set the technical direction to get there.
  • You build the team around you. You’ll own Cloud’s hiring strategy, career paths, and engineering culture.
  • You work closely with product. You’ll partner day to day with the Head of Product, Cloud, on what the team builds and why.

Nuitée raised a $48M Series A led by Accel and works with companies such as Revolut, Grab, and Sabre.

The kind of problems you’ll work on

  • How do we build one engineering culture across a distributed team that ships much faster at higher quality?
  • How should Cloud’s architecture change so a product built for speed and R&D also becomes more reliable and secure?
  • How do we give every engineer clear work, a clear reason to be on the team, and a real path to grow at Nuitée?

This role fits if you

  • Have led at least 10 engineers as a Director, Head of Engineering, or Senior Engineering Manager at a well-known product scale-up with a high engineering bar.
  • Have built large-scale, challenging web products, including the front end, and can work out how to architect and scale a product for high volume.
  • Have put engineering practices in place (code, architecture, QA) and built a shared culture that raised the team’s level.
  • Lead as a manager who sets direction and hands out work, and still get into the code when something needs to ship.
  • Have built career paths, hired, and kept engineers motivated.
  • Communicate clearly and drive things forward without waiting to be asked.

You’re strong in at least one object-oriented language. Our backend runs on Go, so experience with it would be ideal.

Nuitée moves quickly, has little process, and gives people a lot of room to make decisions. You’ll do well here if ambiguity does not slow you down, you like going deep into difficult problems, and you want to be accountable for what your team actually delivers.

If this sounds like your kind of engineering leadership role, we’d love to hear from you. You can apply with your LinkedIn profile or CV. You’ll meet our talent team, the Head of Product, Cloud, members of the engineering team, and our leadership.

Why Nuitée?

Nuitée is building the infrastructure to power travel.

  • Real scale: Nuitée Connect gives businesses one API for 2.9M properties, 600+ airlines and 200K+ experiences, and processes 1bn searches a day.
  • Strong backing: We raised a $48M Series A led by Accel.
  • Startup agility: We combine operational discipline with the speed and innovation of a scaling startup.
  • Global impact: Our infrastructure supports customers such as Revolut, Grab, and Sabre, alongside banks, airlines, loyalty programs and hotel brands.
  • Built for AI: Nuitée Connect is built for apps and AI agents alike, so teams can launch intelligent travel experiences quickly.

By joining Nuitée, you’ll be part of a team building a category-defining platform. You’ll work at global scale, innovate alongside industry leaders, and help drive the next phase of travel technology. If you’re excited to push boundaries and grow with us, Nuitée is the place for you.

By submitting your application, you consent to Nuitée processing your personal data for the purposes of assessing your suitability for employment. Your information will be stored securely and will only be retained for as long as necessary for the recruitment process, or up to 6 months afterward, in accordance with our data protection policy and applicable laws. You have the right to request access, correction, or deletion of your personal data at any time by contacting us at . For more details, please see our Privacy Policy: Nuitée Privacy Notice 2026.

jobs.description:
Hiring: Sales Team Leaders (TLs) – Pakistan & Nigeria

Locations: Pakistan (1 opening) and Nigeria (1 opening)
Compensation: $800 base pay during the Team Lead Trainee period, then commission on team performance
Positions Available: 2

About the Role

We’re looking for two motivated, results-driven Sales Team Leaders to lead, coach and develop high-performing sales teams. We need leaders who can drive revenue, improve sales performance and help their agents get strong results week after week.

We’re hiring one Team Leader based in Pakistan and one based in Nigeria.

How You’ll Step Into Leadership: The 90-Day Team Lead Trainee Path

Every new Team Leader starts as a Team Lead Trainee. Before you lead our agents, we want you to know our product, our customers and our sales process from the inside. Throughout the trainee period, you’ll receive $800 base pay until you fully take over a team.

Days 1–30: Learn the floor as an agent

  • You’ll work full-time as a sales agent.

  • You’ll learn our product, customer conversations, sales process, systems and targets firsthand.

  • Day 30 review: We’ll look at your sales performance, how quickly you learn and your ownership.

Days 31–60: Begin taking on leadership responsibilities

  • You’ll gradually take on leadership duties, such as supporting agents, monitoring performance, joining coaching sessions and helping with team KPIs.

  • You’ll keep calling and selling alongside this leadership work.

  • Day 60 review: We’ll look at your early leadership impact, your coaching ability and your judgement.

Days 61–90: Lead while you continue to sell

  • You’ll take on a larger share of leadership responsibilities.

  • You’ll still make sales calls for at least 2 hours per day, so you stay close to the customer and lead by example.

  • Day 90 review: This is the final trainee review. It decides whether you step into the full Team Leader position.

After Day 90: Full Team Leader
If you pass, you’ll take over a team, depending on the internal structure at the time, and move onto the Team Leader commission structure.

Key Responsibilities (Once in the Full TL Position)

  • Lead, motivate and manage a team of sales agents to hit revenue targets.

  • Monitor daily and weekly sales performance, productivity and conversion rates.

  • Coach agents on communication, customer engagement, probing, objection handling and closing.

  • Run regular performance reviews and give actionable feedback.

  • Identify underperforming agents and put improvement plans in place.

  • Support the recruitment, onboarding and training of new sales agents.

  • Track team KPIs, call activity, sales results and revenue.

  • Build a culture of accountability, continuous improvement and high performance.

jobs.excerpt: About ImpruvonImpruvon builds software and connected hardware that makes medication management safer for vulnerable populations in group homes, supported living, assisted living, behavioral health, and long-term care.
jobs.description:
About ImpruvonImpruvon builds software and connected hardware that makes medication management safer for vulnerable populations in group homes, supported living, assisted living, behavioral health, and long-term care. In these settings, a large share of medication administration is handled by non-clinical staff working from paper, spreadsheets, and memory.

Our platform combines eMAR+ software, Smart Medboxes, emergency kits, and gamified self-medication tools into one connected system that prevents errors before they happen rather than documenting them after. We support providers, state agencies, and pharmacy partners across 20+ states, and we recently won the first statewide medication management contract of its kind in the United States.

Our results so far:
  • 48% reduction in medication errors
  • 39% increase in compliance
  • 69% improvement in audit-ready documentation

About the RoleWe are looking for a Head of Product to own product strategy and execution at Impruvon and to build the Product function from the ground up. You will lead a team of two today, a Product Lead and a Product Specialist, with plans to grow.

We are a growing startup, and this function is being built rather than maintained. You will have real ownership, very little inherited process, and a direct line to the CEO and senior leadership. Product has been driven by our leadership team to date, and we are committed to a deliberate, unhurried handoff of that ownership to you, including knowledge transfer, context on customers and commitments, and hands-on support while you take the reins. You will not be handed a backlog and left to guess.

We are building toward empowered product teams, where leadership sets priorities and outcomes and teams have real autonomy to discover how to achieve them. You and our engineering leadership will define how Product and Engineering work together. Our engineers are product-minded and deeply involved in how the product takes shape, and we are intentionally not prescribing a rigid handoff model.

Our product operates in a regulated, high-stakes environment. A missed dose is a patient safety event, not a support ticket, and our customers are audited by state agencies whose requirements differ state by state. Product judgment here means understanding what actually happens in a group home at 7am during a shift change, not what looks good in a spec.

Key Responsibilities

Own the roadmap
  • Own product strategy and the roadmap across our full surface area: software, connected hardware, and pharmacy and EHR integrations. Publish it so the company can see what is coming and why
  • Bring a point of view on where the platform should go over the next 12 to 24 months, and make the case for it, including to leadership when it conflicts with what we currently believe. Product strategy has been set by our leadership team to date. The point of this hire is for that to change.
  • Weigh patient safety, HIPAA, and state-by-state regulatory requirements from the start rather than retrofitting them. In our environment, "ship it and iterate" is not always available
  • Treat reporting, audit trails, and business intelligence as first-class product. Audit-ready documentation is one of the main reasons customers choose us
Lead discovery
  • Spend real time with caregivers, house managers, administrators, nurses, and state agency stakeholders, and observe workflows rather than consuming feedback secondhand
  • Distinguish recurring needs from individual feature requests, and explain the difference to Sales and Customer Success
  • Design for three very different users: administrators who need oversight and audit readiness, caregivers who need speed and clarity mid-shift, and the individuals receiving care, some of whom are building medication independence for the first time
  • Design into existing routines rather than around them. Our customers cannot absorb a system that reshapes how a shift runs, and for non-clinical staff on shared devices, usability is a safety requirement rather than a preference
  • Set the bar for product definition: clear problem statements, acceptance criteria, and edge-case thinking Engineering can build from without guesswork. Define success measures before work starts, and measure what actually happened after release
Build the function
  • Establish how product gets practiced here: how problems get framed, how discovery happens, how decisions get made, and how outcomes get measured
  • Lead, coach, and develop the Product team, and hire as scope expands, including roles that do not exist yet
  • Keep Engineering, Customer Success, Sales, and Operations aligned on priorities and what is changing, and support them on strategic accounts and state-level opportunities where product credibility matters
Work with AI
We expect our product leader to set the standard on AI rather than delegate it.
  • Use tools such as Claude Code, Codex, or equivalent agentic development environments to explore the codebase, work with data, and build functional prototypes rather than relying only on mockups and specs
  • Establish these practices across the Product team and coach your people into them
The goal is better-informed decisions about scope and value, not handing engineering a flashy prototype to productionize.
You do not need to be a software engineer, and you will have strong engineering partnership for that. You do need to be willing and able to build.
What This Role Is NotThis is not a purely strategic or advisory position, and it is not a roadmap-maintenance or backlog-management role. You will be the most senior product person in the company, with no layer between you and the problem.

It is also not a role where you stay there. You will be hands-on from day one because that is what this stage requires. You will also be building the function that eventually changes that: developing the two people already here, making the case for who we hire next, and forming a view of what this product organization needs to become. If you want only the hands-on work, or only the organizational work, this is not the right role.

Skills, Knowledge, & Experience

Requirements
  • 8+ years in product management, including end-to-end ownership of a roadmap covering discovery, definition, and delivery, not solely execution of a roadmap someone else set
  • Experience leading product people, including hiring and onboarding rather than only managing an inherited team
  • A track record of shipping B2B SaaS in close partnership with Engineering
  • Experience building product process where little or none existed
  • Strong discovery skills: customer interviewing, problem validation, prototyping, and experimentation, with examples of how evidence changed your approach
  • Experience with products where the buyer and the user are different people. Our contracts are signed by provider executives and state agencies, and the software is used by non-clinical caregivers mid-shift
  • Practical, frequent use of LLMs in your day-to-day work
  • Comfort working with data directly, strong written communication, and the judgment to decide with incomplete information and own the outcome
  • Willingness to travel occasionally, up to roughly 15%, for customer and facility site visits, team meetings, and industry events
Nice to Have
  • Experience in healthcare technology, IDD services, assisted living, behavioral health, long-term care, or medication management, or another regulated environment where safety and compliance shape product decisions
  • Experience with enterprise, government, or state agency customers, including procurement and reporting requirements
  • Experience shipping products that combine software and connected hardware
  • Experience with integration-dependent products (HL7, JSON, REST APIs, pharmacy management systems, EHRs)
  • Experience scaling a Product function from a small team, or shipping products and internal tools you personally prototyped using AI-assisted development
Personal Attributes
  • A builder. Your instinct when you have an idea is to make something and test it.
  • Low ego and strong point of view. You advocate hard for a position and change it when the evidence changes.
  • Comfortable with ambiguity. You do not need a detailed roadmap to know what to do next.
  • Intellectually curious. You want to understand why a workflow works the way it does, not just what feature someone asked for.
  • Energized by the mission. Many of the people affected by our product cannot advocate for themselves. Medication management failures are not abstract software problems here.

Benefits & Compensation

At Impruvon, we know our people are our greatest asset. We provide a benefits package designed to support your well-being and growth, including:
  • Base salary of $183,000 to $225,000, depending on experience
  • Equity participation
  • 100% company-paid medical coverage (base plan)
  • Dental and vision available
  • 401(k) retirement plan
  • Company-paid life, AD&D, STD and LTD insurance
  • Lifestyle Spending Account (wellness, personal use, and company swag)
  • Flexible PTO plus company holidays
  • Flexible, remote-friendly work environment
Why Join Us
Working at Impruvon means being part of a mission-driven, passionate, and collaborative team. Every role contributes to improving lives and reducing risks in care settings across the country. Your expertise will help ensure we can continue to innovate, grow, and deliver on our promise of safer, smarter care.

Airspace is a tech-enabled freight forwarder that’s redefining how the world’s most critical packages are delivered. Headquartered in Carlsbad, California, Airspace has employees who are based around the world. Our European headquarters is in Amsterdam, The Netherlands.

As a recognized leader in AI and machine learning, our team leverages data and patented technology to coordinate logistics across a global network of drivers and airlines. Our goal is to deliver those packages that are truly mission-critical in a way that is faster, more transparent, more secure, and more accountable than ever before. The items we deliver range from organs for transplant, to parts for critical machinery including grounded aircraft and highly sensitive components such as semiconductors.

Airspace has been rated one of America’s best Startup Employers and listed as one of CNBC’s Disruptor 50 companies. Airspace has the support of leading investors such as Telstra Ventures, HarbourVest Partners, Defy Partners, DBL Partners, and Scale Ventures. To date the company has raised more than $140m.

The company is growing rapidly and serving more places around the world than ever before. We are looking for passionate, motivated individuals who want to make an IMPACT every day to help us execute on our mission of reshaping the world of time-critical logistics.

Own the Judgment Calls That Keep Orders Moving

Every shipment eventually hits a moment that isn't in the SOP — a failed carrier connection, an oversized load with no obvious coverage, a customer who needs a straight answer under pressure. As an Operations Specialist II, you're the person who resolves that moment without waiting for someone else to tell you how.

You've mastered the OS I fundamentals and are now trusted to act on incomplete information, source coverage other people can't, and de-escalate situations independently. This is where reactive execution starts becoming proactive ownership.

What You'll Do

Must be able to perform all responsibilities included in the Operations Specialist I job description, in addition to the following:

Resolve What Doesn't Fit the Standard Playbook

  • Independently start carrier traces for failed-to-load or unable-to-locate shipments
  • Source driver coverage for any segment of an order, including oversized shipments
  • Use bid/quote request tools to source specialized vehicles and provide cost estimates to customers
  • Apply training and tenured knowledge to anticipate complications and proactively solve for them

Exercise Independent Judgment

  • De-escalate most situations without assistance
  • Know when to escalate an order versus independently resolving it using available resources
  • Understand the downstream impact of decisions made within an order

Communicate Proactively and Strengthen the Platform

  • Communicate proactively — not just reactively — with customers, drivers, and agents at every step of the shipment process
  • Maintain any certifications required for your assigned sector and stay current on related compliance requirements
  • Identify and suggest system features or workflow improvements that would help Operations

Maintain a Balanced Level of Performance

As an OS II, you'll be expected to meet minimum metric requirements and customer service standards appropriate for this level. Specific metrics vary by sector and will be communicated by your direct reporting supervisor. Expectations increase with each advancement.

Requirements

  • Demonstrated success as an Operations Specialist I, or equivalent time-critical logistics / customer operations experience
  • Proven ability to make sound decisions with incomplete information and under time pressure
  • Track record of de-escalating difficult customer or operational situations without needing to hand it off
  • Comfort sourcing non-standard solutions (specialized vehicles, oversized loads) rather than defaulting to escalation
  • Any certifications required for your assigned sector (e.g., Dangerous Goods handling, where applicable), or willingness to obtain them
  • Continued availability to work the shift pattern required by your team
  • Available for 2 weeks of training in person on-site in our Carlsbad, CA headquarters

Advancement to Operations Specialist III

To advance to OS III, you'll need to demonstrate all of the following:

  • Minimum of 6-12 months in the OS II role
  • Consistently meeting or exceeding OS II performance standards, tracked through ongoing 1:1 check-ins and confirmed across two consecutive Semi-Annual Reviews (SARs)
  • Demonstrated advanced problem-solving proficiency — independently resolving escalations rather than routing them upward
  • Working understanding of margin and cost tradeoffs as they relate to order decisions
  • Manager recommendation, confirming readiness to operate as an escalation point for the team

Compensation

  • Hourly pay range: $23-26/hr
  • High-quality health, vision, and dental care plan options
  • 401K company contribution program
  • Professional learning and training reimbursements

  • We are One Team. We believe we all accomplish more when we are working together.
  • We make an Impact. We are determined to have a positive influence on our environment, our customers, our industry, and our world.
  • We are Passionate. We care deeply about our mission and are not afraid to raise the bar.
  • We are Transparent. We pride ourselves on having open, honest, and sincere communication with our team and customers.
  • We are Innovative. We never settle and are always striving to improve our product, service, and ourselves.

jobs.description:
Über Lingoda
Vor 12 Jahren gegründet, stellt sich Lingoda einer der drängendsten globalen Herausforderungen unserer Zeit: dem Bedarf wachsender Wirtschaften und alternder Bevölkerungen mit der Mobilität globaler Talente zu begegnen. Angetrieben von unserer Mission – „Menschen weltweit mit Sprachkenntnissen, kulturellem Verständnis und technischem Know-how auszustatten, damit Integration und Erfolg möglich werden“ – hat sich Lingoda als Vorreiter im Bildungsbereich etabliert.
Was wir tun
Seit Oktober 2026 erweitert Lingoda sein Bildungsportfolio über Curani.org mit digitalen Lernangeboten für die häusliche Pflege gemäß § 45 SGB XI. Dabei baut Curani auf Lingodas langjähriger E-Learning-Kompetenz und fundierter Erfahrung im Gesundheitssektor (über 9.500 qualifizierte Pflege- und Gesundheitsfachkräfte) auf.
Wen wir unterstützen
Mit interaktiven Online-Lernformatenunterstützt Curani.org Menschen, die ehrenamtlich Verantwortung bei der Pflege für Angehörige oder im persönlichen Umfeld übernehmen. Unsere eigens entwickelte Lernplattform hilft den Lernenden dabei, ihre Ziele zu erreichen. Mit unserem Kursangebot möchten wir ehrenamtlich pflegenden Personen genau die Entlastung, den Austausch und das Handlungswissen geben, das sie im Pflegealltag brauchen.
Warum du bei uns einsteigen solltest
Ein Einstieg bei Lingoda bedeutet, Teil eines Teams zu werden, das gemeinsam besser wird. Wir leben eine inklusive Kultur, in der Mut, Neugier und persönliches Wachstum gefördert werden. Erkenntnisse setzen wir in Taten um – und jede*r Einzelne trägt dazu bei, positive Veränderungen zu bewirken.
Werde Teil unserer Mission, Leben durch Bildung zu verändern.
Wir suchen zum nächstmöglichen Zeitpunkt eine Pflegefachkraft für online Pflegekurse § 45 SGB XI (alle Geschlechter) Die Stelle kannst du remote von überall in Deutschland aus übernehmen, in Teilzeit oder Vollzeit. Wir suchen jemanden, der abends arbeitet (Montag bis Freitag, 16:00 bis 21:00 Uhr) und gelegentlich auch am Wochenende verfügbar ist.

Deine Mission bei uns: Du übernimmst die fachdidaktische Verantwortung für unsere digitalen Bildungsangebote nach § 45 SGB XI. Komplexe Inhalte erklärst du im virtuellen Raum verständlich und nahbar. Im Live-Unterricht gibst du pflegenden Angehörigen und anderen ehrenamtlich Pflegenden verlässliche Orientierung. Gleichzeitig entwickelst du unser Schulungsportfolio mit Blick auf neue innovative Lernformate und sich ändernde rechtliche Rahmenbedingungen kontinuierlich weiter.

Deine Aufgaben:

  • Live-Online-Unterricht und Gruppenmoderation: Du unterrichtest unsere Online-Pflegekurse nach § 45 SGB XI im virtuellen Klassenzimmer (überwiegend in den Abendstunden). Dabei leitest du die Gruppen, vermittelst Praxiswissen anschaulich und schaffst eine vertrauensvolle Lernatmosphäre. Bei neuen, alternativen Kursformaten übernimmst du die didaktische Erprobung und Moderation in der Praxis.
  • Fachliche Teilnehmenden-Begleitung: Zusätzlich zu den terminierten Online-Kursen stehst du den Teilnehmenden in digitalen Austauschformaten als Fachperson zur Seite und beantwortest empathisch ihre Fragen.
  • Konzeption und strategische Weiterentwicklung: Du bringst deine Expertise aus der Pflege aktiv in die Produktentwicklung ein und gestaltest digitale Bildungsangebote von der Idee bis zur Umsetzung. Dabei verfolgst du politische Entwicklungen (z. B. PNoG, GeDIG) vorausschauend und übersetzt Neuerungen in praxisnahe Kursinhalte.

Das bringst du mit:

  • Ausbildung und Qualifikation: abgeschlossene Ausbildung als Pflegefachkraft (Gesundheits- und Krankenpfleger/in, Altenpfleger/in oder Pflegefachfrau/-mann).
  • Berufserfahrung: mindestens ein Jahr Berufserfahrung in der häuslichen oder ambulanten Pflege.
  • Konzeptionelle und pädagogische Erfahrung in der Erwachsenenbildung und die Fähigkeit, pflegefachliche und sozialrechtliche Themen praxisnah aufzubereiten.
  • Kamera-Präsenz und Freude an digitaler Wissensvermittlung: Du stehst gern vor der Kamera, moderierst Online-Gruppen empathisch und nutzt gängige Videokonferenz-Tools souverän.
  • Zielgruppen- und Praxisverständnis: Du verstehst die Lebensrealität pflegender Angehöriger aus der Praxis und hältst dich fachlich stets auf dem neuesten Stand.
  • Sprachkompetenz: Deutsch auf muttersprachlichem Niveau (mind. C1) sowie hervorragende Kommunikationsfähigkeiten für den virtuellen Unterricht.
  • Verfügbarkeit am Abend: Du bist werktags verlässlich zwischen 16 und 21 Uhr für unsere Live-Kurse verfügbar; gelegentliche Einsätze am Wochenende (ca. zweimal im Monat) sind ein großes Plus.

Schön, wenn du zusätzlich mitbringst:
  • Pädagogische Zusatzqualifikation(en), z.B. als zertifizierte:r Pflegeberater:in gem. § 7a SGB XI oder Kursleiter:in für Pflegekurse nach § 45 SGB XI, sind von Vorteil.

SGB XI, Kassenanforderungen oder Landesregelungen zur Nachbarschaftshilfe) ein und bereitest diese verständlich für unsere Kurse auf. Vorkenntnisse zu einzelnen Bundesländern sind ein Plus, aber kein Muss.
  • Vertrautheit mit E-Learning- und Kollaborations-Tools.

We’re a team of builders, adventurers, and risk takers using technology to help people confidently explore the outdoors. Driven by our mission to awaken the adventurer inside everyone, we build products that optimize every outdoor experience and inspire confidence to get out and go further.

Our impact comes to life through the products we build, in the stories of our customers, and in our growing commitment to land stewardship and recreational access.

ABOUT THIS OPPORTUNITY

onX is seeking a motivated Account Executive II to help grow onX for Business. In this role, you will manage the full sales cycle for inbound and new business opportunities, from initial outreach and discovery through proposal and close. Working within established sales processes, you'll build customer relationships, identify opportunities, and partner with sales leadership to navigate more complex deals. Your initial focus is expected to be law enforcement and public safety organizations, with the flexibility to work other segments as our strategy evolves.

This role requires a sales professional who thrives in a fast-paced, entrepreneurial environment. You will collaborate with Sales, Marketing, and Customer Success to connect customer needs with onX's offline operational mapping solutions. The ideal candidate has a track record of uncovering opportunities, building relationships quickly, and hitting targets.

This position reports to the GM, onX for Business.

WHAT YOU'LL DO
Essential Job Duties & Functions

  • Respond to and qualify inbound leads, and generate net new opportunities through outbound outreach.

WHAT YOU’LL BRING

  • Two (2) or more years of B2B sales experience, with demonstrated ability to manage sales opportunities from prospecting and discovery through proposal and close. Experience in a full-cycle, quota-carrying role is preferred.
  • Comfort with a high-activity sales motion, including daily outbound calls and email.
  • Strong communication and interpersonal skills, including the ability to build customer trust, understand customer needs, and clearly communicate product value.
  • Experience using AI tools to improve sales productivity, such as account research, outreach preparation, or meeting follow-up, with sound judgment in reviewing outputs and protecting customer information.
  • Proven success meeting and exceeding sales targets and KPIs.

ADDED BONUSES

Though not required, we would be thrilled to consider candidates with any of the following:

  • Experience selling to law enforcement, public safety, or other government customers.
  • Technical understanding of GIS software, data visualization, and collaborative mapping technology.
  • Experience with field operations in Emergency Services, Agriculture, or Conservation Agencies.
  • Experience selling SaaS, mobile, or other technology solutions.
  • A bachelor's degree in Business, Marketing, or a related field is a bonus.

THE ONX EXPERIENCE

onX is a distributed company with more than 400 employees across the country. We come together regularly to work in person and stay connected through regional basecamps and a culture that balances individual ownership with deep collaboration.

While we move quickly, we’re not a scrappy start-up. We operate with clear goals, structure, and frameworks that guide how we prioritize and execute. Priorities matter. While they may shift, data shapes how we evolve as our business, products, and the world around us change.

Clear priorities and structure don’t limit ownership - they make it possible. You’ll have the autonomy to define your work and make meaningful decisions within clear strategic boundaries. You’ll partner closely with others to solve complex problems and build solutions that scale across teams and platforms. Along the way, you’ll be supported with feedback, tools, and opportunities to grow your craft as you take on new challenges.

WHERE YOU CAN WORK

We have a strong preference for hiring candidates who live near one of our offices or within a Basecamp, and we prioritize candidates in these locations first. HOW YOU’LL BE COMPENSATED

The pay range will vary based on experience, skills, certifications, and education, among other factors outlined in the job description.

This role is eligible for the Sales Incentive Compensation Plan (SICP). Compensation is structured as 55% base salary and 45% target variable compensation, with total annual on-target earnings (OTE) of approximately $97,783 - $122,229. Target variable compensation is earned by achieving 100% of assigned quarterly quotas throughout the year. Actual incentive earnings depend on performance and are not guaranteed.

In addition, full-time onX employees are eligible for a grant of common share options with vesting schedule.

WHAT WE’RE OFFERING YOU

jobs.description:
Description

CapsLock is a global IT marketing company that pioneers unique, scalable customer acquisition solutions for B2C clients. We solve complex sales challenges across a wide range of industries, primarily for large North American partners. By integrating our expertise in Digital Marketing, IT, Design, AI-driven analytics, proprietary MarTech, and sales consulting, we deliver powerful, data-informed customer acquisition solutions.

At CapsLock, people, technology, and forward-thinking innovation lie at the heart of everything we do. Our diverse, global team, fluent in over 10 languages, thrives on open collaboration and the exchange of new ideas, pushing boundaries to ensure our clients’ success.

Role overview

We’re looking for an IT Systems Engineer to own the administration and security of our core tools, from Okta and Google Workspace to Slack, ClickUp and the AI tools our teams use every day. Our team is fully remote and works with a Bring Your Own Device policy, which makes for some interesting security challenges.

In your first months, you’ll take part in the rollout of Okta, 1Password and an endpoint security solution across the company. You’ll then help us harden our infrastructure, automate onboarding and offboarding, and keep a close eye on security as we scale.

You’ll have opportunity to drive your own initiatives, and you’ll also be the first point of contact when colleagues need help with access or tools. If you have strong foundations in at least one area and enjoy learning the rest, you’ll have a lot of independence, a budget for state-of-the-art tooling, and room to grow into a team lead role as the team scales.

Responsibilities

Security Tool Rollout

  • Take key part in the rollout of Okta, 1Password and an endpoint security solution across the company
  • Evaluate tools and present recommendations to the CTO and IT Director
  • Apply security baselines across tools and devices

Identity & Access Management

  • Own the administration of Okta, including SSO, MFA and integrations with our tools
  • Manage access to new software and AI tools through Okta
  • Run regular access reviews and fix permissions that don’t match current roles

Tool Administration

  • Administer Google Workspace, Slack, ClickUp and AI assistant tools, including users, permissions and security settings
  • Track licences and flag unused or underused accounts
  • Maintain an up-to-date inventory of tools, accounts and admin roles

Automation

  • Automate onboarding so new joiners get the right access on day one
  • Automate offboarding so leavers lose access promptly and their data is handled correctly
  • Build integrations and workflows between tools using automation platforms or scripting

Security Monitoring & Support

  • Monitor security alerts, sign-in activity and admin logs, and act on issues
  • Work with our security and DevOps colleagues on infrastructure hardening
  • Handle first-line access requests and support tickets from colleagues
  • Investigate incidents, then record causes and fixes

Documentation

  • Document every tool, automation and process so others can understand and run it
  • Write clear guides for colleagues on access and security practices
  • Share regular progress updates and agree priorities with your manager

Requirements

Must-Have Skills

  • 3+ years of hands-on experience administering tools for organisations of 50+ people
  • Hands-on experience administering Okta (or equivalent IAM solution) and Google Workspace
  • A track record of driving IT or security initiatives, not only handling tickets
  • Willingness to handle requests from the team, helping keep tools and infrastructure running smoothly

Technical Skills

  • Solid understanding of identity and access management, including SSO, MFA and role-based access
  • Working knowledge of device management and endpoint protection
  • Ability to build workflows with automation platforms, APIs or scripting
  • Understanding of security good practice for SaaS tools and BYOD environments
  • Cybersecurity experience is a strong plus
  • An engineering degree is a plus
  • Upper-intermediate English (B2) or higher

Soft Skills

  • Takes ownership and works independently in a less structured environment
  • Coachable and open to feedback
  • Explains technical topics clearly to non-technical colleagues
  • Organised, prioritises well and follows through
  • Collaborative and low-ego team player

What we offer

  • Remote Work - We offer a truly and fully remote environment. You choose where you are the most productive and comfortable to have an impact.
  • Paid Vacations - Generous paid vacation policy to ensure you have time to recharge.
  • Unlimited Sick Days - We understand that being only human means getting sick or feeling under the weather from time to time, so we guarantee you time off as long as you need to recover and get back on your feet.
  • Ongoing Learning - People at CapsLock are deeply inquisitive and eager to learn new knowledge and skills, that's why we support and create learning opportunities like the Free Books program, workshops, conferences, and more.
  • Home Office -We will cover the equipment and furniture expenses to make sure you have the best work-from-home experience.
  • Physical Well–Being - We will cover costs of your medical insurance. Additionally, we offer an allowance for a flexible fitness program.
  • Fun Stuff - There is never a shortage of fun stuff.

jobs.excerpt: Who WeAre At the birth of digital, Claravine noticed a persistent problem with data integrity.
jobs.description:
Who WeAre

At the birth of digital, Claravine noticed a persistent problem with data integrity. This discovery eventually led to a unique category solution that continues to redefine how top brands manage the digital experience. We are committed to helping our clients develop the data accuracy, depth, and consistency they need to deliver truly world-class digital experiences and marketing campaigns.

What We Do

At Claravine, we help large enterprises solve complex data consistency and accuracy problems. We do this through the Data Standards Cloud, a SaaS platform that enables customers to set their own data standards and gives their teams a way to validate their data.

Who You Are

You are a consultative technical advisor who makes Claravine work inside customers' real technology stacks and keeps it working as their businesses change. You see the gap between what a customer uses today and what they could be doing, and you can explain that gap to executives and operations teams alike.

As a Solutions Architect (SA), you will own the technical solution for a book of enterprise accounts, from discovery through a validated build.

This is an advisory role with hands-on build responsibility. You will be prescriptive about the decisions a customer needs to make, including the sequence, the trade-offs, and their technical consequences, and you will give a recommended starting point. The customer owns the final content of their taxonomy. You make sure they can make those decisions early, with confidence, and build something that lasts. You will work closely with Customer Success, our Forward-Deployed Product Managers, Enablement, Support, and Product.

What You'll Do

Design and deliver the right solution

  • Lead technical discovery: understand the customer's workflow from brief to reporting, what consumes Claravine data downstream, and what that system requires.
  • Solve the business requirement rather than the stated request, and have that conversation openly when the two differ.
  • Design solutions that the customer's own administrator can maintain and that survive their next reorganization.
  • Build to a high standard (structure, naming, testing, and documentation) and validate against real customer data before declaring a build complete.
  • Surface scope change, risk, and blockers early instead of absorbing them quietly.

Advise customers through the decisions that stall implementations

  • Guide customers through the taxonomy and governance decisions they need to settle (structure, granularity, ownership, approvals, and enforcement) using Claravine's decision guides and a recommended starting point.
  • Bring these decisions forward to kickoff and discovery, where they are cheap, rather than letting them block the build.
  • Challenge what customers bring instead of overlaying Claravine on top of a broken process, and identify the organizational problem when it is presented as a technical one.
  • Document the why behind every design decision as it is made.

jobs.description:
Lead Digital Forensics and Incident Response (DFIR) Engineer

Location: Remote (United States)
Reporting to: Director of Cybersecurity

At STN, we don't just adapt to the digital future, we engineer it. Our mission is to help organizations thrive in a rapidly evolving technology landscape through strategic insight, cutting-edge solutions, and a security-first mindset. We provide end-to-end services spanning cloud consulting, AI infrastructure, and enterprise security, enabling secure, scalable, and future-ready transformation.

As trusted advisors, we align IT investments with business outcomes that drive performance and growth, starting with deep strategic engagement and delivering tailored solutions built for long-term impact.

Our approach is innovation-led and rooted in cybersecurity, with a focus on leveraging the right technologies to solve real-world challenges. We invest in our people and foster a culture of growth, inclusion, and purpose because we believe empowered teams build transformative technology.

Overview
We are seeking a Lead Digital Forensics and Incident Response (DFIR) Engineer to independently investigate significant security incidents and guide technical response across customer and internal STN environments. The right person can preserve evidence, reconstruct attacker activity, establish defensible conclusions, direct containment and eradication recommendations, and communicate clearly under pressure.

Key Responsibilities

Digital Forensics & Incident Investigation
  • Lead investigations involving ransomware, endpoint compromise, credential abuse, unauthorized access, lateral movement, persistence, and suspected data exfiltration.
  • Acquire and analyze evidence from Windows and Linux hosts, endpoints, memory and disk images, network traffic, firewall logs, cloud audit sources, and identity telemetry.
  • Correlate EDR, SIEM, endpoint, network, authentication, and infrastructure data to build host-centric and cross-environment incident timelines.
  • Develop hypotheses, identify indicators and attacker techniques, assess confidence levels, and distinguish confirmed observations from investigative assumptions.
Threat Detection & Compromise Analysis
  • Investigate incidents across hybrid data-center environments, including Linux and Windows servers, virtualization infrastructure, network controls, and high-performance compute systems when within engagement scope.
  • Use Cortex XSIAM/XDR, SentinelOne, firewall and network telemetry, identity logs, and independent forensic tools to test hypotheses and validate the scope of compromise.
  • Preserve chain of custody, evidence integrity, analysis notes, and repeatable procedures appropriate to the engagement's legal and contractual requirements.
Incident Response & Stakeholder Communication
  • Advise customers and internal stakeholders on containment, credential rotation, recovery sequencing, monitoring, and remediation validation.
  • Produce technically rigorous reports, incident briefings, executive summaries, and prioritized lessons learned; lead customer-facing readouts.
Process Improvement & Cross-Functional Collaboration
  • Guide junior responders, improve forensic collection and analysis playbooks, and automate repetitive triage and evidence correlation tasks.
  • Partner with SOC, engineering, and security leadership on detection improvements, incident readiness assessments, and post-incident hardening.

Experience & Qualifications

Required
  • 7+ years in incident response, digital forensics, threat hunting, or related security operations, including independent leadership of serious incidents.
  • Deep Windows and Linux forensic knowledge, endpoint artifact interpretation, and understanding of attacker persistence, privilege escalation, and lateral movement.
  • Strong analysis across SIEM/EDR telemetry, network logs, identity events, and cloud or virtualized environments; ability to handle large datasets.
  • Experience with forensic collection and analysis tooling, incident timelines, integrity verification, and structured evidence management.
  • Strong customer-facing communication and judgment during evolving incidents, including the ability to document uncertainty clearly.
  • At least one recognized DFIR certification, such as GCFA, GCFE, GNFA, GREM, CFCE, or a comparable current forensic/incident-response credential.
Preferred
  • Experience responding to ransomware or high-impact Linux and virtualization incidents, including GPU/compute or data-center infrastructure.
  • Familiarity with Cortex XDR/XSIAM, SentinelOne, firewall telemetry, and cloud investigation workflows.
  • Python/PowerShell tooling, forensic automation, memory analysis, and development of customer incident response playbooks.

Compensation

  • Full-Time, Exempt
  • $145,000-$185,000/year, DOE

  • FSA Health and Dependent Care available
  • 401(k) Plan
  • Unlimited Paid Time Off (PTO)
  • Observed Holidays Paid
  • Cell Phone Allowance
  • Collaborative, growth-driven culture

jobs.title: [Contractor] Staff Software Engineer (AI-Native, Full-Stack)
jobs.excerpt: Cheesecake Labs is an AI, data, and product engineering partner for established and scaling organizations navigating legacy systems, fragmented data, AI pressure, or limited engineering capacity.
jobs.description:
Cheesecake Labs is an AI, data, and product engineering partner for established and scaling organizations navigating legacy systems, fragmented data, AI pressure, or limited engineering capacity.

Our services include AI Implementation, Application Modernization, Data & Analytics, Product Engineering, AI-Accelerated Delivery, and Embedded Engineering Teams. We deliver agentic workflows in 8-12 weeks and modernize applications in 5-10 months rather than 2 years. We also build trusted data foundations and digital products designed to scale. Our agentic software development lifecycle accelerates execution, while experienced engineers embed with client teams to provide technical depth, security, and clear ownership.

Member of Anthropic's Claude Partner Network; technology partners include Databricks, Snowflake, dbt, and AWS.

Across 13+ years, Cheesecake Labs has built 300+ products for clients including Eurasia Group, MoneyGram, the World Bank, Stellar, Wedgewood, PepsiCo, Merck, Sodexo, and Mercado Libre.

The story behind this role

Many AI engineering roles are still built around experiments, isolated prototypes, or research. This is not one of them.

At Cheesecake Labs, we build software and AI-powered solutions for real businesses, with real users, real constraints, and real deadlines. Our squads are small and senior, and they ship in weeks and months, not years.

Today, AI agents write most of our code. This role is for the engineer who decides how things get built, directs the agents, verifies the result, and answers for it in front of the client. At Staff level, that also means deciding how the squads around you specify, build, and verify.

We are looking for a Staff Software Engineer: someone who owns the technical outcome of a project or account, and whose impact reaches beyond their own code. You set how work is specified and verified, shape architecture across projects, and evolve the harness that every squad uses. Where the project has a PM, product direction sits with them and you are their technical counterpart. Where it doesn’t, you take the problem from the founder or client yourself.

Engagement details

  • Contractor / project-based engagement
  • Paid in USD
  • Remote-first
  • Flexible allocation depending on project availability and fit
  • Opportunities may vary in duration, scope, and weekly commitment depending on client needs

Some opportunities may start immediately.
Others may become active as new projects enter our pipeline.

What this role actually looks like

This is not a “receive tickets and implement features” role. It is not a “write every line yourself” role either. It is also not a role where you only advise from the side: you stay close to real delivery.

On a typical project, you might:

  • Set how the project specifies work: spec templates, how deep each type of change needs to go, and what a good spec looks like for the client’s domain. Turn recurring review comments into checklists the whole squad uses.
  • Run CKL Spec Driven, our spec-driven development flow, and turn a client’s business problem into a technical design and a spec that an AI agent can execute and you can verify.
  • Design how the project verifies output: what automation checks, what needs human eyes, and which changes always get a second human reviewer, such as auth, payments, and data migrations. Set up automated review and quality gates in the first week of a new project.
  • Direct AI agents (Claude Code, Cursor, or similar) to implement against your spec. Writing code by hand is the exception, not the default.
  • Review what the agents produce, using automated review loops plus your own check of architecture and behavior. You answer for 100% of what ships and can explain every decision in it.
  • Make the architecture decisions across a project or several, and write them down so people and agents can follow them. See where the system will hurt in 6 to 12 months.
  • Lead technical assessments, such as taking over an existing project, and give the Engineering Manager the risk list before kickoff.
  • Be the technical reference when a squad hits a harder area, such as blockchain, DevOps, or data and AI.
  • Own the technical outcome of the project or account. Raise risks to the Engineering Manager early, with options attached, for example when the scope won’t fit the budget.
  • Arrive at client conversations with a recommendation and the technical authority to defend it. Handle the pushback, and when the client makes the call, execute it well. Join pre-sales conversations when technical credibility matters, and bring the opportunities you spot to the Engineering Manager.
  • Evolve the shared harness (skills, agents, and review loops) for the whole company: turn patterns you see across projects into skills, publish them, and teach others how to use them.
  • Mentor Senior and other engineers, and pair with someone who is struggling when the Engineering Manager asks.
  • Keep your own work tested and visible: check it in staging before saying “done”, post short written updates without being asked, and raise blockers the day they appear.
  • Ship and iterate, then close the loop by feeding decisions and edge cases back into the project’s context, so the next spec starts smarter.
  • Work within each client’s rules on AI use (see How we use AI here).

Some projects are heavy on architecture. Others are heavy on client conversations. Most mix both. You work with a lot of autonomy, with an Engineering Manager behind you and squads that count on you.

What tends to work well here

People who thrive in this role usually:

  • Have built and shipped real software products end-to-end, and can walk us through the decisions they made, including architecture that held up in production and after the team changed.
  • Already use AI agents daily to design, build, debug, and research, and can show what they built.
  • Think in specs: they turn ambiguity into structured, testable definitions, and can set the standard for how others write them.
  • Have a full-stack mindset and experience across more than one stack. You may be strongest in one layer (backend, frontend, mobile, or AI), but you think about the product as a whole and move across layers when the project needs it.
  • Have raised the level of the people around them, through mentoring, review culture, or tools and standards that other engineers adopted.
  • Have been the technical voice in front of a client: they recommend, defend the recommendation, and still execute the client’s decision.
  • Test what they build before saying “done”, and state clearly what was and wasn’t verified.
  • Surface problems early, with options attached, and share what they learn with the team.
  • Think critically: they question the request, see how a change affects the rest of the system, and bring a recommendation, not only the problem.
  • Work fluently in English with clients and stakeholders (calls, discussions, async), advanced level or above.
  • Operate well with high autonomy, low bureaucracy, and fast feedback loops in a 100% remote setup, knowing when a conversation needs to be live and when async works, and communicating well in both.

This probably won’t be your thing if

Just to be transparent:

  • You need detailed requirements or constant direction before getting started.
  • You see AI as a side tool, or you prefer writing most of the code by hand.
  • You are comfortable shipping AI output you haven’t verified.
  • You prefer to keep your impact to your own tasks and your own code.
  • You prefer roles focused only on implementation, without client or business conversations.
  • You are uncomfortable talking directly to clients or working through ambiguous problems.
  • You find it hard to execute the client’s decision after you have made your recommendation.
  • You tend to go quiet between kickoff and delivery, or wait to be asked for an update.
  • You expect the PM or anyone else to test what you built.
  • You prefer stable priorities over fast iteration and high ownership.

There’s nothing wrong with any of that. It’s just not how we operate.

One last thing

To participate in this selection process, you must:

  • Have a valid business registration in your country (CNPJ, VAT, EIN, or equivalent)
  • Have a bank account eligible to receive USD payments
  • Be able to issue invoices accordingly

These requirements are necessary for contractor engagement and payment processing.

Not sure if you check every box?

That’s okay.

We know that many great people — especially from underrepresented groups — hesitate to apply unless they meet 100% of the requirements.

If this opportunity sounds interesting, we’d still love to hear from you.

IMPORTANT TIP -> The communication during the selection process is done by email. We suggest that you keep an eye on your email inboxes and set the permission to receive messages from @cheesecakelabs.hire.trakstar.com so our messages will not be directed to the spam box ;)

How we use AI here

At Cheesecake Labs, AI agents do most of the execution: code, infrastructure, data models, research, prototypes, and documentation. People make the decisions: what gets built and in what order, the architecture, team allocation, and anything about people. Every role here specifies, directs AI, verifies the result, and answers for what ships.

On every project, we also follow a few rules:

  • Use only approved tools, through Cheesecake Labs company accounts
  • Follow each client’s rules on AI. Some clients require a specific AI stack, and highly regulated markets (such as banking in Brazil) may require models hosted in-country
  • Never put client data or personal data (names, birth dates, emails) into an LLM without anonymizing it first. The same goes for our own people’s data
  • Comply with LGPD and other applicable data-protection laws

The collected personal data will be used only to manage and control candidate resumes in order to assess the necessary requirements such as the contact information, and also to conduct this selection process.

The collected data will not be shared with others (“third parties”) without your authorization, and their use will be restricted to Cheesecake Labs internal staff, and also to the service providers that process your data for the selection process. At any time, you can contact us and we will remove your data from our data collection system. In order to do that, just simply send an email to .

About us:

Jerry.ai is a Series C, YC-backed tech startup with 5M+ customers and $240M in funding. Founded in 2017, product launched in 2019, and achieved profitability in 2024.

Why we exist:

Your car, home, and motorcycle aren't just purchases, they're the physical embodiment of the life you've worked hard to build. Yet the experience of owning them is stuck in the 90s. Every step of the journey — buying, insuring, maintaining, repairing, selling — is fragmented, complicated, and expensive.

Imagine having a trusted friend in your pocket who takes care of everything: they find you the right car or home at the right price, lock in the best insurance rate without you lifting a finger, remind you before that service appointment turns into an expensive repair, and help you sell at the best price when the time is right. That friend is Jerry.

We are building the first AI-powered advisor to manage all your physical assets. We started with your car in 2019, now we’re expanding into new verticals (e.g. home, motorcycle, RV, boat).

Why We’re Hiring

Our BizOps & Analytics team has been a force multiplier and accelerant to our business that has helped us reach these pivotal milestones in spite of headwinds and within a highly competitive market. They are a team of former McKinsey, BCG and Bain consultants who drive data & insights, and inform decision-making across every corner of our business. They are analytical powerhouses and first principles problem solvers who push forward our most important initiatives across product, growth, tech, and operations.

Every business unit has a BizOps team member embedded within it — someone who doesn't just run analyses and build dashboards, but shapes what questions we should ask, what data to pull, what conclusions to draw, what decisions to make, and then drives our teams towards our next goal: go from 5M to 50M customers and become a $10B business in the next 4 years.

As our business continues to expand, there is growing demand for more BizOps team members. We are hiring 4-6 people to drive impact in these areas:

  • Growth Marketing

  • Product Development

  • AI & Automation

  • Strategic Partnerships

On leveling: You may see job ads for this role at different job levels. Our priority is finding the right people, we can be flexible with job title/leveling.

Why You Will (Or Won't) Like Working Here

  • No slides: If you've worked in consulting, you know what it feels like to be up at 3am reformatting a deck. That doesn't exist here. The only work that gets done at Jerry is work that will materially change the trajectory of our business — an important product, a new growth channel, a key metric, a critical partner relationship, etc.

  • No corporate fluff: The BizOps & Analytics team is 14 insatiable learners who care deeply about solving difficult problems and making a tangible impact. Every person owns a critical domain. There is no bloat, unnecessary meetings, or waiting for approvals.

  • Hands-on: This is not a pure strategy role, you will also own execution. Your day-to-day will be surfacing analytical insights, driving decisions, and seeing them through end-to-end.

What You'll Own

You'll sit on our central BizOps & Analytics team but you’ll be embedded in one of Jerry's core business areas — growth, product, AI and automation, strategic partnerships — and own the analytical function for that business unit end-to-end.

  • Define the right problems: Before any analysis, understand what business question it's answering and what decision it will inform. Push back if the question is flawed.

  • Data and insights: Define metrics, build reports, run analyses, design experiments, and surface data insights that move your team's key metrics.

  • Drive outcomes: Bring recommendations to your counterparts in product, growth, finance or operations, tell them what's happening and why, and what next steps should be.

Who You Are

  • First principles thinker: You break ambiguous problems into clear hypotheses before touching data. You're analytically strong (comfortable with Excel, SQL or Python) but your instinct is to ask "what are we trying to solve here?" before jumping to "what should I build?"

  • Direct communicator: You can walk a skeptical stakeholder through a complex finding and get buy-in quickly. You write clearly, speak precisely, and don't bury the lede.

  • Owner: You act like your name is on the door. If something is broken, you feel responsible for fixing it, even if it’s outside of your swim lane.

What You'll Bring

  • 6+ years of experience at a consulting firm, investment bank, or high-growth technology company.

  • Strong analytical skills; ability to pull, structure, and interpret data independently.

  • Track record of owning ambiguous problems and delivering impact.

  • Clear, persuasive communicator who can influence decisions at the leadership level.

Our Tools

SQL (Clickhouse), Metabase, Python, Jupyter Hub, GitHub.

JumpCloud® is the AI-powered unified IT management platform designed to secure the modern workforce. JumpCloud is Intelligent, Secure IT.

About the Role:

Identity is the new security perimeter, and JumpCloud’s Access & Authentication team owns it.

With remote work and the domainless enterprise here to stay, every login is now a security decision. Our products decide who gets access to what across devices, SSO apps, servers, RADIUS and LDAP. They power MFA, passwordless, and Zero Trust conditional access built on identity, location, risk, and certificate-based device trust.

As a Senior PM, you’ll define how millions of users prove who they are. You’ll balance two customers: IT admins who need control, and users who just want to get to work. And you’ll shape the strategy for our platform in a market being redefined right now. If you want to prove security and simplicity aren’t a tradeoff, join us.

About SuiteOp

Hospitality is one of the most human businesses in the world, and one of the hardest to run. Behind every great stay is someone who answered a guest at midnight, a cleaner who turned a home in two hours, and an operator holding it all together with spreadsheets and group chats.

We started SuiteOp because we've been those operators. Our founders ran rentals before they built software for them, and that's still how we build: we sit with operators, watch where their day breaks, and fix it.

Today more than 30,000 units run on SuiteOp, across short-term rentals and boutique hotels. With SuiteOp V2, AI agents take on the repetitive work, from guest messages to turnovers, so operators and their teams can get back to the part that matters: hospitality.

We're a small team (seed stage, $3M+ raised), headquartered in New York with customers around the world. We care deeply about the craft. We sweat the details operators feel every day, we ship fast, and we use AI in everything we do because it lets a small team build something great.

About the role

Be SuiteOp's first person in Latin America. Vacation rentals are booming across South America, and most operators still run on spreadsheets and WhatsApp. You'll open the market for us, starting the conversations in Spanish (and Portuguese) that turn operators into SuiteOp customers.

You'll own the top of the funnel: find the right operators, reach them by phone, email, and LinkedIn, and book qualified meetings for our Account Executives. The phone is where you shine. Operators don't buy from bots. They buy from people who understand their business and ask sharp questions.

You'll work side by side with our Account Executives and sales leadership, and what you hear from operators will shape our messaging and our product.

What you'll do

  • Make 100+ outbound dials a day to Latin American operators managing anywhere from 10 to 1,000+ units
  • Book qualified demos for our Account Executives, with clear handoff notes
  • Run multi-touch outreach across phone, email, and LinkedIn, in Spanish (and Portuguese for Brazil), personalized for every operator
  • Research every account and prep every call, so you can hold a real conversation without a script
  • Keep HubSpot clean: every call, every note, every next step
  • Bring back what you hear from operators: what's landing, what's not, and why
  • Help build the outbound playbook for Latin America, from target lists to talk tracks

AI is how we work

Our reps run on Claude. It isn't a trend for us. It gives every rep hours back each week to spend on the phone instead of on busywork. We're looking for someone who already works this way and loves it.

  • You build your own AI workflows and agents for research and call prep, and you can't wait to walk us through one you're proud of
  • You use AI to understand each operator more deeply, not to send more generic emails
  • You know when to put the tools down and pick up the phone
  • Bonus: you've built with Claude Code, Clay, n8n, or similar tools

What you bring

  • You love the phone, and a hard no rolls right off you
  • You're competitive, coachable, and hungry to grow
