jobs.description:
About QC Servion

QC Servion is the strategic operational hub of the QC Ecosystem, an integrated network of six specialized companies spanning the full data center lifecycle, from concept and engineering through infrastructure development, construction, commissioning, and delivery.

Together, DLB Associates, Galtra Solutions, AI2IO, Fluid2Chip, CEQEL Critical Commissioning, and 2AI-DC Integrators deliver comprehensive solutions for hyperscale, AI, and mission-critical data center infrastructure.

QC Servion connects and enables these businesses through centralized people, operational, and business strategies that support growth and execution across the ecosystem.

Position: Talent Acquisition Partner

Position Location: Remote - work virtually from anywhere in the United States

Salary

QC Servion recognizes salary ranges from job boards do not necessarily reflect our pay ranges. In many instances we out-compete those ranges for well-qualified candidates.

Job Summary

The Talent Acquisition Partner helps build the teams behind some of the fastest-growing businesses across the QC Ecosystem.

You may be recruiting an engineer, commissioning professional, or technical field hire one week and supporting a project management, accounting, marketing, operations, or completely new position the next. While this role will sit within our overhead/shared-services organization, your recruiting portfolio will evolve based on where the business needs support most.

You don't need to come in having recruited every role we hire for. We're looking for someone who is curious, scrappy, resourceful, and comfortable figuring things out. When you're handed an unfamiliar position, we want your instinct to be to ask questions, learn the business, understand what good looks like, dig into the talent market, and build a search strategy.

You'll own the recruiting lifecycle for the teams you support, partnering directly with hiring managers to define what they need, find and assess talent, manage interviews, navigate offers, and keep searches moving. As you build relationships and learn your teams, you'll have the opportunity to become their go-to Talent Acquisition partner and take real ownership of how you support their growth.

This is a great opportunity for someone who likes variety, moves quickly, doesn't need every step mapped out, and wants room to grow alongside an organization that is continuing to evolve.

Essential Functions

  • Own full-cycle recruiting across technical, field-based, project, operational, and corporate/shared-services positions based on evolving business needs.
  • Manage multiple active requisitions simultaneously while understanding which searches and business needs require the most attention.
  • Lead intake and calibration conversations with hiring managers to understand the role, team, business need, candidate profile, level, and interview expectations.
  • Learn unfamiliar roles and functions quickly enough to confidently source, screen, and speak with candidates about the opportunity.
  • Develop targeted search strategies using LinkedIn Recruiter, job boards, referrals, internal databases, direct outreach, specialized communities, and other creative sourcing channels.
  • Build pipelines of active and passive candidates rather than relying solely on inbound applicants.
  • Conduct recruiter screens focused on experience, capabilities, communication, career motivations, compensation expectations, and overall alignment with the opportunity.
  • Partner closely with hiring managers throughout the search, providing visibility into pipeline health, candidate feedback, market conditions, compensation expectations, and potential challenges.
  • Recognize when a search isn't producing the right results and use market feedback to recommend changes to the candidate profile, sourcing strategy, level, compensation, or other search parameters.
  • Coordinate interviews and proactively manage scheduling, feedback, and next steps so searches continue moving forward.
  • Maintain thoughtful and consistent communication with candidates throughout the process, including searches with longer or evolving timelines.
  • Gather and synthesize interviewer feedback and help hiring teams reach timely, informed decisions.
  • Manage the offer process from compensation alignment and verbal offer through formal documentation, negotiation, acceptance, and pre-employment handoff.
  • Maintain accurate and current information within the ATS so hiring teams and leadership have clear visibility into recruiting activity and pipeline status.
  • Use recruiting data and market insight to identify bottlenecks, adjust strategies, and improve hiring outcomes.
  • Leverage AI, automation, sourcing technology, and emerging tools to improve research, sourcing, communication, and day-to-day recruiting efficiency.

What Success Looks Like

  • The hiring managers you support view you as their Talent Acquisition partner, not simply someone managing requisitions.
  • You understand your teams well enough to represent their opportunities confidently and provide informed guidance throughout a search.
  • You're comfortable picking up a role you've never recruited before, asking the right questions, and figuring out how to find the talent.
  • You proactively build pipelines rather than waiting for applicants to come to you.
  • Hiring managers have clear visibility into their searches and know what is working, what isn't, and what you recommend doing next.
  • You keep interviews, feedback, decisions, and offers moving without needing someone else to continuously push the process forward.
  • Candidates receive timely, honest, and thoughtful communication throughout their experience.
  • You can move between very different roles, functions, and talent markets based on where the organization needs you.
  • You develop trusted relationships with the leaders and teams you support.
  • As your knowledge and credibility grow, you take greater ownership of your recruiting relationships and increasingly complex hiring needs.

Position Requirements

  • Bachelor's degree in Human Resources, Business, Communications, or a related field or equivalent professional experience in recruiting, sourcing, staffing, HR, or another relevant people-focused field.
  • 3+ years of recruiting, sourcing, staffing, or Talent Acquisition experience preferred, with demonstrated ability to independently manage searches and candidate relationships.
  • Experience recruiting technical, engineering, construction, field-based, professional-services, project-based, or corporate talent is helpful; the ability to quickly learn unfamiliar roles and talent markets is equally important.
  • Demonstrated ability to proactively identify and engage passive candidates through LinkedIn Recruiter, targeted outreach, referrals, job boards, databases, and other sourcing methods.
  • Strong interviewing and candidate-assessment skills with the ability to evaluate experience, transferable capabilities, motivations, communication, and overall alignment.
  • Comfortable partnering directly with hiring managers and asking thoughtful questions when hiring requirements are unclear or still evolving.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills with the ability to build credibility with candidates, hiring managers, and internal stakeholders.
  • Highly organized with strong follow-through and the ability to manage multiple searches, deadlines, candidate conversations, and shifting priorities.
  • Comfortable operating independently, exercising judgment, and moving work forward without having every step mapped out.
  • Experience working within an applicant tracking system; Rippling ATS experience is a plus.
  • Familiarity with LinkedIn Recruiter and other sourcing and recruiting technologies.
  • Comfortable using AI, automation, and emerging technology to improve productivity and recruiting effectiveness.

How You'll Work

We're less concerned with whether you've recruited every role on our org chart and more interested in how you approach something you haven't seen before. You'll probably enjoy this environment if you:

  • Ask good questions and learn quickly.
  • Aren't intimidated by unfamiliar or highly technical positions.
  • Will dig into competitors, adjacent industries, LinkedIn, referrals, and new sourcing channels until you figure out where the talent is.
  • Don't need a perfectly written job description or step-by-step instructions before getting started.
  • Know when to ask for help but are willing to try solving the problem first.
  • Adjust quickly when a search or hiring priority changes.
  • Communicate directly and consistently with candidates and hiring managers.
  • Bring recommendations when something isn't working rather than simply reporting the problem.
  • Build genuine relationships with the teams you support.
  • Are willing to jump in when the business needs help.
  • Want more ownership as you demonstrate you're ready for it.

Why QC Servion

  • The variety and growth here are a big part of the opportunity.
  • You won't be locked into one job family or spend every day recruiting the same profile. While you'll sit within our overhead/shared-services organization, your recruiting portfolio can flex across businesses and functions based on where support is needed.
  • As you work with those teams, you'll have the opportunity to become genuinely embedded in their hiring. You'll learn what they do, understand what makes someone successful there, build relationships with their leaders, and become someone they trust to help them make good talent decisions.
  • And because we're growing, your own path doesn't have to be completely defined on day one. As you demonstrate what you're good at, there may be opportunities to support new teams, take on harder searches, deepen your expertise, expand your relationships across the organization, or grow your responsibilities naturally with the business.
  • You don't need to arrive knowing everything.
  • You do need to be willing to jump in, learn quickly, build trust, and make the role your own.

Physical Demands

The following physical demands must be met by the employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions. While performing the duties of this job, the employee is:

  • Frequently required to remain in a stationary position.
  • Frequently moving through home office.
  • May occasionally lift up to 20 pounds.

Travel Requirements

  • Up to 5%, this may include travel to any or all 50 US states.
  • Travel is defined as physically leaving home on behalf of business activities including but not limited to client sites, meetings with other employees, meeting for business development purposes, running errands on behalf of the business, attending industry conferences, etc.

Benefits

  • Choice of comprehensive medical plans (including two PPO-style plans and a HDHP w/ HSA option).
  • Flex spending accounts (FSA).
  • Dental and vision plans.
  • Comprehensive medical, dental and vision benefits extended to spouse / domestic partner and dependent children up to age 26.
  • 401k with company match and self-directed brokerage account option.
  • PTO including additional paid time off during the last week of the year.
  • Company paid life insurance coverage for employees and their eligible dependents.
  • Short and long-term disability, AD&D coverage.
  • Professional development opportunities, tuition reimbursement, and professional licensing assistance.
  • Paid parental leave after one year of employment.

CO, CA, IL, NY, WA, and Washington DC residents only: In accordance with CO, CA, IL, NY, WA, and Washington DC law, the range provided is QC Servion's reasonable estimate of the base compensation for this role. The actual amount may differ based on non-discriminatory factors such as experience, knowledge, skills, abilities, and location.

EEO

QC Servion provides equal employment opportunities (EEO) to all employees and applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, genetics, sexual orientation, gender identity, or gender expression. We are committed to a diverse and inclusive workforce and welcome people from all backgrounds, experiences, perspectives, and abilities.

Notice To Third Party Agencies
QC Servion does not accept unsolicited resumes from recruiters, employment agencies, or other staffing services. Unsolicited resumes include any resume or hiring document sent to QC Servion in the absence of a signed Service Agreement where QC Servion has expressly requested recruitment/staffing services specific to the position at hand. Working closely with the CEO and senior leaders across policy and advocacy, membership, programs and business lines, you will bring communications judgment to organizational decisions and equip your team and colleagues to deliver a clear, coordinated narrative. You will remain directly engaged in executive counsel and the highest-stakes communications, including writing and refining key messages when your judgment is needed.

About the National Council

The National Council for Mental Wellbeing’s vision is to make mental wellbeing, including recovery from substance use challenges, a reality for everyone.

Founded in 1969, the National Council is a membership organization that drives policy and social change on behalf of 3,000 mental health and substance use organizations and the more than 15 million children, adults and families they serve. We advocate for equitable access to high-quality care, build our members’ capacity and promote mental wellbeing as a core part of health. Through Mental Health First Aid, we have trained more than 5 million people in the United States.

With a $76 million budget and more than 225 staff members, the National Council combines a national advocacy platform with programs and services that help communities meet growing needs.

What you will lead

A cohesive, national brand, voice and platform

  • Set and lead an enterprise communications strategy aligned with the National Council’s mission and priorities. Define priority audiences, annual objectives and the communications initiatives that will have the greatest impact.

  • Shape a compelling, consistent narrative that reflects the experiences of members and the people and communities they serve.

  • Set the strategy for the CEO’s national platform and lead the Strategic Comms and PR team to deliver through earned media, speaking opportunities, opinion pieces and other thought leadership. Position other leaders and experts as trusted voices in their areas of expertise.

  • Direct the team’s media engagement and preparation of leaders for interviews, public appearances and major announcements. Personally cultivate key national and trade media relationships and lead preparation for the most consequential engagements.

  • Serve as a spokesperson when appropriate and advise leaders on positioning, reputation and sensitive issues.

Communications that mobilize

  • Agree communications priorities and campaign objectives with policy and advocacy leaders, then direct the team’s delivery of clear messages and meaningful opportunities for members and partners to act.

  • Bring research, member experience and practical expertise into communications that demonstrate what is at stake and what change can make possible.

  • Lead the organization’s approach to messaging policy developments and public events, advising when and how the organization should respond. Direct timely, accurate execution and bring senior judgment to sensitive or fast-moving issues.

  • Work with membership, program, product and growth marketing colleagues to agree campaign goals and hold the communications function accountable for its contribution in connecting audiences with the National Council’s resources, training, products and services, including Mental Health First Aid. Use audience insights and results to refine priorities and investment.

An integrated, trusted communications, marketing and events function

  • Set brand standards and messaging and editorial direction across executive communications, media, National Council’s Web site and other digital channels and major initiatives. Establish guidelines and approval responsibilities that enable the team to deliver effectively, with your direct review of high-stakes communications.

  • Partner with colleagues responsible for marketing and events to use campaigns, convenings and other platforms to advance thought leadership, member engagement and mission impact.

  • Lead crisis communications planning and response, establish clear decision and escalation protocols, and advise the CEO and senior leadership on emerging issues and reputational risks.

  • Partner with organizational leaders on internal communications so staff understand major priorities, decisions and changes and can connect their work to the broader mission.

A strong team and effective partnerships

  • Lead, coach and develop a high-performing, future-forward communications and events team. Delegate clear ownership and decision-making, strengthen leadership capacity, and hold people accountable for quality, collaboration, efficiency and results.

  • Lead a culture of building trusted partnerships across the organization, ensure communications informs major initiatives from the outset, and resolve competing communications demands with senior colleagues.

  • Lead the National Council’s communications and mobilization in response to policy developments and public events. Advise senior leaders on when and how to respond, and direct timely, accurate messaging and coordinated action, bringing sound judgment to sensitive or fast-moving issues.

  • Review progress with senior leadership across national visibility, audience engagement, member participation, advocacy activity and connections to relevant programs and services, and refine the approach as priorities evolve.

What success will look like

In your first year, success will include:

  • A shared national narrative and messaging framework, with an agreed communications plan and priorities.

  • A focused thought leadership platform for the CEO, supported by a sustained pipeline of relevant media and speaking opportunities.

  • Coordinated communications campaigns that advance policy and advocacy priorities and connect audiences with useful programs and services.

  • A team with clear ownership, effective delegation and strong collaboration across policy, membership, marketing and programs, with communications engaged early in important work.

  • Regular review with senior leadership of progress in national visibility, stakeholder engagement and member participation.

What you bring

We recognize that there are many ways to build relevant expertise. We encourage you to apply if you can demonstrate most of the following:

  • At least 12 years of progressively responsible experience in communications, public affairs or related fields, including at least seven years leading multidisciplinary teams and senior managers.

  • A record of shaping public understanding of complex or contested issues from a national or statewide platform.

  • Experience building a consistent brand and message across channels, working effectively with marketing and events teams, and using data to connect communications activity to organizational results.

  • Strong media relationships and the skill, judgment and credibility to serve as a spokesperson.

  • Experience advising a CEO and senior leaders on communications strategy, public positioning, reputation and sensitive issues.

  • Excellent writing and editorial judgment, including the ability to turn complex policy, research and organizational priorities into clear, persuasive communications.

  • Deep experience in executive communications, policy communications, crisis communications and rapid response.

  • A collaborative, accountable leadership style, with a demonstrated ability to build trust, develop people, engage in productive debate, and align colleagues across functions around shared goals and results.

We would particularly value experience in a national association, membership or advocacy organization, Congress, an administration or a national campaign; experience in healthcare, behavioral health or another mission-driven setting; and experience guiding communications through organizational change. A master’s degree in a relevant field is also valued.

Compensation and benefits

The proposed salary range for this position is $250,000–$275,000, based on experience, education and internal equity.

Benefits include medical, dental, vision, life and disability insurance; a 403(b) retirement plan with employer contributions after one year of service; paid vacation, sick, personal, floating holiday, bereavement and federal holidays; parental support, including adoption, fertility and surrogacy reimbursement and two weeks of paid parental leave; professional development and tuition reimbursement funds; and Calm Premium access.

Equal opportunity and accessibility

The National Council is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. We welcome people of all races, ethnicities, religions, genders, sexual orientations and ages, as well as veterans, people with disabilities and those with lived experience of mental health and substance use challenges.

jobs.excerpt: Consultant Role Content Expert - AI Evaluation, Agricultural Content, Research & MEL Engagement Period Six months, with possibility of extension Location Nigeria / Remote, with field participation as specifically authorized About Digital Green Digital Green is a global non-profit that has spent nearly two decades helping smallholder farmers build more prosperous, resilient livelihoods—reaching over 10 million farmers to date.
jobs.description:
Consultant Role

Content Expert - AI Evaluation, Agricultural Content, Research & MEL

Engagement Period

Six months, with possibility of extension

Location

Nigeria / Remote, with field participation as specifically authorized

About Digital Green

Digital Green is a global non-profit that has spent nearly two decades helping smallholder farmers build more prosperous, resilient livelihoods—reaching over 10 million farmers to date. Our flagship product, FarmerChat, is a multilingual AI-powered advisory platform that gives farmers timely, locally relevant guidance—from climate-resilient practices to pest management, input use, and market access—in the language and format that works for them. Today FarmerChat reaches farmers across India, Kenya, Ethiopia, Nigeria, and Brazil, with millions of questions asked and answered in over 15 local languages. We combine deep, on-the-ground agricultural extension experience with modern AI to meet farmers where they are, and help them make better decisions, faster.

1. Background

Role Summary

We are seeking an experienced Nigeria-based agricultural content expert who can support AI response validation, agricultural content and terminology review, and research, product testing, and field/program activities. The ideal candidate combines strong local crop and/or livestock knowledge with the ability to review information carefully, communicate clear recommendations, and collaborate with remote and field teams. Assignments across the three workstreams will vary based on program needs.

Digital Green is enhancing its AI-driven agricultural advisory systems, including FarmerChat, by improving the agronomic accuracy, contextual relevance, localized applicability, usability, and safety of AI-generated responses and farmer-facing agricultural content.

The Consultant will serve as an independent Content Expert with the expertise to support all three core workstreams:

  • Workstream A: Reviewing and Checking the Quality of AI-Generated Agricultural Advice
  • Workstream B: Developing and Reviewing Agricultural Content, Crop Calendars, and Local Terminology
  • Workstream C: Ad hoc support—Research, Monitoring, Evaluation & Learning (MEL), Product Testing, and Program Support

Actual assignments will depend on the Consultant's capabilities and Digital Green's needs. All assignments must be agreed upon in writing with Digital Green's designated Technical Lead before work begins. The scope, volume, timing, and cadence of work will be determined for each assignment. Work under any particular workstream is not guaranteed.

2. Workstream A - Reviewing and Checking the Quality of AI-Generated Agricultural Advice

The Consultant shall perform independent quality validation of agricultural Q&A pairs and AI-generated outputs that have undergone first-level expert review.

  • Independently review outputs assessed by Content Expert Reviewers.
  • Verify whether reviewer assessments and corrections meet Digital Green's quality standards for agronomic and technical accuracy, relevance, completeness, clarity, local agricultural context, farmer usability, safety, and appropriateness.
  • Validate assigned evaluation formats, including text, image, MCQ, and other formats specifically assigned by Digital Green.
  • Confirm, correct, or reject reviewer assessments where appropriate.
  • Identify inconsistencies, reviewer errors, model hallucinations, recurring quality issues, and systemic patterns.
  • Provide corrective feedback to improve reviewer consistency and overall evaluation quality.
  • Support the development and maintenance of reliable Golden Q&A datasets, evaluation benchmarks, and model-quality datasets.
  • Record and submit final validation decisions through Digital Green's designated platform, spreadsheet, dashboard, or other approved workflow.

3. Workstream B - Developing and Reviewing Agricultural Content, Crop Calendars, and Local Terminology

Upon written assignment from Digital Green, the Service Provider may:

  • Perform technical, agronomic, and localized review of agricultural Content Cards.
  • Review AI-generated or manually drafted agricultural advisory content and provide technical corrections, edits, recommendations, and supporting references or citations where required.
  • Develop, adapt, update, or review crop calendars and seasonal advisory workflows.
  • Tailor agricultural content to relevant crops, livestock systems, agro-ecological zones, local seasons, farming systems, and agricultural practices.
  • Develop, review, validate, and map locally relevant agricultural terminology, including terminology related to crops, livestock, pests and diseases, agricultural inputs, agronomic practices, measurements, and other domain-specific concepts.
  • Support development and improvement of agricultural glossaries, terminology datasets, taxonomies, thesauri, and structured agricultural knowledge resources.
  • Undertake other agricultural content and knowledge activities as specifically authorized.

4. Workstream C - Supporting Agricultural Research, Farmer Feedback, Field Activities, and Product Testing

  • Review agricultural research reports, data, and farmer feedback to ensure the information is accurate and relevant to local farming practices.
  • Support monitoring and evaluation activities, including reviewing farmer surveys, field observations, and program results.
  • Provide technical input for agricultural research, field studies, and program activities.
  • Test FarmerChat and its new features to check the accuracy, usefulness, and clarity of agricultural advice.
  • Identify issues in agricultural content or product performance and suggest improvements.
  • Support field activities, pilot programs, and farmer feedback sessions, including coordination, documentation, and sharing observations.
  • Participate in partner discussions, technical workshops, training sessions, and program meetings as required.
  • Prepare brief reports, summaries, and recommendations based on research findings, field activities, and program needs.

Participation in technical workshops, training activities, stakeholder working groups, or other external engagements must be assigned and approved in writing by Digital Green in advance. The Consultant may not represent or speak on behalf of Digital Green without express written authorization and must immediately notify Digital Green of any external requests concerning FarmerChat or other Digital Green products or activities before accepting or responding substantively.

5. Work Authorization and No Minimum Commitment

The Consultant shall perform Services only as expressly authorized by Digital Green through this SOW, a written task order, assignment, email instruction, or other written authorization from Digital Green's designated Technical Lead. Any estimated volumes, hours, workload, frequency, or timing are non-binding planning estimates only and do not create a guaranteed minimum commitment.

The Consultant shall not exceed authorized work or level of effort, incur expenses, or undertake additional activities outside the approved scope without prior written approval from Digital Green.

6. Quality Review and Acceptance

Digital Green may return deliverables for correction if they are incomplete, inaccurate, technically incorrect, inconsistent with applicable guidelines, or otherwise fail to meet required quality standards. Reasonable corrections associated with the original assignment shall be completed as part of that assignment.

7. Progress Updates and Communication

  • Participate in alignment and calibration meetings as reasonably requested.
  • Maintain accurate records of completed units and hours.
  • Provide progress updates when requested by the Technical Lead.
  • Submit deliverables through Digital Green's designated platform, spreadsheet, dashboard, or other approved workflow.

8. Minimum Qualifications

Education: Advanced degree in Agriculture, Agronomy, Agricultural Extension, Veterinary Sciences, Horticulture, or a related discipline, or equivalent demonstrated professional expertise.

Experience: Minimum of five years of relevant experience in agricultural advisory services, extension, research, veterinary/agronomic services, agricultural content development, or related technical work.

Technical Expertise: Strong understanding of smallholder farming systems, localized agricultural practices, crop and/or livestock management, and farmer advisory workflows.

Preferred: Experience with digital agriculture, AI-assisted advisory systems, human-in-the-loop AI evaluation, RLHF, agricultural content development, quality validation, or digital product testing.

This role is open to fully remote candidates in the United States, with a preference for the Eastern time zone. Some travel to client sites will be required.

What you'll do

    Client Leadership

  • Serve as the senior day-to-day partner for your clients, building trusted, long-term relationships at the brand and leadership levels

  • Understand your clients’ business, disease areas and brand strategy deeply, and bring a proactive point of view on where the brand should go next

  • Anticipate risks, resolve issues before they escalate, and keep complex programs moving through MLR and launch timelines

    • Team Leadership

  • Lead, mentor and develop Account Supervisors and Account Executives, setting clear priorities and creating real opportunities to grow

  • Foster a collaborative, low-ego team culture across account, creative, strategy and project management

What you bring

  • 8+ years of experience in pharmaceutical advertising, with experience managing HCP and/or DTC promotional campaigns

  • Proven success leading client relationships at a senior level and growing accounts

  • Strong digital and omnichannel marketing experience

  • Experience with new product launches and label updates is a strong plus

  • Deep knowledge of medical, legal and regulatory compliance and the US MLR review process

  • Experience owning account financials, including SOWs, forecasting and profitability

  • A track record of leading and mentoring account teams

  • Excellent communication, negotiation and presentation skills

  • Bachelor’s degree in communications, marketing, business or a related field

    • What this role is not
    This isn’t a project-management or coordination role. You’ll be expected to think strategically, bring a point of view to your clients, and grow the business, not just keep the trains running. And it’s not a hands-off leadership seat. In our flat structure, Account Directors stay close to the work and their clients every day.

What you’ll get:

  • Remote, for real: P10 has been fully remote for 15 years, by design. No office mandates, no return-to-office surprises
  • Time to recharge: 15 days of paid vacation (plus one more day for every year with us), unlimited flex and sick time, and a company holiday calendar
  • Health coverage: medical, dental and vision through Cigna, with P10 covering 80% of employee medical premiums and 100% of employee dental and vision
  • Peace of mind: life insurance, plus short- and long-term disability coverage for everyone
  • Planning ahead: a retirement savings plan with a company match of up to 2% (Betterment in the US, Wealthsimple in Canada)
  • Set up for success: a laptop shipped to you before day one, plus a home office stipend to make your space your own
  • Real connection: an annual all-company offsite, plus a Slack culture full of shout-outs, side channels and people who actually know each other
  • A flat, hands-on team: small teams, fewer approval layers and leaders who are in the work with you

The environment

P10 is remote-first, always has been. This role is open to candidates in the United States, with a preference for Eastern time zone. You'll be working inside a structure flat enough that your creative vision actually shapes client work.

Interested in working with us? Apply online today. For this role, a copy of your work portfolio will also be required for later interview stages.

Not an agency*

The layer-laden teams. The prehistoric processes. The impersonal, ego-driven dog-and-pony shows. Take what you think you know about agencies and burn it. P10 was born of the idea that if something isn't working—or could work better—change it. And that's exactly what we did. We know that what we're not makes us who we are. And we're not just another agency. We are people driven by a palpable passion and purpose, felt by our clients from the very first conversation.

P10 brings together a team of diverse, remote-only seasoned professionals to deliver exceptional value for our clients. Dare to do something different - join us.

jobs.description:
About us

At Viasat, the work you do helps people stay connected in ways that matter, from everyday moments to critical missions across air, land, sea, and space.

We’re a place for people who are curious, bold, and motivated by meaningful work. Here, you'll have the opportunity to make an impact, explore new possibilities, and grow your career in ways that align with your interests and goals. When you're ready to take on something new, you'll find leaders who support your development and help you turn your ambition into action.


What you'll do

This team plays a critical role in sustaining the security posture, compliance evidence, and documentation integrity across multiple networks and systems within Viasat Government.

You will be a key contributor to our Risk Management Framework (RMF) and Authority to Operate (ATO) lifecycle - hardening and validating equipment against the current DISA STIG, evaluating identifiers (CVE, IAVM, STIG IDs, CCIs) that come back from the Security team's scans, and keeping our system documentation accurate and audit-ready.

This is a high-impact role for someone who takes pride in precise, defensible work and who thrives on collaboration. Beyond executing hardening tasks, you will navigate the environment confidently - moving between physical and virtual systems, STIG checklists, and documentation repositories to trace a finding from the Security team's scan output to the affected component, through the change, and into the record of remediation. You will help uphold the standards that keep our networks accredited and operational.

The successful applicant must be self-motivated, capable of completing structured compliance work with minimum supervision, and comfortable asking the right questions in a working session before acting.

The role will require coordination with a wide range of other project teams both within and external to Viasat, including the Cyber Security Operations Center, Security Engineering, and system owners. The successful candidate must be able to represent the team clearly in working groups, scan review meetings, and audit discussions. The role may require travel to support compliance activities at operational sites.


The day-to-day

  • Performing preventative maintenance of hardware, software, and networks. This is accomplished via routine inspection, backup, physical maintenance, etc. Collaboration with the other team members to ensure accuracy and thoroughness of pre, main, and post execution work.
  • Documenting procedure creation, corrective actions, configurations, diagrams, etc. The documentation consists of trouble tickets and logs, equipment configurations, wiring diagrams, block and level diagrams, logic diagrams, rack elevation drawings, physical interconnection diagrams, backhaul circuit information, System Change Control, Corrective Action Reports.
  • Cyber and Information Assuredness. You will work closely with the Cyber Security Operations Center, and the Security Engineering team to identify vulnerabilities, verify network impact, and remediate applicable components. You will perform STIGs on a quarterly basis along with other RMF/ATO activities on a routine basis.
  • Configuration-Level STIG Hardening. Perform hands-on configuration work on the gear that supports Viasat Government: Cisco IOS/NX-OS routers and switches, Palo Alto PAN-OS firewalls, Red Hat Enterprise Linux (shell, systemd, SELinux, auditd), Windows Server and Windows 11 (Group Policy, local policy, PowerShell), PostgreSQL and SQL Server, PDUs, security/infrastructure appliances, VMware ESXi and vCenter, VDI, and NetApp A400 (ONTAP). Pull the current running configuration, compare it against the applicable DISA STIG, apply the gap-closing changes, and confirm each setting behaves as intended before marking it closed.
  • Impact Analysis from changes. Before touching a setting, understand what it controls, what it is likely to affect operationally, and what to watch for during and after the change. Flag operational risk to senior engineers and IA and help shape the mitigation, rather than applying changes blindly from the benchmark.
  • Collaborate with Team & Stakeholders. Join working sessions with the team to discuss vulnerability scan results, agree on applicability and ownership for each item, and translate findings into concrete configuration work on the affected platform.
  • Evidence Capture and Deliverables. Record required information using an approved template. This can include findings addressed, the exact setting changed, the validation performed, the supporting command output or screenshots, and the resulting state for each hardening action - and keep the surrounding artifacts current, including STIG checklists, POA&M entries, change control records, interconnection and rack diagrams, and Corrective Action Reports.

What you'll need

  • 5+ years of experience administering virtualized environments (VMs), managing multi-tenant storage systems, integrated network routing/switching, and enterprise firewall policies
  • Familiarity with virtualized environments (VMs), storage, routing/switching, and firewall policies (CCNA-level understanding is sufficient)
  • Hands-on comfort at the command line and management console for networking gear, Linux, and Windows - able to pull a running configuration, apply a change under direction, and confirm it took effect
  • Working knowledge of DoD security posture, including DISA STIGs, POA&Ms, IAVMs, and the RMF compliance framework
  • Demonstrated attention to detail producing technical documentation - checklists, diagrams, change records, and audit evidence
  • Strong collaboration and communication skills, with a willingness to take direction from senior engineers
  • Security+ certification or equivalent that meets the DoD Directive 8570 baseline (must be able to obtain within 45 days)
  • Active DoD Secret Clearance or ability to obtain when administratively feasible
  • Ability to travel up to 15%
  • Ability to work an on-call rotation.

What will help you on the job

  • RedHat Certified Systems Administrator (RHCSA)
  • VMware Certified Professional
  • Windows Server AZ-800 / AZ-801
  • CCNA, CCNP, or CISSP
  • Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Information Technology or equivalent experience
  • Nessus, Security Center familiarity
  • Identity and access management
  • Automation using Python, Ansible, PowerShell, etc.
  • Identity and access management
  • Experience configuring, administering, upgrading, and securing a wide variety of equipment and applications

jobs.title: CRM Practice Lead
jobs.excerpt: With 75 years of experience, our focus is on helping the most vulnerable children overcome poverty and experience fullness of life.
jobs.description:
With 75 years of experience, our focus is on helping the most vulnerable children overcome poverty and experience fullness of life. We help children of all backgrounds, even in the most dangerous places, inspired by our Christian faith.

Come join our 31,000+ staff working in nearly 100 countries and share the joy of transforming vulnerable children’s life stories!

Key Responsibilities:


IMPORTANT INFORMATION:

  • All CVs should be submitted in English.
  • This position is open to candidates based in countries where World Vision International is legally registered to operate.

JOB PURPOSE:


Lead the GTD CRM practice as a product-and-service capability for World Vision. Set direction and operational discipline for the global CRM core, guide its lifecycle and roadmap, and coordinate delivery with Support Offices (SOs) and FOs, Global Centre teams and implementation partners. Ensure the practice delivers dependable, secure and supportable CRM capabilities that improve supporter and donor engagement, fundraising operations across websites and fundraising channels, and partnership-wide reuse—while allowing justified local variation.


This is a manager-level role: accountable for people and partner leadership, prioritisation, service outcomes, budgets and cross-office alignment, product delivery, while working with technical specialists on detailed design and implementation, and ensuring the practice operates within the enterprise architecture and its standards. The role operates within approved governance and investment decisions; it develops evidence and recommendations where decisions remain open.


KEY RESPONSIBILITIES:


Practice leadership and product direction


  • Translate World Vision’s GTD CRM and MarTech direction into a prioritised practice plan, product roadmap, release plan and service objectives.
  • Steward the global CRM core as a reusable product: manage lifecycle, backlog, releases, documentation, support readiness and continuous improvement
  • Steward the local CRM variants as reusable product to reduce fragmentation: manage lifecycle, backlog, releases, documentation, support readiness and continuous improvement. Steward the enterprise integration products’ needs to be in line with Enterprise Architecture, Cloud and Integration Strategies.
  • Identify business value streams and value of required capabilities for implementation. Evaluate cost benefits for localization and impact in product roadmap.
  • Maintain a clear boundary between global core capabilities and SO-owned local processes, last-mile configuration, customisation and external integrations under Enterprise Architecture and GTD Strategy. Apply the principle “common where possible, different where proven.”
  • Assess demand, capability gaps and adoption readiness across offices; present options, dependencies, risks and investment cases to the appropriate governance forums.
  • Keep platform recommendations evidence-led and fit to office needs; do not treat any single vendor or implementation pattern as a predetermined outcome.
  • Under the Enterprise Architecture team’s lead, contribute CRM-domain input to the business capability map of the CRM and MarTech landscape, showing which platforms (such as Dynamics 365, Business Central, SIMMA, iVISION, HubSpot and the CSM application) support each capability across the Global Centre and SOs; use it to identify overlaps, gaps and consolidation opportunities, and to inform roadmap and investment decisions.

Governance and partnership engagement


  • Establish effective working arrangements with SO/ FO business and technology leaders, Global Centre stakeholders, service teams and vendors.
  • Facilitate CRM governance, product forums and decision-making, including transparent prioritisation, decision rights, escalation paths and clear records of commitments.
  • Ensure SO representatives have meaningful input into priorities and that delivery commitments, service levels and decision authority are aligned.
  • Coordinate adoption planning, communications, training and change enablement with local leaders; support offices with different levels of readiness, scale and investment capacity.
  • Resolve cross-office issues constructively and escalate strategic, funding, policy or risk decisions to the designated sponsor or steering body.
  • Clear ownership and escalation.
  • Improved documentation and knowledge transfer.
  • Evidence of reusable capabilities and reduced avoidable duplication.
  • Supplier performance.
  • Appropriate security and privacy controls.

Delivery, service and supplier performance


  • Lead a predictable portfolio of CRM changes, deployments, upgrades and stabilisation work with accountable plans, milestones, risks, dependencies and acceptance criteria.
  • Coordinate internal teams and suppliers across discovery, design, build/configuration, integration, data migration, testing, release, hyper care and transition to support.
  • Embed recognised platform and engineering best practices across internal and supplier teams, including application lifecycle management, environment strategy, source control, CI/CD pipelines, automated testing, configure-before-customise guardrails, low-code/Power Platform governance, vendor-recommended practices (e.g. Microsoft Success by Design and Well-Architected guidance, AWS) and timely adoption of platform updates.
  • Oversee operational service performance, incident/problem trends, change control, release quality, knowledge transfer and support readiness.
  • Manage supplier capacity, deliverables, quality, commercial performance and service levels; reduce avoidable vendor dependency through documentation and internal capability.
  • Protect business continuity for fundraising and supporter-facing operations; ensure issues affecting revenue, payments or supporter care receive timely attention.
  • Oversee the fundraising and payment capabilities supported by the CRM, including campaigns, online and offline donations, recurring giving and sponsorship payments, direct debit and card processing, payment gateway integrations, refunds, chargebacks and reconciliation with finance; ensure PCI DSS compliance, secure handling of payment data and timely resolution of failed payments.
  • In partnership with digital, marketing and SO/FO teams, oversee the CRM-connected fundraising websites and channels, including donation and sponsorship websites, online donation forms and checkouts, supporter portals, mobile, email and SMS, social, peer-to-peer, events, telemarketing, face-to-face and partner channels; ensure reliable data capture and hand-off to CRM, consent capture, a consistent supporter experience, conversion tracking and attribution, accessibility, security and availability during peak campaigns.
  • Achieve SLA commitments and properly escalate, own remediation plan with delivery teams.

Architecture, integration, data and risk stewardship


  • Partner with architecture, security, data and integration leads to ensure CRM capabilities comply with enterprise architecture principles, reference architectures, standards and approved designs; bring significant changes to the architecture review board or design authority and manage any exceptions through the agreed waiver process with documented risks and remediation plans.
  • Provide practice-level oversight of the integrated CRM ecosystem, which may include Dynamics 365, Business Central, the CSM application, AWS native integration or other integration technologies, and connections to Horizon, RMT, payment gateways and payment service providers, fundraising websites and digital donation platforms, and supporter-facing and fundraising channels.
  • Promote reliable supporter data, data quality, privacy, security, data residency and appropriate controls; ensure risks and compliance obligations are visible in plans and governance.
  • Reduce uncontrolled copies of data across CRM, MarTech and local systems in alignment with Cybersecurity: agree an authoritative source for each key data set (such as supporter, sponsorship and child records), prefer reuse through shared services and APIs over replication, and retire redundant data stores and extracts.
  • Ensure integrations that exchange child and sponsor data are inventoried, risk-assessed and approved before go-live; apply data minimisation, least-privilege access, encryption, logging and monitoring; protect child images and identifying information in line with World Vision safeguarding, privacy and data protection policies; and act promptly on any exposure.
  • Contribute with the Enterprise Architecture team to the target-state CRM, Sponsor Engagement and MarTech architecture and transition roadmap; keep the CRM domain’s content in the EA-owned application portfolio, integration inventory and architecture artefacts current.
  • Ensure solution and service documentation is maintained, reusable and sufficient for operations, audit, knowledge transfer and future deployments.
  • Assess technical debt, product dependencies, end-of-life exposure and resilience risks; sponsor mitigation plans with accountable owners.

Financial and performance management


  • Build transparent budgets and total-cost-of-ownership (TCO) views covering product, licensing, environments, delivery, integrations, suppliers, support and local participation.
  • Track forecasts, actuals, benefits, capacity and cost allocations; surface assumptions and variances early.
  • Define and report a balanced set of practice measures, such as roadmap progress, delivery against approved commitments, release quality, service performance, payment processing reliability, deployment readiness, adoption, user outcomes, stakeholder confidence, data quality, platform rationalisation, CRM-domain contributions to the EA-led capability map, adoption of engineering best practices, enterprise architecture compliance and exceptions, reduction of uncontrolled data copies, protection of child and sponsor data, risk and cost transparency; agree baselines and annual targets with the sponsor and governance body.
  • Use evidence from office feedback, operational data and delivery results to improve the product and the service model.

People leadership and capability building


  • Lead, coach and develop assigned team members; set clear objectives, support wellbeing and build a collaborative, inclusive and accountable culture.
  • Plan capability and capacity across product management, business analysis, CRM configuration, integration, data, service management and change enablement.
  • Build communities of practice and practical knowledge-sharing across Global Centre, SOs and delivery partners.
  • Identify skills gaps and develop succession, learning and internal capability plans that strengthen sustainable product ownership.

KNOWLEDGE, SKILL AND EXPERIENCE:


Required Education, training, license, registration, and/or Certification

  • Bachelor’s Degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, or other related field. Or equivalent work experience.

Required Professional Experience

  • Typically has 7 to 10 years of relevant IT and business work experience.
  • Requires demonstrated ability to launch and deliver a single IT project on time and within budget.
  • Substantial experience leading CRM or enterprise business application products, services or transformation programmes across multiple stakeholder groups.
  • Demonstrated people leadership, delivery management and supplier-management experience at manager level.
  • Experience in product road mapping, backlog prioritisation, service operations, governance, financial planning and benefits/performance reporting.
  • Strong understanding of CRM-enabled supporter/customer journeys, fundraising or relationship-management processes, data quality, integrations and change adoption.
  • Working knowledge of business architecture practice, or equivalent including business capability modelling, application portfolio management and architecture governance, and experience contributing to them under an enterprise architecture team’s lead.
  • Experience overseeing and ensuring modern delivery practices to business application platforms, such as application lifecycle management, DevOps, CI/CD and automated testing.
  • Understanding of data protection and child safeguarding principles as they apply to systems and integrations handling sensitive personal data, including data minimisation and access control.
  • Experience working across countries or federated organisations, balancing shared standards with legitimate local needs.
  • Strong written and verbal communication, facilitation, negotiation and executive-level decision support skills.

Leadership Behaviours

  • Leads with integrity, humility and a service mindset aligned to World Vision’s mission and values.
  • Makes complex technology and cost trade-offs understandable and transparent.
  • Builds trust across cultures and functions, listens to office needs and follows through on commitments.
  • Uses evidence, manages risk openly and distinguishes confirmed decisions from proposals.
  • Encourages learning, accountability, inclusion and sustainable change.

Required Language(s)

  • Excellent command of spoken and written English, with the ability to communicate clearly and effectively with diverse stakeholders.

Preferred Experience, Knowledge and/or other Qualifications

  • Experience with Microsoft Dynamics 365 and related CRM/marketing capabilities (such as SIMMA, iVISION, Hubspot, etc); familiarity with Business Central, Integration or comparable integration platforms is an advantage.
  • Experience with supporter, donor, sponsorship, payment or nonprofit CRM processes, including payment gateway integration, PCI DSS compliance and fundraising or digital donation platforms.
  • Familiarity with cloud service management, information security, privacy, data residency, vendor ecosystems and total-cost-of-ownership analysis.
  • Relevant product, project/programme, service-management or change-management certification.
  • Worked in a DevOps, cloud native environment, familiar to CICD practices and expectation from DevSecOps team.

Local and International Applicants (IA's) Accepted

Executive Partner, CFO Advisory


About Gartner

Gartner is the world's leading research and advisory company, helping business leaders across every major industry make faster, smarter decisions and achieve their most critical priorities. Gartner's CFO & Finance Executive Programs provide finance leaders with objective insight, expert guidance, and a powerful peer network to accelerate business performance and transformation.


About the Role

Gartner is seeking accomplished current and former Chief Financial Officers from publicly traded organizations with at least $1 billion in annual revenue to join our CFO Executive Partner team.

As an Executive Partner, you will serve as a trusted advisor to a portfolio of CFOs and senior finance executives, helping them navigate complex business challenges, advance strategic priorities, and improve organizational performance. Leveraging your executive leadership experience, you will engage as a peer counselor, coach, and thought partner while helping clients maximize the value of Gartner's research, insights, and advisory resources.

This role provides a unique opportunity to remain engaged with senior business leaders, influence the future of the finance function, and share your expertise across multiple industries while enjoying the flexibility of a fully remote position.


What You'll Do

Trusted Advisor to CFOs

  • Serve as a strategic advisor to a portfolio of senior finance executives and CFOs.
  • Conduct regular executive consultations focused on leadership effectiveness, organizational transformation, financial performance, and strategic execution.
  • Help CFOs identify priorities, evaluate challenges, and develop practical action plans to achieve business outcomes.
  • Share insights, best practices, and lessons learned from your own executive leadership experience.

Executive Engagement & Thought Leadership

  • Facilitate executive workshops, peer discussions, and leadership sessions for CFO members.
  • Lead discussions and executive roundtables at Gartner conferences and client events.
  • Foster executive networking and knowledge sharing among senior finance leaders.
  • Contribute to the development and delivery of CFO-focused thought leadership and research initiatives.

Client Success & Business Growth

  • Partner closely with Gartner sales, service, and research teams to deliver exceptional client value.
  • Participate in account planning, renewal discussions, and prospective member conversations.
  • Help organizations understand how Gartner's research and advisory capabilities can accelerate business outcomes.
  • Support member retention by building trusted, long-term executive relationships.

Ideal Background

Successful candidates will bring:

  • Current or former Chief Financial Officer experience within a publicly traded company generating at least $1 billion in annual revenue.
  • Demonstrated success leading enterprise finance organizations through growth, transformation, restructuring, digital modernization, M&A activity, capital allocation decisions, or operational performance improvement.
  • Experience engaging Boards of Directors, Audit Committees, investors, analysts, and external stakeholders.
  • Broad expertise across core finance disciplines, including financial planning and analysis, accounting, treasury, investor relations, capital markets, risk management, and finance technology.
  • A proven ability to influence senior executives and drive enterprise-wide outcomes.
  • Strong executive presence, facilitation skills, and business judgment.

Highly Valued Qualifications

  • Fortune 500 leadership experience.
  • Multi-industry or multinational operating experience.
  • Public company governance and SEC reporting expertise.
  • Experience leading large-scale organizational transformation initiatives.
  • Prior consulting, advisory, board, executive coaching, or mentoring experience.

Location & Travel

  • Fully remote position.
  • Candidates may reside anywhere within the continental United States.
  • Domestic travel typically ranges from 20% to 25%, varying based on client engagement needs, conference participation, and business priorities.

Why Executive Leaders Join Gartner

Many Executive Partners join Gartner after distinguished operating careers because they want to continue making an impact while engaging with some of the world's most senior finance leaders. The role offers the opportunity to:

  • Influence and advise CFOs across diverse industries.
  • Remain connected to the most important trends shaping the future of finance.
  • Leverage decades of executive leadership experience in a highly strategic capacity.
  • Collaborate with an elite network of former and current business leaders.
  • Enjoy flexibility while continuing to operate at the highest levels of executive leadership.

Executive Partners are full-time Gartner employees with full benefits. The role can be based anywhere in the continental United States.


Who are we?

At Gartner, Inc. (NYSE:IT), we guide the leaders who shape the world.

Our mission relies on expert analysis and bold ideas to deliver actionable, objective business and technology insights, helping enterprise leaders and their teams succeed with their mission-critical priorities.

Since our founding in 1979, we’ve grown to 20,000 associates globally who support over 13,000 client enterprises in ~90 countries and territories. We do important, interesting and substantive work that matters. That’s why we hire associates with the intellectual curiosity, energy and drive to want to make a difference. The bar is unapologetically high. So is the impact you can have here.

What makes Gartner a great place to work?

Our vast, virtually untapped market potential offers limitless opportunities – opportunities that may not even exist right now – for you to grow professionally and flourish personally. How far you go is driven by your passion and performance.

We hire remarkable people who collaborate and win as a team. Together, our singular, unifying goal is to deliver results for our clients.

Our teams are inclusive and composed of individuals from different geographies, cultures, religions, ethnicities, races, genders, sexual orientations, abilities and generations.

We invest in great leaders who bring out the best in you and the company, enabling us to multiply our impact and results. This is why, year after year, we are recognized worldwide as a great place to work.

Gartner is the world authority on AI

At Gartner, you’ll join a company at the very center of the AI revolution. Gartner has proactive, objective guidance throughout clients’ AI journeys. We set the standard for how organizations leverage artificial intelligence to drive meaningful impact. You’ll have access to unmatched resources, expertise, and technology, and play a key role in helping Gartner and our clients innovate and grow as we leverage AI to transform business and technology landscapes.

It’s an exciting time to be at Gartner, with limitless opportunities to make a real impact, grow your skills, and build a lasting, meaningful career in a field that’s reshaping the way we operate. If you’re passionate about AI and want to be part of a team that’s guiding the leaders who shape the world, Gartner is the place for you.

What do we offer?

Gartner offers world-class benefits, highly competitive compensation and disproportionate rewards for top performers.

In our hybrid work environment, we provide the flexibility and support for you to thrive — working virtually when it's productive to do so and getting together with colleagues in a vibrant community that is purposeful, engaging and inspiring.

Ready to grow your career with Gartner? Join us.

Gartner believes in fair and equitable pay. A reasonable estimate of the base salary range for this role is 188,000 USD - 225,000 USD. Please note that actual salaries may vary within the range, or be above or below the range, based on factors including, but not limited to, education, training, experience, professional achievement, business need, and location. In addition to base salary, employees will participate in either an annual bonus plan based on company and individual performance, or a role-based, uncapped sales incentive plan. Square Roots is a global technology leader in indoor farming, founded in 2017 by entrepreneurs Kimbal Musk and Tobias Peggs. The company’s advanced modular farming platform empowers partners to accelerate agricultural research and bring new food innovations to market faster. Collaborating with leading organizations, such as Gordon Food Service and the Gates Foundation in the US, UAE and Japan, Square Roots leverages its controlled-climate systems to advance plant science, develop resilient crop varieties, and strengthen food supply chains in the face of climate change.

About the role

We are seeking a Director of Program Management, Commercial R&D, to own delivery of our international client programs, from the first scoping conversation to client sign-off. You'll turn commercial vision into programs our teams can execute. That means testing scope and feasibility before we commit, running one integrated plan across several concurrent statements of work, and leading the client relationship day to day. Current programs span techno-economic assessments, new crop development and building R&D farms.

This is a senior, hands-on role. You will work through hard problems and make decisions, anticipate risks, align competing priorities, and drive execution while maintaining client expectations and trust. You'll report to the Vice President with a close working line to the VP of Platform, and alongside our R&D, hardware, software and build teams.

Responsibilities

jobs.excerpt: Alignment Health is breaking the mold in conventional health care, committed to serving seniors and those who need it most: the chronically ill and frail.
jobs.description:
Alignment Health is breaking the mold in conventional health care, committed to serving seniors and those who need it most: the chronically ill and frail. Working at Alignment Health provides an opportunity to do work that really matters, not only changing lives but saving them. Together.

The Data Analyst – Technology is a mid-level individual contributor responsible for querying, analyzing, and reporting on Medicare Advantage healthcare data to support operational decision-making and regulatory compliance across technology operations. This role works closely with the Senior Data Analyst, product managers, and platform engineers to translate business requirements into analytical outputs — including reports, dashboards, and data validations — within an agile development environment. The Data Analyst builds foundational expertise in healthcare data domains including claims, member/eligibility, and provider data, and contributes to the team's data quality and documentation standards. This position is a key development role on the path toward senior-level analytical ownership and growing specialization in Medicare Advantage data platforms.

Job Duties/Responsibilities

Data Analysis & Querying: Write and maintain SQL queries to extract, transform, and analyze healthcare datasets — including medical claims, pharmacy claims, member/eligibility, and provider data — in support of operational reporting and ad hoc analytical requests.

Requirements Gathering Support: Participate in agile/scrum ceremonies and assist in translating business requirements into analytical specifications, data mappings, and reporting logic under the guidance of senior team members.

Reporting & Dashboard Support: Build and maintain recurring reports and dashboards using Power BI, Tableau, or equivalent BI tools that present healthcare data clearly for operational and compliance audiences.

Data Quality Validation: Apply data quality checks, validate source-to-target mappings, and identify anomalies or inconsistencies in healthcare datasets to support data integrity and audit readiness.

Regulatory & Compliance Reporting: Support the production of HEDIS, STAR ratings, CMS encounter, and risk adjustment reporting outputs by executing defined analytical processes and validating results against established data standards.

Documentation & Process Support: Maintain analytical documentation — including query libraries, data dictionaries, and process notes — to support team knowledge continuity and operational handoff requirements.

Continuous Learning & AI Awareness: Develop familiarity with cloud data platforms, data modeling concepts, and AI-assisted analytics tools, and actively build skills that support growth toward the Senior Data Analyst level.

Supervisory Responsibilities

This role has no direct supervisory responsibilities.

Job Requirements

Experience

Required:

  • 3–5 years of progressive experience in data analysis, business intelligence, or a closely related analytical function
  • Demonstrated hands-on experience writing SQL queries for data extraction, transformation, and validation in a production or near-production environment
  • Experience working with healthcare data, including at least one of the following domains: medical claims, pharmacy claims, member/eligibility, or provider data
  • Working knowledge of reports and dashboards using Power BI, Tableau, or an equivalent BI platform
  • Familiarity with working in an agile or scrum team environment, including participation in sprint ceremonies and iterative delivery
  • Experience in a regulated data environment with exposure to data quality validation, HIPAA requirements, or PHI/PII handling practices

Preferred:

  • Experience in a Medicare Advantage, Medicaid, or managed care health plan environment
  • Exposure to CMS reporting requirements, HEDIS measures, STAR ratings logic, or risk adjustment data
  • Familiarity with cloud data platforms (Azure, AWS, or GCP) or data transformation tools (e.g., Databricks, Azure Data Factory, or equivalent)
  • Experience applying AI-assisted or automated analytics tools to routine analytical workflows

Education

Required:

  • Bachelor's degree in Data Science, Information Systems, Informatics, or a related field; an equivalent combination of education and directly relevant experience will be considered

Preferred:

  • Progress toward or completion of a Master's degree in Data Science, Health Informatics, Business Analytics, or a related discipline

Training

Required:

  • Demonstrated proficiency in SQL through direct work experience; equivalent hands-on experience accepted in lieu of formal training
  • Working knowledge of at least one BI or data visualization tool (Power BI, Tableau, or equivalent), demonstrated through project or work experience

Preferred:

  • Introductory or intermediate training in cloud data platforms (Azure, AWS, or GCP)
  • Completion of relevant healthcare data analytics coursework or professional development (e.g., AHIMA, CPHIMS, or equivalent)
  • Exposure to AI-augmented analytics tools or data storytelling training

Skills & Competencies

Technical/Role-Specific Skills

SQL & Data Querying: Solid, hands-on SQL skills for data extraction, filtering, joining, and basic transformation across relational databases; ability to write and maintain queries for recurring analytical needs.

Healthcare Data Domains: Working knowledge of medical claims, pharmacy claims, member/eligibility, and provider data structures, with growing familiarity with EDI standards (834/837), ICD-10/CPT codes, and CMS data formats.

BI & Data Visualization: Proficiency in Power BI, Tableau, or equivalent tools for building and maintaining operational dashboards, standard reports, and data summaries for business and compliance audiences.

Data Quality & Validation: Ability to apply data quality checks, identify anomalies, and validate outputs against source data to ensure accuracy, completeness, and compliance readiness across healthcare datasets.

Data Documentation: Demonstrated ability to write and maintain clear analytical documentation including query logic, data dictionaries, source-to-target notes, and process runbooks.

Cloud Platform Awareness: Basic familiarity with cloud data environments (Azure, AWS, or GCP) and willingness to develop hands-on proficiency in cloud-native analytics tools such as Databricks or Azure Data Factory.

Analytical Communication: Ability to translate data findings into clear written summaries and visualizations that support non-technical stakeholders in making informed operational decisions.

Licensure

Required: None

Preferred: None

Essential Physical Functions

The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodation may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

  • The employee frequently lifts and/or moves up to 10 pounds. Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision and the ability to adjust focus.

This role translates commercial priorities into scalable enablement programs that strengthen field readiness, build commercial capability, and drive high performance across field teams.

This role works hand in hand with Product Marketing, Enablement, and Commercial team members with one shared goal: help sales win. Through strong cross-functional partnerships, the Senior Manager enables better understanding of WCG’s markets and solutions, strategic alignment to high-value market opportunities, stronger differentiation in competitive deals, and more consistent buyer experiences.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES/RESPONSIBILITIES: To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential duty and responsibility satisfactorily. The accountabilities listed below are representative of the knowledge, skills, and/or ability required.

Enablement Strategy & Execution

  • Develop and manage the enablement roadmap and help operationalize Go-to-Market (GTM) plans to drive consistent execution, adoption, and performance across the field.
  • Partner with commercial and GTM leaders to identify execution gaps and determine a prioritization process for balancing planned initiatives with emerging field requirements.

Commercial Readiness & Capability

  • Establish and reinforce consistent commercial practices that improve how teams engage customers, navigate opportunities, and execute throughout the sales cycle.
  • Support consistent application of WCG’s sales methodologies, commercial practices, processes, and tools through training, coaching resources, and practical field guidance.
  • Partner with Commercial Operations to translate sales processes, systems, and workflow changes into effective field practices.
  • Identify and scale effective practices across teams while adapting enablement to different customer segments, solutions, and commercial motions.

Onboarding & Ongoing Development

  • Own and continuously evolve WCG’s commercial onboarding program, developing role-based learning journeys that equip new team members with the knowledge, skills, tools, and processes needed to ramp quickly.
  • Establish assessment and coaching frameworks that measure readiness, reinforce learning, and build proficiency over time.
  • Develop foundational learning and development programs that strengthen core commercial capabilities – discovery, qualification, value-based selling, objective strategic, storytelling, etc. – and address evolving seller, manager, and business needs.
  • Equip commercial managers with resources and guidance to reinforce learning, coach to key capabilities, and support continued seller development.

Training, Tools & Seller Efficiency

  • Design and deliver role-relevant programs, workshops, and assessments that improve commercial effectiveness and field application.
  • Develop learning resources, sales playbooks, and process guidelines that support consistent execution.
  • Leverage enablement and AI tools to enhance enablement content, seller workflows, and create scalable tools and processes that support productivity and insight-led selling.
  • Act as an expert user of Dock and Gong to improve access to information, reinforce learning, and support customer-facing workflows.
  • Support change management and adoption for new commercial tools, processes, and ways of working.

GTM, Field Readiness & Product Marketing Collaboration

  • Partner with Product Marketing and cross-functional teams to support commercial readiness for new offerings, launches, campaigns, and evolving go-to-market priorities.
  • Help translate positioning, buyer insights, competitive intelligence, solution updates, and market priorities into practical learning and reinforcement that help commercial teams apply them effectively in customer conversations.
  • Support development and activation of sales plays, narratives, and other resources that improve field execution, while ensuring commercial learning programs remain current with WCG’s portfolio, value propositions, customer needs, and market strategy.
  • Gather feedback from commercial teams on customer conversations, market response, and execution challenges and share relevant insights with Product Marketing or other cross-functional partners.

Growth & Performance

  • Assess key commercial signals and measure enablement effectiveness through training completion and assessment scores, launch readiness, content and tool adoption in workflows, and sales productivity, ramp time, and win rates.
  • Monitor onboarding and development data to identify proficiency gaps , or reinforcement needs, and opportunities to improve.
  • Translate performance insights into actions that improve commercial outcomes and grow sales bookings for respective offerings.
  • Act as a champion of the commercial team throughout the product and customer lifecycle, gathering feedback to continuously refine enablement approaches and GTM execution.
  • Other duties as assigned by supervisor. These may, on occasion, be unrelated to the position described here.

CERTIFICATIONS/LICENSE/REGISTRATION REQUIREMENTS:

  • Sales enablement, learning & development, or sales methodology certification (e.g., MEDDICC, Challenger, Sandler) preferred, but not required
