jobs.description:
We are hiring a Security Governance, Risk and Compliance (GRC) Manager to lead the team that keeps Canonical's security and compliance credible to the Enterprises, Clouds, Telcos and Governments that run on Ubuntu, and to bring our controls and risk management to the standard a public company requires.

Location: EMEA or Americas — fully remote (home-based), with the option to work from our London office.

About our Team

Canonical's customers trust Ubuntu with critical systems. That trust rests on evidence: our ISO 27001 and SOC 2 certifications, how we manage risk, and how we respond as security regulation such as the EU Cyber Resilience Act reaches open source software. The Governance, Risk and Compliance (GRC) team produces that evidence and makes it real across the company. As Canonical prepares to list on a public exchange, the team is also central to the controls and risk reporting our Audit Committee and Board rely on.

The team is part of Operations and reports to the Chief Operating Officer. It covers both sides of the discipline: keeping us certified and compliant today, and looking ahead at risk across corporate IT, infrastructure and products. It works closely with Engineering, Security Operations, Information Systems, Legal, Finance and Sales.

You will lead the team, set its priorities and operating rhythm, and be the first escalation point for security and compliance decisions.

What you'll do

  • Lead and develop a team of GRC engineers: hire, coach and set priorities, and run a roadmap that balances planned work with operational requests, so the team delivers predictably and reports progress clearly to leadership. You own the team’s budget, vendors and tooling.
  • Own our ISO 27001 and SOC 2 certifications end to end: audit readiness, evidence collection, auditor relationships and fieldwork, so certifications are renewed on time with clean outcomes.
  • Run the risk management framework across corporate IT, infrastructure and products — asset classification, risk assessments, the risk register and key risk indicators — so leadership and the Board can see and decide on the company’s most important risks.
  • Own the information security policy framework — annual reviews, new policies, exceptions and risk acceptance — and make the call, or escalate it, when a policy and a business need conflict.
  • Partner with Finance on IT General Controls and internal controls over financial reporting — remediation, control execution and Audit Committee reporting — to make Canonical ready for a public listing.
  • Turn security regulation and standards — the EU Cyber Resilience Act, NIS2, DORA, the EU AI Act and IEC 62443 — into practical programmes with Legal and Engineering, including our secure software development lifecycle and penetration testing, so our products meet their obligations as they ship.
  • Build business continuity and disaster recovery with Information Systems and business owners — impact analysis, plans and tested recovery — so critical services can be restored when it matters.
  • Oversee third-party risk, access reviews and the governance of new tools and AI usage, and support customers and colleagues when it counts — security questionnaires, RFPs, our Trust Center, contract security terms and incident response — alongside Sales, Legal and Security Operations.

What we are looking for in you

  • Hands-on ownership of ISO 27001 and/or SOC 2 certification through external audit cycles
  • Experience designing or running a risk management framework (such as ISO 27005, NIST CSF or ISO 31000), including a risk register and reporting to senior leadership
  • Experience with IT General Controls supporting financial audits, under SOX or an equivalent regime
  • Experience leading a governance, risk and compliance, security compliance or IT risk team in a software or technology company
  • Experience turning regulatory and technical requirements into controls that engineering and business teams you don’t manage actually adopt
  • Sound judgement on risk acceptance and policy exceptions, and the confidence to hold a position with senior stakeholders
  • Passion for technology evidenced by personal projects and initiatives
  • Exceptional academic track record from both high school and university
  • Professional written and spoken English with excellent presentation skills
  • Ability to travel internationally twice a year for company events up to two weeks long

Nice-to-have skills

  • Experience preparing a company for a public listing
  • Experience with product security compliance for a software vendor (EU Cyber Resilience Act, IEC 62443 or NIST SSDF)
  • Business continuity and disaster recovery programme experience
  • Professional certifications such as CISSP, CISM, CISA or ISO 27001 Lead Auditor or Lead Implementer

How we work

We look for a track record of going above-and-beyond expectations to achieve outstanding results, backed by self-motivation and drive. Our people deliver their work precisely, taking care to deliver correctness and clarity. Reliability is at our core, where colleagues deliver high quality work that builds trust and confidence. We make ourselves accessible, collaborating to build products and systems that are usable. Finally we are adroit, blending enthusiasm, knowledge, adaptability, style and character.

What we offer colleagues

We consider geographical location, experience, and performance in shaping compensation worldwide. We revisit compensation annually (and more often for graduates and associates) to ensure we recognize outstanding performance. In addition to base pay, we offer a performance-driven annual bonus or commission. We provide all team members with additional benefits which reflect our values and ideals. We balance our programs to meet local needs and ensure fairness globally.

  • Distributed work environment, with bi-annual team travel to connect in person
  • Priority Pass for travel
  • Personal learning and development budget of USD 2,000 per year
  • Bi-annual compensation review
  • Recognition rewards
  • Annual holiday leave
  • Maternity and paternity leave
  • Team Member Assistance Program & Wellness Platform

About Canonical

Canonical is a pioneering tech firm at the forefront of the global move to open source. As the company that publishes Ubuntu, one of the most important open-source projects and the platform for AI, IoT, and the cloud, we are changing the world of software. We recruit on a global basis and set a very high standard for people joining the company. We expect excellence; in order to succeed, we need to be the best at what we do. Most colleagues at Canonical have worked from home since our inception in 2004. Working here is a step into the future and will challenge you to think differently, work smarter, learn new skills, and raise your game.

Canonical is an equal opportunity employer. Diversity of experience, perspectives, and background create a better work environment and better products. We are proud to foster a workplace free from discrimination, and regardless of your identity we will give your application fair consideration.

About CORA Banking & Financial Services Group:

CORA Banking & Financial Services Group is a division of CORA Group, part of Constellation Software Inc. (TSX: CSU), the world’s most prolific acquirer of vertical market software businesses. We buy and hold software companies that serve banks, credit unions, lenders, collection agencies and enterprise financial institutions, and we never sell them. Our focus areas are core and digital banking, payments, lending and credit, debt collection and recovery, risk and compliance, and financial operations and analytics. PhoenixWorx, acquired from Finastra in 2026, anchors the group alongside a growing portfolio including WebRecon and CORA Loyalty. We give founders a permanent home for their business, their people and their customers, and we give our team the chance to learn acquisitions inside the Constellation model, disciplined pricing, long-term ownership, and a seat at the table on every deal.

Job Profile (Location – USA/Canada, flexible):

Title: M&A Associate

Location: USA or Canada, flexible

Reports to: Vice President, M&A

Start: January 2027

The Associate builds and works our acquisition pipeline. You identify and research software businesses in our verticals, open relationships with founders and owners, qualify opportunities against our investment criteria, and bring the ones that fit to our twice-weekly deal review with a clear thesis. You own a defined territory of accounts, keep it current in Salesforce, and are measured on the quality of the conversations you create and the deals you move to an offer. You’ll learn how a Constellation acquirer screens, prices and buys software businesses, with a path to the modelling and deal-execution side as you progress.


What you’ll do:


  • Own a territory of target accounts across core and digital banking, payments, lending, debt collection and recovery, risk and compliance, and loyalty; research, prioritise and work it systematically.
  • Reach out to founders and owners by phone, email and in person; hold roughly five to ten substantive founder conversations a week once ramped.
  • Qualify opportunities against our criteria (revenue scale, recurring revenue, vertical fit, geography) using our screening tools, and log every interaction in Salesforce to CSI standards.
  • Write a one-page thesis for each opportunity you advance and present it at deal review.
  • Nurture long-cycle relationships with owners who aren’t ready to sell yet.
  • Support conference and event work: pre-show target lists, meeting booking, on-site coordination and post-show follow-up.
  • Work with the Senior Associate and VP on the early stages of modelling and diligence as opportunities progress.
  • Keep your pipeline current in our deal-workflow system.

Qualifications

Required:


  • 2 to 4 years in business development, sales development, corporate development, investment banking analyst work, or a research or sourcing role at an acquirer.
  • Demonstrated comfort with outbound outreach and high-volume relationship building; you’re not put off by cold calls.
  • Ability to read a software company quickly: what it does, who it sells to, how it makes money, whether it fits.
  • Strong written and verbal communication; you’ll be the first voice many founders hear from us.
  • Organised and disciplined about CRM hygiene and follow-up.
  • Eligible to work in Canada or the United States.

Preferred:

  • Exposure to B2B software, fintech, banking or collections.
  • Salesforce experience.
  • Basic financial literacy (recurring revenue, EBITDA, margins) and an interest in moving toward M&A execution.
  • A second language relevant to our markets.

Compensation and benefits:

  • Base salary within the posted range, set by experience and location.
  • MBO bonus tied to qualified founder conversations and opportunities advanced to an approved offer, with a quality condition so volume alone doesn’t pay.
  • Health, dental and vision benefits; retirement plan with employer match (RRSP in Canada, 401(k) in the US); paid vacation and personal days.
  • Remote work; Toronto office presence expected one to two days a quarter for Toronto-based hires.
  • Training in Constellation’s acquisition model and a defined path to Senior Associate, M&A.
  • Travel: approximately 20%, primarily to industry conferences and trade shows across North America, with occasional travel to meet target companies alongside the VP.

Description

About Us

When you join the LII LATAM U.S. Region Planning & Reportingteam at Liberty Mutual, you will help shape the financial narrative and strategic direction of a dynamic, multi-country business. You’ll work closely with Regional Executive leaders, the Regional President, Product Line Managers, and cross-functional stakeholders to provide timely, actionable insight into business performance.

About the Role

In this role, you will participate in the planning, reporting, and analysis of the LII LATAM U.S. Region’s financial results. You will analyze topline and bottom-line performance against plan, identify country- and product-line-level trends, and translate complex financial information into clear, compelling stories and recommendations for leadership. You will also serve as a key planning and reporting partner for assigned product lines, building subject-matter expertise and acting as a trusted resource for stakeholders.

This is an opportunity to combine strong financial acumen, analytical rigor, communication skills, and a continuous-improvement mindset (including the use of AI and emerging technologies) to enhance how the region plans, reports, and makes decisions.

Responsibilities

  • Support monthly Management Operating Review (MOR) meetings with the Regional Executive Team and Regional President by preparing clear, accurate, and insightful reporting on financial performance.
  • Analyze topline and bottom-line deviations from plan, forecast, prior year, and other relevant benchmarks; identify material drivers, emerging trends, risks, and opportunities.
  • Develop an understanding of financial performance by country, product line, and key business driver, and communicate findings in a concise, executive-ready format.
  • Serve as the primary planning and reporting contact for assigned product lines, partnering closely with Product Line Managers to support decision-making and build expertise in the business.
  • Help lead and coordinate elements of the annual and multi-year financial planning process, including topline assumptions, expense planning, consolidating outputs, and developing the overall financial story.
  • Partner with stakeholders to validate assumptions, investigate significant variances, resolve data questions, and ensure alignment on reporting results and planning inputs.
  • Prepare recurring and ad hoc analyses, reports, presentations, and financial models in accordance with established procedures and regional business needs.
  • Maintain clear documentation of recurring reporting processes, data sources, business assumptions, methodologies, and controls; update documentation as processes evolve.
  • Identify opportunities to improve reporting processes, planning tools, controls, data quality, and stakeholder experience.
  • Help drive innovation across the team by identifying and implementing practical applications of AI, automation, and other technologies to improve the speed, quality, and efficiency of financial planning and reporting.
  • Support regional strategic initiatives and special projects, including analysis, business-case development, implementation planning, and rollout support.
  • Act as a key communication link among Finance, Product Line leadership, Regional leadership, and other internal stakeholders, ensuring financial information is understood, aligned, and actionable.
Qualifications
  • Bachelor`s degree (Finance or Accounting) required.
  • CPA or advanced degree in Accounting, Finance, or Business preferred.
  • Minimum of 5 years of finance experience.
  • Must demonstrate attention to detail in a fast-paced work environment and the ability to manage and prioritize multiple projects simultaneously to drive results.
  • Communicates well with own team and across organizational boundaries to ensure the successful completion of shared goals.
  • Comfortable leading meetings and able to communicate issues and trends to senior management and other groups at the appropriate level of detail.
  • Solid understanding of Finance Tools and Analytical Methods.

locationRestrictions: South Georgia and the South Sandwich Islands
jobs.description:
On this journey for over 12 years, Qventus is leading the transformation of healthcare. We enable hospitals to focus on what matters most: patient care. Our innovative solutions harness the power of machine learning, generative AI, and behavioral science to deliver exceptional outcomes and empower care teams to anticipate and resolve issues before they arise.

Our success in rapid scale across the globe is backed by some of the world's leading investors. At Qventus, you will have the opportunity to work with an exceptional, mission-driven team across the globe, and the ability to directly impact the lives of patients. We’re inspired to work with healthcare leaders on our founding vision and unlock world-class medicine through world-class operations.

About the role:

We're looking for a Senior Analytics Specialist to head up ongoing analytics projects and help build analytical products people trust. You’re the analytical partner our product teams count on, from helping craft the analytics behind a solution’s value (strengthening internal product analytics and ROI storytelling) to refining the product vision and the details of a new analytical product for execution. Product brings the user, the problem, and the direction; you own what it takes to answer it well: defining the right metrics, shaping a coherent story and visualization design, and bringing the rigor that makes people trust the result.

From there, you translate that into the technical substance that gets built: context-rich metric definitions, dashboard requirements, and the validation that makes it hold up, so product leadership can stand behind the results rather than just present them. You’ll report into the Analytics Program Lead and assist in setting the analytics standards for the organization. If you like telling stories with data, leading small teams, and are passionate about rigorous, usable analytics, this is that role.

Key Responsibilities:

At Qventus, Analytics is treated as a first-class product, rather than a secondary output. As an Senior Analytics Specialist, you will:

  • Partner with PMs to turn a product idea and initial story into a technically defensible analytics product, defining metrics precisely, shaping the dashboard narrative, and setting the validation methodology, and surfacing the gaps in the design before anything gets built
  • Lead analytics projects as their technical owner: scoping key initiatives, running sprints, ticketing, leading project management for the pod, and holding the bar for what ships while keeping things unblocked.
  • Build and steward the metric stories, definitions, and semantic context for your pod's scope, grounded in hands-on data exploration and documented so downstream users, future teams, and AI agents can trust them
  • Own analytical quality for your pod, setting the bar for rigor and correctness, catching flawed definitions and misleading framings before they reach a customer, and holding ultimate technical responsibility for what the pod ships
  • Bring analytical rigor into early product discovery, supporting the exploratory analysis and POCs that pressure-test ROI stories and surface what is really provable before the team commits to building

What We're Looking For:

  • Sharp, experienced analytical thinking, with a track record of building out high-quality, narratively complete analytical components, not just running ad hoc analyses
  • Versatile critical thinking, with demonstrated ability to ramp up quickly and translate general skills into tactical enablement, even without deep domain expertise
  • Hands-on expertise with SQL and modern data warehouses (DBX preferred): deep enough to run analysis, support and debug metric definitions, and set the technical standard for your pod.
  • Strong data visualization design & BI development skills (Sigma or similar)
  • Demonstrated ability to partner with PMs as a trusted peer, turning rough ideas into defensible products and pushing on the thinking without friction
  • Experience leading delivery for a small team: comfortable owning sprints, sequencing, and coordination, and getting good work out of a pod without becoming the bottleneck

It's a Plus if You Have…

  • Experience leading dashboard development end to end, from design through validation and including hands-on build
  • Expertise in the healthcare domain and familiarity with healthcare operational data, clinical workflows, hospital operations, or common healthcare measurement challenges
  • Familiarity with data governance, metric governance, or semantic layer concepts, especially where consistency across teams, solutions, or customer implementations is critical
  • Deeper technical expertise with hands-on data modeling and transformation experience and standards setting (dbt preferred)
  • Experience contributing to analytics QA processes, validation workflows, peer review practices, or release readiness checks for customer-facing analytics

We welcome all qualified applicants and ensure fair consideration for employment without discrimination based on any legally protected characteristics, including, but not limited to: veteran status, uniformed service member status, race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, pregnancy (including childbirth, lactation and related medical conditions), national origin or ancestry, citizenship or immigration status, physical or mental disability, genetic information (including testing and characteristics) or any other category protected by federal, state or local law (collectively, "protected characteristics"). Syneos Health® is a leading fully-integrated life sciences services organization built to accelerate customer success. We partner with innovators at every point across the drug development and commercialization continuum, helping them navigate complexity, anticipate change and accelerate progress.

Our Clinical Solutions team members act with a drug development mindset, applying their years of experience and deep expertise to truly understand customer needs and represent those in the solutions we shape.

Whether you join us in a Functional Service Provider partnership or a Full-Service environment, you’ll collaborate with passionate problem solvers, innovating as a team to help our customers achieve their goals. We are agile and driven to deliver – for one another, our customers, and, most importantly, for those in need.

Discover what your 25,000 future colleagues already know:

Why Syneos Health

• We are passionate about developing our people, through career development and progression; supportive and engaged line management; technical and therapeutic area training; peer recognition and total rewards program.
• We are committed to building an inclusive culture – where you can authentically be yourself. Central to this is our purpose – Driven to Deliver – which captures the passion of our colleagues to show up each day and shape solutions that have the ability to dramatically impact someone’s life.
• We are continuously building the company we all want to work for and our customers want to work with. Why? Because we know that when we bring together smart colleagues from across the world, we can shape the future of healthcare, driving impact for customers and defining the pace of patient progress.

Job Responsibilities

  • Responsible for site management oversight, clinical monitoring and central monitoring deliverables with a focus on patient safety, protocol/GCP/regulatory compliance and data integrity.
  • Oversees site interactions post activation through site closeout. This may include patient recruitment, investigator payments or other related activities.
  • May be responsible for identification of critical data and process, protocol execution risks and risk mitigations related to completion of the Risk Assessment and Categorization Tool (RACT).
  • Reviews the study scope of work, budget and protocol content and ensures the clinical project team (CRAs/Central Monitors) is aware of the contractual obligations and parameters.
  • Uses prior clinical experience, operational data, metrics and reports to identify risks to clinical trial management deliverables.
  • Escalates to the project manager any risks to clinical trial management deliverables (timeline, quality and budget) and any activities and requests which are out of contracted scope.
  • Employs strategic thinking and problem-solving skills to propose and implement risk mitigations.
  • Participates and presents in key meetings such as Kick Off Meeting.
  • Serves as an escalation point for communications with investigator site staff and may be required to interact on the phone or in person with principal investigators or other site staff members. This may include accompanying CRA team members to sites for observation or conflict resolution.
  • Collaborates with other functional leaders such as Study Start Up, Patient Recruitment and Data Management to coordinate delivery handoffs and meet expected study milestones such as site activation targets, enrollment targets and database lock timelines. Reviews and provides feedback on other functional plans (e.g. Data Management Plan, Communication Plan) as they relate to the clinical trial management activities.
  • Responsible for development and ongoing maintenance of clinical study tools and templates, including the Clinical Monitoring Plan. Ensures CTMS, dashboards and other systems are set up and available for use by the clinical team, including overseeing user acceptance testing (UAT) as needed. Ensures access and audit trail reviews are conducted as required.
  • Coordinates initial and ongoing training to the study team regarding protocol specificities, Case Report Form (CRF) completion, dashboards, Sponsor Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), clinical plans and guidelines, data plans and timelines for the study.
  • Oversees resourcing allocations for CRAs and Central Monitors, site assignments and study team members' conduct, and identifies risks to delivery or quality.
  • Ensures quality of the clinical monitoring, central monitoring and site management deliverables within a project and maintain proper visibility of its progress by the use of approved systems and / or tracking tools.
  • Reviews the project oversight dashboards and other clinical trial systems (e.g. Clinical Trial Management System (CTMS), Electronic Data Capture (EDC), eDiary, Electronic Patient Reported Outcomes (ePROs),Trial Master File (TMF), IVRS/IWRS, Central Monitoring dashboards), to oversee site and patient activities, study team conduct and to ensure the data has been updated to reflect timely execution of all operational aspects (required visits/calls, duration, and frequency) according to plan.
  • Understands the monitoring strategy required for the study and, where required, participates in the development of the study risk assessment plan. Is accountable for their assigned clinical team members' understanding, ongoing compliance and delivery according to the stated monitoring strategy, CMP/SMP, and risk plans.
  • Reviews the content and quality of site and central monitoring documentation (site monitoring calls, site visit reports, site letters, central monitoring reports and pertinent correspondence), to ensure they represent site management activities and conduct and that they appropriately convey any risks to protocol/GCP compliance, trial conduct, patient safety or data integrity. Document requested revisions and approvals in CTMS. Ensures these deliverables are provided according to company and/or sponsor specifications, including delivery deadlines.
  • Interacts with the client and other functional departments related to clinical monitoring, central monitoring and site management activities and deliverables. Provides status updates on the clinical deliverables and risks to clients, project management and leadership as per departmental or study agreements. Provides solutions for obstacles in protocol execution and site management.
  • Demonstrates understanding of other functions' roles in achieving compliance and delivery according to protocol, SOPs, ICH GCP and country regulations. This may include data management, study start up, patient recruitment, medical monitoring, pharmacovigilance and Quality Assurance (QA). Supports Inspection Readiness for clinical trial management scope.
  • Oversees CRAs and Central Monitors assigned to the study and routinely assesses study-specific process and training compliance, CMP compliance, and identifies emerging risks. May develop and support execution of corrective action plans at site and study level. Supports and completes activities to achieve data cut and lock deadlines.
  • Provides feedback to line managers on staff performance including strengths as well as areas for development. May be assigned to larger,more complex trials.

Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s degree or RN in a related field or equivalent combination of education, training and experience
  • Demonstrated ability to lead and align teams in the achievement of project milestones
  • Demonstrated capability of working in an international environment.
  • Demonstrated expertise in site management and monitoring (clinical or central)
  • Preferred experience with risk-based monitoring
  • Demonstrates understanding of clinical trial management financial principles and budget management
  • Knowledge of Good Clinical Practice/ICH Guidelines and other applicable regulatory requirements
  • Must demonstrate good computer skills
  • Good communication, presentation and interpersonal skills among project team and with sites
  • Strong conflict resolution skills
  • Demonstrated ability to apply problem solving techniques to resolve complex issues, and apply a risk management approach to identifying and mitigating potential threats to the successful conduct of a clinical research project.
  • Demonstrates critical thinking to determine the cause and appropriate solution in the identification of issues
  • Moderate travel may be required, approximately 20%

Get to know Syneos Health

Over the past 5 years, we have worked with 94% of all Novel FDA Approved Drugs, 95% of EMA Authorized Products and over 200 Studies across 73,000 Sites and 675,000+ Trial patients.

No matter what your role is, you’ll take the initiative and challenge the status quo with us in a highly competitive and ever-changing environment. Learn more about Syneos Health.

Position Overview

APEX TK is searching for a Programmatic Subject Matter Expert (SME) to support The Marshall Space Flight Center (MSFC) Environmental Control and Life Support Systems (ECLSS).

The desired candidate shall interact with senior project personnel at MSFC, prime contractors, other NASA centers, DoD, industry, and academia as specified. This can be a remote position. The contractor shall serve as a subject matter expert for ECLSS and will provide evaluations and recommendations on proposed ECLSS systems and development activities. The contractor will be expected to lead major ECLSS assignments, including conducting comprehensive technical assessments of the Blue Origin and SpaceX Environmental Control and Life Support System (ECLSS) designs to evaluate system maturity, identify critical technical and programmatic risks, and assess realistic development, integration, testing, and certification schedules. Develop evidence-based risk assessments that clearly articulate key challenges, potential impacts, mitigation strategies, and the activities required to achieve system certification. Identify opportunities for technical collaboration, shared risk-reduction activities, and coordinated testing and certification efforts to improve confidence in system readiness and support informed programmatic decision-making.

Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Aerospace Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Chemical Engineering, Systems Engineering, or related technical field
  • 10+ years of direct experience with Environmental Control and Life Support Systems (ECLSS), specifically on both air revitalization and water recovery/management systems
  • Demonstrated experience supporting or leading technical assessments of ECLSS designs across multiple development phases (design, integration, test, certification)
  • Experience interfacing with NASA programs, prime contractors, or DoD customers at a senior/project-lead level
  • Experience conducting risk assessments and developing risk mitigation strategies for complex space systems
  • Experience developing and evaluating technical and programmatic schedules for life-critical systems
  • Experience with ECLSS certification requirements and verification planning
  • Thorough understanding of ECLSS subsystem architecture including: atmosphere revitalization, CO₂ removal/reduction, oxygen generation, water recovery, thermal control interfaces, and trace contaminant control
  • Familiarity with crew health and safety requirements and life support margins for crewed spaceflight
  • Working knowledge of NASA technical standards and human spaceflight requirements (NASA-STD-3001, NPR 7120.5, etc.)
  • Demonstrated ability to lead major technical assignments independently with minimal direction
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills; ability to brief senior leadership and produce monthly summary reports on schedule
  • Ability to obtain and maintain a government security clearance (or currently holds one)
  • Willingness and ability to travel with government approval

Desired Qualifications

  • Master's degree or PhD in a relevant engineering discipline
  • PMP certification or equivalent program management credential
  • Prior NASA civil servant, contractor, or FFRDC experience supporting MSFC, JSC, or a crewed spacecraft program (ISS, Orion, Gateway, Artemis)
  • Direct experience with Blue Origin or SpaceX ECLSS development programs or technical evaluation thereof
  • Experience supporting Gateway, Lunar Surface Systems, or Commercial LEO Destinations (CLD) programs
  • Experience conducting Independent Technical Assessments (ITAs), Independent Review Team (IRT) activities, or Technical Review Board (TRB) support
  • Prior experience coordinating cross-agency ECLSS testing or shared risk-reduction activities between NASA centers or with commercial partners
  • Experience with ECLSS analog environments (EVA suits, hyperbaric systems, closed-loop habitats)
  • Familiarity with DoD life support or CBRNE/environmental control system standards and crosswalk to NASA requirements
  • Understanding of ECLSS-adjacent systems integration: thermal control, power, structures/mechanisms, GN&C interfaces
  • Familiarity with model-based systems engineering (MBSE) tools applied to ECLSS design and verification
  • Knowledge of ECLSS lessons learned from ISS and Shuttle programs
  • Established professional relationships across the ECLSS community (NASA centers, academia, national labs, commercial providers)
  • Experience contributing to or leading proposal efforts, source selections, or acquisition strategies for ECLSS procurements
  • Familiarity with NASA's Systems Engineering Handbook (SP-2016-6105) and human-rating processes
  • Prior experience as a Contracting Officer's Representative (COR) or technical monitor for ECLSS-related contracts

jobs.description:
Vannevar builds AI systems for the Department of War's most consequential missions. We have 125 deployments across every branch and combatant command spanning our core platform and five distinct products. An an example of how we work, when major combat operations started with Iran, we fielded a new product supporting 24/7 operations and 9,000+ users in three months.

How we build is our advantage: we deploy forward with the people who own the mission. Our engineers, product team, and CTO deploy forward to the point of friction, including visiting units in Ukraine. We focus on embedding directly with operational units supporting great power competition with China, combat operations with Iran, and counter-narcotics missions.

About the role

As an Information Systems Security Officer (ISSO), you will help get our products authorized and keep them authorized. Supporting our ISSM and government ISSMs, you will own day-to-day security and authorization work across multiple systems, spanning cloud (FedRAMP, DoD IL5) and classified (IL6, Secret, TS/SCI) systems. You will partner with engineering, AppSec, and DevOps to keep packages current, keep controls verifiable, and move our systems toward continuous ATO (cATO). This is a hands-on technical role that directly shapes how quickly our software reaches the mission.

What you'll do

  • Build and maintain ATO and IATT packages (SSPs, FIPS 199 / CNSSI 1253 categorization, CRMs, POA&Ms) under NIST SP 800-37, NIST SP 800-53, FedRAMP, the DoD Cloud Computing SRG, and JSIG.
  • Assess security controls across cloud and on-prem classified systems (IAM, logging, encryption, network segmentation) and document inheritance from cloud and hosting providers.
  • Complete DISA STIG checklists and run vulnerability scans, then drive remediation with engineering.
  • Support cATO and continuous monitoring (NIST SP 800-137): automate evidence collection, review changes for security impact, track POA&Ms, and keep eMASS and Xacta current.
  • Respond to customer security questionnaires and coordinate with government customers and third-party assessors.
  • Monitor deployed systems for unauthorized changes and suspicious activity, and support incident response, audits, and media sanitization.
  • Maintain security policies and procedures aligned to customer and authorization requirements.

What you should have

  • Active TS/SCI clearance
  • 4+ years in cybersecurity, including 2+ years as an ISSO, ISSE or in a similar authorization role on DoD, IC, or federal systems
  • Hands-on ATO experience under NIST SP 800-37 and 800-53 in cloud and classified environments
  • Working knowledge of cloud security (AWS, Azure, or GCP) and on-prem classified systems, plus familiarity with containers and microservices (e.g., Kubernetes) and Git-based change management (e.g., GitHub)
  • Experience with eMASS or Xacta, DISA STIGs, and SCAP/SCC or ACAS scans
  • DoD 8140 compliant certification (Security+ CE or higher)
  • Clear, concise writer who can explain controls to engineers and authorizing officials

Nice to have

  • DoD IL5/IL6, FedRAMP High, or cATO experience
  • AWS GovCloud and cloud security tooling such as Wiz, CrowdStrike, or Splunk
  • Scripting in Python, Bash, or PowerShell
  • CISSP, CCSP, or AWS Certified Security Specialty

  • 401k matching

  • Flexible work environment - you manage your workday
  • Pet and child care reimbursement during travel

jobs.description:
The Operations Enablement Lead builds and sustains the capability system that enables Virtuox Operations to deliver consistent, scalable, high-quality service. As a senior individual contributor, the role owns the design, scaling and continuous improvement of operations-wide training and onboarding programs, knowledge management, standard operating procedures, continuous improvement, quality enablement, and adoption of new processes and tools.


The role partners across Practice Support, Clinical Operations, Logistics, Customer Service, Revenue Cycle Management, Quality, Compliance, Product, Technology, and the People Team. Functional leaders remain accountable for service delivery and employee performance; the Operations Enablement Lead provides the standards, methods, content, governance, facilitation, and insights that help teams adopt consistent ways of working.


What You'll Do

Operations training strategy: Define and maintain an integrated training and enablement approach across Virtuox Operations, aligned to business priorities, role requirements, quality expectations, and changing processes.

Onboarding programs: Design, implement, and continuously improve role-based onboarding pathways, facilitator guides, learner materials, checkpoints, and readiness criteria for new and transitioning employees.

Learning needs assessment: Partner with functional leaders and subject-matter experts to assess capability gaps, translate operational needs into learning plans, and prioritize training based on risk and business impact.

Knowledge management: Manage and maintain centralized operations knowledge base solution that makes current procedures, job aids, process maps, FAQs, decision guides, and best practices easy to find and use.

SOP governance: Establish standards, templates, ownership, review cycles, version control, approvals, and retirement practices for operations SOPs and related documentation.

Content development: Develop and maintain training materials, knowledge articles, job aids, playbooks, simulations, and other enablement tools in partnership with subject-matter experts.

Continuous improvement: Facilitate process discovery, root-cause analysis, workflow redesign, and improvement initiatives that reduce waste, rework, variation, manual effort, and avoidable customer friction.

Quality enablement: Translate quality findings, audit themes, recurring errors, and operational risks into targeted learning, process controls, documentation improvements, and corrective-action support.

Change readiness and adoption: Create readiness, communication, training, reinforcement, and adoption plans for new systems, products, processes, services, policies, and organization changes.

Cross-training and resilience: Build cross-training approaches, skill matrices, role-readiness criteria, and reinforcement plans that improve operational flexibility, coverage, and continuity.

Measurement and insights: Define and report metrics for onboarding effectiveness, time to readiness, training completion, knowledge usage, process adoption, quality outcomes, and improvement benefits.

Program governance: Maintain a visible roadmap, priorities, risks, decisions, owners, and status reporting for the operations excellence and enablement portfolio.

Consulting and facilitation: Serve as a trusted advisor and facilitator to operational leaders, using expertise and influence to align stakeholders and move complex, cross-functional work forward without direct authority.

Sustainable handoff: Ensure new processes and tools transition into clear operational ownership, with documented controls, trained users, updated knowledge, and agreed monitoring routines.

What You Bring

  • Bachelor's degree in operations, business, organizational development, learning, quality, industrial engineering, healthcare administration, or a related field preferred, or an equivalent combination of education and relevant experience.
  • Significant experience in operational excellence, training and enablement, knowledge management, quality, continuous improvement, change management, or a related discipline.
  • Demonstrated success leading complex cross-functional programs and delivering results without direct authority.
  • Experience designing onboarding, learning content, SOP governance, process documentation, and adoption strategies.
  • Experience using performance, quality, learning, and process data to identify gaps and measure results.
  • Experience in healthcare, medical device, diagnostic services, DME, or another regulated environment preferred.
  • Continuous improvement, quality, learning, project, or change-management certification preferred.
  • Domestic travel as needed

What Sets You Apart

  • Advanced consulting, facilitation, stakeholder-management, and influencing skills.
  • Strong instructional design, adult-learning, onboarding, and capability-development skills.
  • Strong knowledge-management, technical-writing, information-architecture, and document-governance capability.
  • Practical expertise in process mapping, root-cause analysis, continuous improvement, standard work, and operational measurement.
  • Ability to translate quality, compliance, and operational requirements into clear learning and process controls.
  • Strong change-readiness, communication, reinforcement, and adoption-planning skills.
  • Ability to prioritize a broad portfolio, manage ambiguity, and convert complex work into clear actions and decision-ready recommendations.
  • Proficiency with Microsoft 365 and relevant learning, knowledge, workflow, reporting, or quality systems.

Why Join Resmed

We are shaping the future at ResMed, and we recognize the need to build on and broaden our existing skills and continue to attract and retain the world’s best talent. We work hard to offer holistic benefits packages, provide flexible work arrangements, cultivate a workforce culture that allows employees to grow personally and professionally, and deliver competitive salaries to our team members. Employees scheduled to work 30 or more hours per week are eligible for benefits. This position qualifies for the following benefits package:  comprehensive medical, vision, dental, and life, AD&D, short-term and long-term disability insurance, sleep care management, Health Savings Account (HSA), Flexible Spending Account (FSA), commuter benefits, 401(k), Employee Stock Purchase Plan (ESPP), Employee Assistance Program (EAP), and tuition assistance. Employees accrue three weeks Paid Time Off (PTO) in their first year of employment, receive 11 paid holidays plus 3 floating days and are eligible for 14 weeks of primary caregiver or two weeks of secondary caregiver leave when welcoming new family members.

jobs.description:
About MedeAnalytics

MedeAnalytics is the Enterprise Healthcare Performance company that delivers AI-driven, cloud-native solutions to help payers, risk-bearing providers and other value- and risk-bearing entities measurably improve performance by reducing costs, improving quality and MLR, optimizing utilization, increasing reimbursement, and elevating care quality across all lines of business. Its enterprise health data management platform—built on its proprietary Health Fabric™—unifies clinical, claims, financial, and social data into a single, scalable source of truth that fuels insights, action, and AI.

As the industry’s healthcare intelligence partner of choice for more than 30 years, MedeAnalytics combines its platform, cross-domain enterprise analytics, AI-powered workflows, and Strategic Advisory™ services to transform intelligence into accountable execution—delivering greater ROI across value-based care, risk and quality, cost and utilization management, and network optimization.

MedeAnalytics empowers organizations to move faster from insight to impact with confidence and measurable results. To learn more, visit medeanalytics.com and follow MedeAnalytics on LinkedIn and Facebook.

About Our Opportunity

Core Requirement

This role requires a proven strategic payer sales leader with demonstrated success selling and expanding enterprise solutions with health plans, primary focus in Medicare Advantage and Medicaid, secondarily in Commercial markets. The ideal candidate understands the distinct business, regulatory, operational, and market dynamics of each line of business and can translate payer priorities into credible executive-level strategies that drive measurable growth.

Position Overview

The Vice President, Payer Growth is responsible for generating new business and expanding strategic health plan relationships within an assigned territory and account portfolio. This leader will develop territory and account strategies, build trusted relationships with payer executives, identify and quantify whitespace, and lead complex enterprise sales opportunities from initial engagement through contract execution.

A key focus of the role is creating a comprehensive growth strategy for an existing portfolio of health plan clients, meaning accelerate cross-sell opportunities; and pursuing new logo opportunities with national, regional, State sponsored, and other risk-bearing payers.

The successful candidate will connect payer priorities—including affordability, healthcare economics, risk and quality performance, value-based care, population health, member engagement, customer and group reporting, AI, and enterprise data strategy to the MedeAnalytics Health Performance Platform and broader solution portfolio. This individual must be equally effective as an enterprise seller, strategic account leader, healthcare advisor, and cross-functional team orchestrator.

Key Responsibilities

New Business and Revenue Growth

  • Develop and execute a territory growth strategy across Medicare Advantage and Medicaid.
  • Build and manage a qualified pipeline through executive relationships, market intelligence, targeted prospecting, partnerships, and industry engagement.
  • Create account-specific strategies for priority health plans, including relationship maps, business hypotheses, solution alignment, and pursuit plans.
  • Lead consultative conversations that connect payer business priorities to MedeAnalytics' data, analytics, AI, workflow, and advisory capabilities.
  • Manage complex enterprise sales cycles from discovery and solution development through executive presentations, RFPs, commercial negotiations, and contract execution.
  • Consistently achieve or exceed annual new-logo, expansion, ARR, and revenue targets.

Strategic Account Expansion

  • Serve as the commercial growth leader for an assigned portfolio of existing health plan clients.
  • Partner with Account Management to develop and execute strategic growth and success plans for each priority account.
  • Build a deep understanding of each client's strategy, operating model, technology and analytics environment, financial objectives, transformation initiatives, and competitive landscape.
  • Identify and quantify whitespace across the MedeAnalytics portfolio and convert it into actionable near- and long-term opportunities.
  • Expand relationships beyond current users and buyers by developing executive sponsorship across business, clinical, financial, technology, analytics, and operational functions.
  • Lead the commercial strategy for expansions, cross-sells, and upsells, positioning MedeAnalytics as a long-term enterprise partner.
  • Coordinate executive sponsorship and internal resources around the highest-value growth opportunities.

Territory and Market Leadership

  • Maintain a comprehensive territory plan covering current clients, priority prospects, market dynamics, competitive positioning, and revenue potential.
  • Apply a strong understanding of the distinct priorities of Medicare Advantage, Medicaid, dual-eligible, and commercial health plans to shape relevant executive conversations and growth strategies.
  • Monitor payer trends, policy changes, competitive activity, and emerging client needs, translating market intelligence into commercial opportunities.
  • Represent MedeAnalytics at industry conferences, client events, executive meetings, and other payer forums.
  • Establish MedeAnalytics as a strategic thought partner—not solely a technology or analytics vendor—with health plan leadership.

Cross-Functional Leadership and Operating Discipline

  • Serve as the commercial lead for assigned strategic accounts, coordinating Account Management, Product, Marketing, Solution Consulting, Services, Partnerships, and executive leadership.
  • Translate client needs and market intelligence into actionable input for product strategy, partnerships, messaging, and go-to-market priorities.
  • Collaborate with solution and product leaders to develop compelling business cases tied to measurable clinical, financial, operational, and member outcomes.
  • Lead regular account and territory reviews focused on pipeline, client health, revenue risk, whitespace, relationship coverage, and next actions.
  • Maintain disciplined opportunity management, forecasting, account planning, and CRM hygiene.

Measures of Success

  • New-logo ARR and revenue
  • Expansion ARR and revenue from existing clients
  • Qualified pipeline creation, progression, and conversion
  • Growth of MedeAnalytics' footprint within strategic accounts
  • Executive relationship depth and breadth
  • Strategic account and territory plan execution
  • Forecast accuracy
  • Client advocacy and referenceability
  • Achievement of annual territory revenue objectives

Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree or equivalent professional experience.
  • 10+ years of successful enterprise sales, strategic account growth, or business development experience in healthcare technology, analytics, SaaS, consulting, or related solutions serving health plans.
  • Demonstrated sales and account-expansion success across Medicare Advantage, Medicaid, and commercial health plan markets.
  • Strong understanding of the distinct economics, regulatory requirements, operating models, purchasing dynamics, and strategic priorities of government-sponsored and commercial health plans.
  • Proven ability to originate, develop, and close complex, multi-million-dollar enterprise opportunities.
  • Experience developing and expanding relationships with large national, regional, Blue Cross Blue Shield, and/or provider-sponsored health plans.
  • Strong understanding of payer priorities, including affordability, medical cost management, value-based care, risk adjustment, quality, population health, network performance, member engagement, and enterprise analytics.
  • Working knowledge of healthcare data, including medical and pharmacy claims, clinical, financial, eligibility, provider, and social risk data.
  • Ability to engage credibly with C-suite and senior executives across business, clinical, financial, operational, technology, and analytics functions.
  • Experience navigating complex RFPs, procurement processes, contracting, and enterprise decision-making environments.
  • Strong executive communication, presentation, negotiation, and relationship-management skills.
  • Demonstrated ability to lead cross-functional teams and influence without direct authority.
  • Highly self-directed, with the discipline to manage a large territory and portfolio of complex strategic accounts.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Established executive relationships within the U.S. payer market.
  • Experience selling enterprise healthcare data platforms, analytics, AI, population health, value-based care, quality, risk, or financial performance solutions.
  • Understanding of modern healthcare data architecture, cloud platforms, interoperability, AI/ML, and enterprise analytics environments.
  • Experience helping health plans unify fragmented data and analytics environments or expand enterprise adoption of a strategic platform.
  • Demonstrated payer-market thought leadership and the ability to represent MedeAnalytics credibly with senior industry executives.

Leadership Profile

This is a senior individual contributor role with no direct reports. The ideal candidate will bring strong commercial ownership, strategic thinking, and executive relationship-building skills to manage their territory and account portfolio as a trusted partner to health plan leaders.

Additional Information:

MedeAnalytics believes in fair and equitable pay. A reasonable estimate of the base salary range for this role is $165,000 - $195,000 USD + commission opportunities. Please note that actual compensation for all roles may vary within the range, or be above or below the range, based on factors including, but not limited to, education, training, relevant work experience, professional achievements/qualifications, skill level, business need, location and will be finalized at the time of offer.

jobs.description:
📍 Remote (U.S.-Based) | Optional hybrid in the Bay Area
Reports to: Senior Director, Asynchronous Care
Job Type: Full-time W2

Overview

Midi Health is on a mission to redesign care for women in midlife - and we're growing fast. As our asynchronous operations scale, we need to ensure our Medical and Practice Assistants have the training, tools, and feedback they need to consistently deliver high-quality work.

We're looking for a Senior Operations Manager, Performance & Enablement to build and own the programs that help our frontline teams perform at their best.

This person will design, establish, and own the performance measurement, operational QA, and training programs that support Medical and Practice Assistants across Async Operations. You'll set consistent standards across teams, build scalable systems for evaluating frontline execution, and give Managers the tools and insights they need to identify gaps, coach effectively, and drive measurable performance improvements.

This role goes beyond traditional quality assurance or training. You'll connect performance data, quality findings, and frontline observations to diagnose complex performance challenges, distinguish between individual execution and broader operational issues, and develop targeted interventions that lead to sustained improvement.

The ideal candidate brings deep experience in frontline quality, performance management, and training, with strong analytical judgment and a track record of building scalable programs. They're comfortable operating independently, influencing leaders across teams, and using modern AI tools to accelerate analysis, develop resources, and improve how frontline teams work.

This is a senior, hands-on role for someone who enjoys building programs from the ground up and turning performance insights into meaningful operational improvements.

The goal: Build a consistently high-performing MA workforce that delivers accurate, timely, and high-quality patient support at scale.

You won't just measure frontline performance — you'll build the systems that help our teams continuously improve.

What you'll do

MA Quality & Performance

  • Design and own a scalable framework for evaluating MA performance consistently across Async Operations.
  • Establish performance measurement standards and reporting that give Managers actionable visibility into individual and team performance.
  • Bring together quality, productivity, and adherence metrics to create a comprehensive view of frontline performance.
  • Design and maintain operational QA scorecards, evaluation rubrics, sampling methodologies, and reporting frameworks.
  • Establish consistent approaches for evaluating whether MAs follow established workflows, SOPs, and service standards accurately and effectively.
  • Define and measure performance across accuracy, completeness, responsiveness, communication, resolution, and process adherence.
  • Lead calibration processes across teams to ensure quality standards are interpreted and applied consistently.
  • Identify high performers, recurring performance gaps, and opportunities for targeted coaching and development.
  • Equip Managers with actionable performance insights, coaching frameworks, and resources to drive accountability and improvement.
  • Own the effectiveness of performance measurement and QA programs, continuously refining them based on operational results and frontline feedback.

Training & Frontline Enablement

  • Design, establish, and own scalable onboarding and continuous-learning programs for Medical and Practice Assistants across Async Operations.
  • Develop training strategies, curricula, onboarding materials, job aids, and ongoing learning resources that support consistent frontline execution.
  • Identify recurring knowledge and skill gaps through quality reviews, performance data, and frontline observations.
  • Translate performance gaps into targeted training, retraining, and reinforcement programs.
  • Establish processes to keep training materials current as workflows, SOPs, tools, and expectations evolve.
  • Partner with subject-matter experts to ensure training reflects established operational and clinical standards.
  • Develop tools and resources that enable Managers to reinforce expectations and coach their teams effectively.
  • Build mechanisms for ongoing learning, knowledge retention, and skill development beyond initial onboarding.
  • Define measures of training effectiveness and continuously improve programs based on their impact on frontline quality, consistency, and performance.

Performance Insights & Continuous Improvement

  • Independently analyze complex quality and performance trends to identify recurring execution gaps, root causes, and improvement opportunities.
  • Identify patterns across quality reviews, patient feedback, repeat contacts, escalations, and operational performance.
  • Distinguish between problems caused by knowledge gaps, individual execution, unclear processes, or system limitations, and recommend appropriate interventions. ● Partner with Operations Managers to establish coaching, training, and performance improvement priorities based on data and frontline observations.
  • Identify systemic workflow and technology issues affecting frontline execution and translate findings into actionable recommendations for the appropriate owners. ● Ensure operational changes are reflected in training, quality measurement, and performance expectations.
  • Establish feedback loops between frontline teams, Managers, and operational leaders to drive continuous improvement.
  • Measure the effectiveness of coaching, training, and performance interventions, refining approaches to achieve sustained improvements.
  • Advise Async Operations leadership on frontline performance trends, emerging risks, and opportunities to improve consistency, efficiency, and patient experience.

Cross-Functional Partnership

  • Serve as a strategic partner to Async Operations Managers, providing the performance frameworks, insights, and enablement resources needed to lead high-performing teams. ● Collaborate with Analytics & Workforce Planning to align performance reporting, productivity measurement, and operational insights.
  • Partner with Operations, Systems Operations, and Product to ensure workflow and technology changes are incorporated into frontline training and performance expectations.
  • Work with Clinical leadership and Clinical Quality to ensure training and evaluation reflect approved clinical protocols and escalation standards.
  • Influence performance and enablement priorities across teams, establishing consistent standards while adapting programs to the needs of different workflows.
  • Communicate complex performance findings and recommendations clearly to operational leaders, helping translate insights into measurable improvements.

What you will need to succeed

  • 7+ years of experience in Operations, Quality Assurance, Training & Enablement, Performance Management, or a related field, including demonstrated experience designing and scaling frontline performance or training programs.
  • Deep expertise in frontline quality assurance, performance measurement, coaching frameworks, and operational accountability.
  • Experience designing and implementing QA scorecards, evaluation rubrics, sampling methodologies, calibration processes, and performance reporting.
  • Demonstrated success building scalable onboarding, training, and continuous-learning programs for operational teams.
  • Strong analytical judgment and data fluency, with the ability to independently evaluate complex performance trends, identify root causes, and develop actionable recommendations.
  • Comfort leveraging modern AI tools to accelerate analysis, develop training resources, evaluate performance trends, and improve operational processes.
  • Experience establishing performance standards and measurement frameworks across multiple teams or workflows.
  • Ability to distinguish between individual performance gaps, training needs, process problems, and system limitations.
  • Strong business judgment and ability to connect frontline performance to operational efficiency, service levels, and patient experience.
  • Experience influencing frontline Managers and operational leaders to drive improvements without directly managing their employees.

Join a global Contract Resource Organization (CRO) where innovation meets purpose. At Worldwide Clinical Trials, we're driven by a shared commitment to improving lives through high-quality clinical research. Our teams are empowered to think creatively, take ownership, and deliver meaningful work that helps bring life-changing therapies to patients around the world.


With more than 4,000 professionals across the globe, we foster a collaborative and inclusive environment where diverse perspectives are valued, growth is encouraged, and every contribution makes an impact. Whether you're building your career or bringing years of experience, you'll have the opportunity to learn, grow, and help shape the future of clinical research.


Make an Impact as a Associate eCOA Manager at Worldwide


Bring your eCOA and clinical trials experience to a role where you can take meaningful ownership of study delivery. As an Associate eCOA Manager, you’ll oversee key eCOA vendor deliverables, timelines, risks, budgets, and communications across assigned studies.


You’ll be a central link between eCOA vendors, sponsors, and Worldwide study teams, helping ensure systems and associated activities meet study requirements throughout the clinical trial lifecycle. Your work will span project oversight, study design review, user acceptance testing, change management, data transfer requirements, and issue resolution.

You’ll join a Clinical Systems Department that works across a broad range of clinical technologies and provides opportunities for mentorship, training, and internal growth.


Where You'll Work


This is a remote role open to candidates based in US. You will collaborate with global teams across multiple time zones.


What You'll Do


  • Manage eCOA project activities from system maintenance through decommissioning, keeping deliverables and timelines on track and aligned with Worldwide SOPs.
  • Partner with eCOA vendors, sponsors, and internal study teams to identify study trends, address requirements, manage risks, and resolve project issues.
  • Coordinate clear and timely project communications, including study status reports, meeting agendas, minutes, project calls, and stakeholder updates.
  • Oversee eCOA study design activities, review post-go-live changes in scope, and approve User Requirements Specifications (URS) as required.
  • Review User Acceptance Test plans, oversee testing activities, and facilitate sponsor completion of system user acceptance testing.
  • Manage the financial aspects of assigned eCOA studies, including vendor work orders, budgets, financial reviews, and Change Orders.
  • Prepare and review site, support, and helpdesk materials, while performing quality-control checks on manual database edits and other activities as required.
  • Facilitate collaboration between eCOA processes and Data Management data-transfer requirements, and provide eCOA input for protocol amendments.


What You'll Bring


  • A degree in a relevant discipline or equivalent experience, combined with a minimum of 1 year of experience working with eCOA and clinical trials and a minimum of 1 year of project management experience.
  • Knowledge of Phase I–IV clinical research operations, gained within a Contract Research Organization (CRO) or pharmaceutical environment.
  • Knowledge of the Software Development Life Cycle (SDLC) and familiarity with eCOA topics, including eCOA designs and scales.
  • Strong project and time-management skills, with the ability to prioritize multiple projects and make effective decisions in a fast-paced, dynamic environment.
  • Effective client-facing and stakeholder communication skills, with the ability to escalate risks and project issues clearly and promptly.
  • Strong attention to detail and sound independent judgment, together with a proactive, organized, and collaborative approach.
  • Adaptability and problem-solving skills, including the ability to work with new technologies, concepts, and processes and identify opportunities for improvement.
  • Proficiency in written and spoken English to conduct day-to-day business and collaborate effectively with stakeholders.

Discover the Difference


We love knowing that someone is going to have a better life because of the work we do.  Discover the Difference at Worldwide Clinical Trials. Explore additional opportunities on our careers page, visit , or connect with us onLinkedIn.

Under the general supervision of the Scoping & Licensing Manager, the Senior Scoping & Licensing Consultant serves as a subject matter expert responsible for end-to-end scoping, quoting, licensing, and feasibility assessment of Clinical Outcomes Assessment (COA) projects.

The LV Team is over 20 years of experience in the COA field, positioning us as the industry leader. Our team performs a wide variety of functions in addition to translation, including recruitment and interviewing of patients around the world, development of novel research for presentation and publication, expertise in licensing and copyrights, and management of electronic implementation of COAs (eCOA) in over 80 languages.

Work at Home Bilingual Slovene/Slovenian-English Phone Interpreter

Position Overview:


The Slovene/Slovenian Telephone Interpreter is responsible for handling calls on demand, and renders the meaning of conversations between Slovene/Slovenianand English speakers. The interpreter breaks the communication barrier in a wide range of industries that LanguageLine Solutions serves: Healthcare, Government, Insurance, Financial, Utilities, Travel & Hospitality, General Business, Law Enforcement, Court, and 911.


The interpreter processes information quickly, concisely and recognizes sensitive cultural differences. The interpreter is professional and courteous at all times and uses appropriate terminology and understands common industry procedures and practices. The interpreting sessions may involve simple or complex, technical or non-technical subjects.


This position does not involve written translation however translators and other skilled linguists are encouraged to apply. The Interpreters translate verbally.


**This is a remote position. The Interpreter works from his/her home-office. It is essential to ensure a quiet & secure environment.**


Essential Job Functions

  • Respond to the interpreting sessions promptly and conduct interpretation in a friendly and professional manner.
  • Render correct concepts and meanings according to the conventions of established interpretation protocol, avoiding omissions or additions.
  • Speak clearly in both languages using proper pronunciation, enunciation and polite expressions.
  • Maintain a professional demeanor throughout the interpreting sessions at all times.
  • Remain calm during interpreting sessions in the event that one of the primary speakers is incoherent or upset, especially in emergency situations such as 911 calls.
  • Maintain punctuality and availability during work hours.
  • Follow client instructions, in compliance with protocol to ensure client expectations are met with the Limited English-speaking Person (LEP), avoiding interaction with the LEP without client’s permission.

The interpreter may need to remain on a call for extended periods without breaks due to the nature of the call or may, at times experience high call volumes.   • Excellent listening, retention and note-taking skills to maintain a high level of accuracy during interpretation.

Riva is looking for a Motion and Visual Designer who loves turning ideas into videos people want to watch and is excited about what AI tools make possible. You’ll create everything from campaign and social videos to explainers and product demos, using AI to work faster and try more ideas.

WHAT YOU WILL BE DOING

You’ll turn ideas and briefs into compelling videos, from writing scripts and developing storyboards to editing footage and adding the motion graphics that bring ideas to life. You’ll also contribute to broader creative projects and help shape how the Content and Creative team uses AI in video production.

This role suits someone who combines creative judgment with strong execution, takes ownership of their work, and is always experimenting with better ways to get things done.

More specifically, your responsibilities will include:

Write and Develop Video Content

  • Develop concepts, write original scripts, and create storyboards that connect the message, visuals, and intended audience.
  • Write strong hooks, clear narratives, natural dialogue or voiceover, and effective calls to action.
  • Translate complex topics into engaging content suited to the channel and intended runtime.
  • Plan videos such as product explainers and demos, day-in-the-life stories, interviews, campaign content, event highlights, and social videos.

Edit Video and Create Motion Graphics

  • Edit footage, audio, graphics, music, and captions into polished final videos.
  • Create 2D animation and motion graphics, including animated explainers, workflow and process flows, typography, diagrams, transitions, and branded graphics.
  • Bring scripts and storyboards to life through clear visual storytelling, timing, pacing, and movement.
  • Combine animation with recorded footage and screen recordings to explain products and ideas, including release demos recorded with the product team.
  • Prepare assets for animation and build reusable motion templates.
  • Adapt finished videos and animations for different channels, formats, and audiences.

Shape How We Use AI in Video

  • Use AI tools across the whole workflow, from concepts, scripts, and storyboards to animation, transcription, editing, and adapting content for new channels.
  • Evaluate and refine AI outputs for accuracy, originality, visual consistency, and brand alignment.
  • Test new AI tools as they emerge, share what works, and turn the best ideas into reusable templates and workflows for the team.
  • Follow company requirements for confidentiality, permissions, and responsible AI use.

Support the Creative Team

  • Help deliver campaign assets, presentation materials, social content, and other creative projects.
  • Adapt existing assets, complete revisions, and prepare files for different formats and channels.
  • Learn shared tools and processes so you can jump in on other creative projects when the team needs it.
  • Maintain organized source files, templates, and clear handoffs.

Own Your Delivery

  • Clarify briefs, identify missing information, and confirm expectations before production.
  • Manage multiple assignments and meet agreed deadlines.
  • Communicate progress and flag delivery risks early.
  • Apply feedback accurately and check your work before submitting it for review.

WHAT YOU BRING TO THE TABLE

  • A portfolio demonstrating video editing, motion graphics or animation, and scriptwriting.
  • The ability to take a video from brief through script, storyboard, production, and final delivery.
  • Proficiency in professional video editing and animation software, such as Adobe Premiere Pro and After Effects, or equivalent tools.
  • A good eye for motion, typography, composition, audio, pacing, and visual storytelling.
  • The ability to animate UI elements, workflows, and diagrams from a storyboard (3D experience is not required).
  • Hands-on experience using AI tools in your video workflow, curiosity about what comes next, and sound judgment about when and how to use them.
  • A record of delivering quality work efficiently and managing revisions within agreed timelines.
  • Strong writing skills and the ability to make complex subjects clear and engaging.
  • Attention to detail, organized working habits, and clear communication.
  • A collaborative approach and the flexibility to contribute beyond video and animation.
  • Deep understanding of standard design software, including Figma.

Bonus Points For

  • Experience producing video at a B2B SaaS or technology company.

WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE

  • Strong creative work: Your videos and animations tell a clear story, engage the intended audience, and meet Riva’s brand and technical standards.
  • Effective scriptwriting: Your scripts are accurate, engaging, suited to the intended runtime, and ready for production with limited substantive rewriting.
  • Reliable delivery: You manage projects from brief through final review, meet agreed deadlines, provide realistic estimates, and flag risks early.
  • Accuracy and attention to detail: Your work meets the brief, incorporates feedback correctly, and requires few avoidable corrections.
  • AI in practice: You bring new AI tools and techniques to the team and use them, along with templates and reusable assets, to ship faster without losing quality.
  • Dependable team support: You provide reliable support on agreed creative tasks, communicate clearly, and maintain organized files and handoffs.

CORE COMPETENCIES FOR SUCCESS

  • Communication: Ability to effectively convey information across all levels using verbal, non-verbal, written, and visual mediums while actively listening to ensure understanding.
  • Collaboration: Inspires and motivates others, embraces diverse perspectives, and works effectively in teams to achieve shared goals.
  • Business Acumen: Ability to make effective decisions by understanding key drivers of company success and applying knowledge to achieve business goals and positive outcomes.
  • Design Thinking: Ability to take a systemic, customer-focused problem-solving approach to effectively respond to a rapidly changing environment for the best results possible.
  • Analytical Thinking & Decision Making: Ability to approach problems by relying on logic, data and facts. Uses the information available to effectively decide on an optimal path forward.
  • Managing Resources & Digital Dexterity: Combines adaptability to new technologies with effective utilization of time, budget, and talent to optimize outcomes and drive continuous improvement.
  • Organizational Alignment: Ability to direct focus and effort towards a goal set by the organization.

MORE ABOUT RIVA

We are an Edmonton-based software development company with a global footprint. Our Relationship Engine creates seamless data flow between applications like email, calendar, contacts, and tasks and CRM - synchronizing data and eliminating the need for task switching, application toggling, and data entry duplication across platforms.

We offer a work culture that fosters diversity, equity, inclusion, and fun. Where curiosity is rewarded, and each day offers the chance to learn, grow, and contribute to the efforts of people you like, respect, and value.

Total compensation package including;

This role needs to work alongside our sales and marketing teams based in MT, ET, and AT time zones where we will have periodic or recurring meetings and where flexibility will be required.
